## Critical (12)

### AR-01 — SIGTERM hangs forever when ASH is enabled (default) (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:334`

**Category:** deadlock · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Shutdown calls mgr.Close() (run.go:333-335) while the ASH sampler still holds a DedicatedConn from Manager. Manager.Close holds m.mu and calls pgxpool Close on the target and per-DB pools (conn.go:373-381). pgxpool Close blocks until every acquired connection is released. The ASH stop funcs run only in the deferred block at run.go:184-188, which executes after mgr.Close returns. The sampler's run loop (internal/ash/sampler.go:165-190) also does not release its conn on ctx.Done. Result is a deadlock on the main goroutine.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** Operator runs docker stop or systemctl stop on an agent with default config. The agent never exits after SIGTERM, the orchestrator waits for its grace period and sends SIGKILL, and the DedicatedConn stays open on the monitored server until the TCP session dies. Every shutdown is a hard kill, and the healthz server is never cleanly stopped.

**Correction (from verification):** Correction to the finding: the healthz server is shut down at run.go:332, before the hang, so only the shutdown-complete part of the failure scenario is wrong.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reproduced on a local throwaway PG container: with default config (ash enabled) SIGTERM never exits. Goroutine dump shows main in agent.(*Manager).Close conn.go:377 called from run.go:334. With checks ash enabled false the process exits in about 2s. Code: run.go:184-188 (deferred ash stops), run.go:330-335 (flush, healthSrv.Shutdown, mgr.Close loop), conn.go:373-381, internal/ash/sampler.go:165-190, cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:122-174.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code path verified: run.go:314-335 does cancel(), scheduler.Stop(), flushEnvelope, healthSrv.Shutdown, then mgr.Close() in a loop. The ASH stop funcs are in a defer (run.go:184-188) that runs only after main returns, so they cannot run before mgr.Close. Manager.Close (conn.go:373-381) holds m.mu and calls pgxpool Close, which blocks until every acquired connection is released (pgx v5.10.0 pool.go:456-461 -> puddle v2.2.2 pool.go:179-180 'defer p.destructWG.Wait()'). The ASH DedicatedConn is an acquired pool connection (conn.go:141-151, ash.go connectLocked). ashConn releases only in Close(), which runs from stop() (ash.go:95-101), and the sampler run loop (sampler.go:172-174) does not release on ctx.Done. No guard elsewhere. Correction to the finding: the healthz server is shut down at run.go:332, before the hang, so only the shutdown-complete part of the failure scenario is wrong. The flush also completes before the hang. Impact is a non-exiting agent on every SIGTERM with default config, ending in SIGKILL.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run -d --name pglens-review-ar01-7q3 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 127.0.0.1::5432 postgres:19rc1-alpine (resolved to 127.0.0.1:32787). Temp test cmd/pglens-agent/zz_review_test.go (TestZZReviewAR01ShutdownHang): NewManager + startASH(default config), sleep 3s, cancel(), mgr.Close() in a goroutine. Command: AR01_DSN='postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:32787/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test ./cmd/pglens-agent -run TestZZReviewAR01ShutdownHang -v. Output: 'AR-01 step1: mgr.Close still blocked after 5s while ASH holds its DedicatedConn (HANG)' then 'AR-01 step2: mgr.Close returned only after ash stop() released the conn'. Test file deleted afterwards. Cleanup: pglens-review-ar01-7q3 removed. Seven other pglens-review-* containers belong to other sessions and were left running.
```

**Suggested fix:** Stop the ASH sampler and release its DedicatedConn before mgr.Close (move the ashStops loop ahead of lines 333-335), or make Manager.Close context-aware so it cannot block on acquired conns. Move pool.Close outside m.mu. Make the sampler release its conn on ctx.Done. Add a test that starts the agent with ASH enabled and asserts clean exit within a bounded time after SIGTERM.

**Fix notes:** Call the ASH stop funcs before the mgr.Close loop in run.go (move the ashStops loop ahead of lines 333-335), or make the ASH sampler release its conn on ctx.Done. Move pool.Close outside m.mu in Manager.Close, the same way ForDatabase's eviction already does at conn.go:190-197, so a blocked close cannot stall other lookups. stop() is sync.Once, so calling it before mgr.Close is safe.

### AR-02 — EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs writes through a second session, bypassing READ ONLY (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:89`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The on-demand EXPLAIN executor wraps the statement in BEGIN READ ONLY / SET LOCAL statement_timeout / EXPLAIN (ANALYZE ...) / ROLLBACK (lines 89-101). Read-only only stops writes made inside that transaction. A function that opens its own session (dblink_exec, postgres_fdw, pg_background and similar) writes through another connection that the read-only transaction does not cover. The code comment at lines 86-88 claims PostgreSQL itself rejects writes under ANALYZE, which is false for these cases. This violates the hard invariant that pglens never alters monitored data.

**Failure scenario:** An operator enables allow_explain_analyze. A user with read-only monitoring rights, or any caller of the EXPLAIN endpoint, submits a SELECT that calls a volatile function which writes via dblink. The write commits on the monitored cluster outside the read-only transaction and is not rolled back.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reproduced on a local throwaway PG19rc1 container with a role holding pg_monitor and pg_read_all_data only: inside BEGIN READ ONLY, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT ar_writer(); where ar_writer() calls dblink_exec with an INSERT, so the row count went 1 to 2. Preconditions: allow_explain_analyze true (opt-in, default false), statement with no $n placeholders, dblink installed and EXECUTE granted. README.md:427 acknowledges that dblink effects are not undone, but this still breaks the stated read-only invariant and decision D1.
```

**Verification reasoning:** explain.go:89-101 wraps the statement in BEGIN READ ONLY, but dblink (and other cross-session extensions) open a separate backend whose session does not inherit the read-only transaction. default_transaction_read_only is a session setting applied only to agent connections (conn.go:77-82), not to the callee's connection. The executor's keyword check (exec_explain.go:53-66) allows SELECT, and placeholders are refused, so SELECT ar_writer() goes through to EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The gates are command/gate.go Allowed (refuses ANALYZE unless allow_explain_analyze, config.go:55, default false). The server never sees statement text (commands.go enqueue validates args only), so there is no server-side gate. README.md:427-429 acknowledges that dblink effects are not undone, but that disclosure does not meet the hard invariant or D1. The comment at exec_explain.go:86-88 is wrong for dblink. Preconditions: opt-in allow_explain_analyze, dblink installed, and a statement in pg_stat_statements that writes through a cross-session call. That includes ordinary application audit-writing functions, which pglens would re-execute. Control: a local writer under the same sequence is refused with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction', so the guard works for local writes only.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run -d --name pglens-review-ar02-7q3 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=scram-sha-256 postgres:19rc1-alpine. Setup as superuser: role monitor LOGIN with pg_monitor and pg_read_all_data; role writer with INSERT on audit; CREATE EXTENSION dblink; VOLATILE plpgsql ar_writer() calling dblink_exec('host=172.17.0.7 port=5432 dbname=postgres user=writer password=<redacted>', 'INSERT INTO audit(msg) VALUES (''via dblink'')'). The loopback address is trust in this image (pg_hba_file_rules: 127.0.0.1 trust), so non-superuser dblink needs the non-loopback container IP, which is scram. Run as monitor, exactly the agent sequence: SET default_transaction_read_only=on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s'; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT ar_writer(); ROLLBACK; then SELECT count(*). Output: rows_before 0, rows_after 1, superuser view shows id=1 'via dblink'. The plan root is a Result node with Output ar_writer(), not Function Scan. Control A (monitor, local writer in READ ONLY): ERROR cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction. Control B (superuser, direct INSERT in READ ONLY): same error, rows stay 0.
```

**Suggested fix:** Default-deny ANALYZE. Allow it only when the EXPLAIN plan without ANALYZE contains no Function Scan and no call to a volatile or non-pg_catalog function. Alternatively reject ANALYZE entirely when dblink, postgres_fdw or pg_background are installed. Correct the comment at exec_explain.go:86-88 and the README claims at README.md:395-429. Add an integration test that an ANALYZE over a dblink-writing function is refused.

**Fix notes:** Pitfall: SELECT f() plans as a Result node, not a Function Scan, so the suggested 'no Function Scan' check misses exactly this case. Untrusted procedural languages (plpython3u, plperlu) and pg_background or postgres_fdw can also open their own sessions, so a denylist of dblink/postgres_fdw/pg_background is incomplete. The connection string is attacker-chosen, so the write session cannot be forced read-only from the agent. Safer options: default-deny ANALYZE unless every function in the plan is pg_catalog and IMMUTABLE/STABLE, or refuse ANALYZE when cross-session extensions are installed in the target database. Correct the comment at exec_explain.go:86-88 and README.md:395-429.

### AB-02 — Torn or partially written tail record strands every later append (CONFIRMED, agent-buffer-wire)

**Location:** `internal/agent/buffer/buffer.go:644`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Segment.Append writes the length header, the CRC and the payload with three separate file.Write calls (lines 644, 651, 655). On any failure it returns without truncating, and fileSize is advanced only after all three succeed (lines 659-660). openSegment walks headers to count records, with no CRC check and no truncation of a torn tail. After a crash or a partial write, the torn bytes remain at the end of the segment, and all records appended after them are unreadable to the reader: it consumes the new records' bytes as the torn record's payload, fails CRC, and never realigns. The loss is silent.

**Failure scenario:** The process is killed (OOM kill, container stop timeout) between the header write at line 644 and the payload write at line 655. The header is on disk with no payload. The next start keeps the torn bytes; every record appended afterwards is silently undeliverable and SamplesDropped stays empty. ENOSPC during a part-write (R6) has the same effect in-process, and on a full disk it is the more likely trigger. Through the AB-01 cascade, the R7 run also deletes segment 0.

**Evidence:**

```text
buffer.go:644 `if _, err := s.file.Write(lenBuf); err != nil {` ; buffer.go:651 `if _, err := s.file.Write(creBuf); err != nil {` ; buffer.go:655 `if _, err := s.file.Write(data); err != nil {` followed by `return err` with no truncate; buffer.go:659-660 `s.recordCount++` / `s.fileSize += int64(len(lenBuf) + len(creBuf) + len(data))` only on success. openSegment is at buffer.go:569-631. Repro R3 (scratch): 3 records, last 5 bytes truncated, reopen, append records 3 and 4: delivered=[0 1] (want [0 1 3 4]), eofs=3, corrupt=1. R3b: appends made after the torn tail are not delivered in the same process (`[]`) or after restart (`[]`), SamplesDropped empty. R6 (in-process partial write: header plus 35 of 40 bytes, fileSize not advanced): delivered [0 1], records 3 and 4 stranded. R7 (5000-byte tail truncation, then 300 appends): delivered 178 of 302, records 3-127 missing, seg0 deleted after the AB-01 cascade, second drain delivered 0.
```

**Verification reasoning:** openSegment (buffer.go:569-631) counts a torn trailing record (Seek past EOF does not fail) and never validates CRC or truncates, and Segment.Append (634-663) does not truncate on a partial write. Reproduced all three shapes. (a) Restart after a torn tail, appends into the same segment: records 3 and 4 are never delivered, and records 5 and 6 are not delivered after a further restart either. (b) In-process short write (header plus 35 of 40 bytes reach disk, fileSize not advanced): later appends stranded. (c) Torn record mid-segment (record 99 of 0-199) and 27 more appends landing in the same segment before it rolls: the reader resumes at a misaligned offset, lands on the caught-up branch at segment end and skips the rest of seg0. Result: 27 records (100-126) lost silently, seg0 deleted, dropped=map[]. The age guard does not save the common case: openSegment sets createdAt from mtime, so a restart more than 1.5h after the last write rolls a new segment and loses only the torn record (confirmed: 199 of 200 delivered). The loss therefore fires on fast restarts and on in-process ENOSPC short writes, which are both ordinary buffer conditions. Verdict critical is justified because the loss is silent and ordinary.

**Repro:**

```text
Test A: 3 records of 40 bytes, Close, truncate last file 5 bytes, reopen, append records 3 and 4, drain: delivered=[0 1] corrupt=1 dropped=map[] (want [0 1 3 4]); after another restart, delivered=[]. Test B: in-process partial write (header plus 35 bytes written directly to segment file, then two Appends): delivered=[0 1]. Test C (chain, 100 records of 65536 bytes, torn record 99, 100 appends): delivered=172 of 200 missing=27 (first [100 101 102 103 104]) dupIdx=0 corrupt=2 dropped=map[] segsNow=[00000001.seg]. Test D (same as C but mtime set 2h back before reopen): delivered=199 missing=0 (excluding torn 99). Commands: go test -count=1 -run 'TestZZ_AB02' -v ./internal/agent/buffer/
```

**Suggested fix:** In openSegment, validate each record's CRC and truncate the file to the end of the last valid record (file.Truncate, then set fileSize), counting the discarded bytes in stats. In Segment.Append, on any write error call s.file.Truncate(s.fileSize) before returning. Build header plus payload into one buffer and issue one Write call to narrow the window. Add regression tests for R3 and R6 expecting [0 1 3 4].

**Fix notes:** In openSegment, validate each record's CRC and truncate only the trailing region after the last valid record (truncating at the first CRC failure would delete valid records after a mid-file bit flip); set fileSize from the truncated size and count discarded bytes. recordCount currently includes the torn record because Seek past EOF succeeds. In Segment.Append, on any write error call s.file.Truncate(s.fileSize) before returning (O_APPEND writes go to the real end, so the truncate must use the tracked size). Build header and payload into one buffer and issue one Write to narrow the window. Regression tests: Tests A and B expecting [0 1 3 4], and test C.

### AC-01 — EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs side-effect functions inside a READ ONLY transaction (pg_terminate_backend) (CONFIRMED, agent-commands)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:101`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The ANALYZE path executes the statement itself inside BEGIN READ ONLY (lines 89-92). READ ONLY does not stop volatile or side-effecting functions. The only gate is tier T1 plus allow_explain_analyze (internal/command/gate.go:14-15); nothing inspects the plan's function calls. The signal path requires T2 and allow_signal and applies guards (ownRole, ownBackend, isPglensApplication in exec_signal.go:60-62); the explain path bypasses all of them.

**Failure scenario:** An operator with T1 and allow_explain_analyze enabled requests EXPLAIN ANALYZE on a pg_stat_statements queryid whose text calls pg_terminate_backend, or calls a view or SQL function that wraps it. Sessions on the monitored instance are killed, including pglens and ash sessions, while the agent reports a read-only operation.

**Evidence:**

```text
PG19rc1 and PG18 containers, shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements. A constant-free SELECT joining pg_stat_activity to pg_roles WHERE NOT rolsuper, with pg_terminate_backend(a.pid) in the target list, run as EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) terminated 2 victim sessions (2 to 0 remaining). Plain EXPLAIN of the same statement terminated none (control: 1 survived). A view v_kill wrapping pg_terminate_backend, read via SELECT * FROM v_kill under ANALYZE, terminated 2 to 0. A session with application_name pglens/ash of the monitoring role was terminated through the explain path.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on postgres:19rc1-alpine and postgres:18.6-alpine. The ANALYZE path (exec_explain.go:89-101) runs the statement inside BEGIN READ ONLY, but READ ONLY does not stop pg_terminate_backend. The only gates are T1 plus allow_explain_analyze (gate.go:11-15), and both are opt-in. No guard in the agent, command or server code inspects the plan's functions. The signal path's ownRole/ownBackend/isPglensApplication checks (exec_signal.go:60-62) are bypassed. A T1 role with no pg_signal_backend still terminated its own pglens/ash session. The docs (docs/LIMITS.md section 4, README security bullets) disclose the effect only 'when the monitoring role holds pg_signal_backend', which understates the T1 reach. Disclosure is not a guard, and it conflicts with D1 (ANALYZE must not be able to alter state). The statement is constant-free, so it passes the keyword and placeholder checks. Critical per the rubric's read-only invariant.

**Repro:**

```text
Image postgres:19rc1-alpine (also postgres:18.6-alpine), started with shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements and POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust. Roles: CREATE ROLE pglens_t1 LOGIN; GRANT pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data TO pglens_t1 (no pg_signal_backend). As superuser: CREATE VIEW public.v_kill AS SELECT pid, pg_terminate_backend(pid) AS killed FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type='client backend' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND usename = current_user; then SELECT * FROM v_kill; once with no victims present, so pg_stat_statements records the text. Start two pglens_t1 client sessions, application_name 'pglens/ash' and 'victim-own', each running SELECT pg_sleep(600). T1 session (control): SET default_transaction_read_only=on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='15s'; EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS) SELECT * FROM v_kill; ROLLBACK; leaves both alive (2). T1 session (attack): same, but SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s' and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM v_kill; ROLLBACK; The plan shows pg_terminate_backend with Actual Rows 2.00. Afterwards, sessions named pglens/ash and victim-own: 2 before, 0 after, on both PG19rc1 and PG18.6.
```

**Suggested fix:** Refuse ANALYZE unless the plan is proven free of side effects. Run plain EXPLAIN (VERBOSE) first and collect every function invoked (Output and filter expressions), resolve each to pg_proc, and walk view and rule bodies transitively (pg_depend, pg_rewrite). Refuse when a function is volatile (provolatile <> 's'), user-defined (oid >= 16384 or a non-pg_catalog schema), or in a built-in deny-list: pg_terminate_backend, pg_cancel_backend, pg_reload_conf, dblink*, pg_advisory_*, pg_notify, pg_logical_emit_message, pg_stat_reset*, set_config, nextval, setval, lo_*, pg_sleep*. Only then run ANALYZE. Add integration tests per deny-list entry that assert refusal and that the target sessions survive. This implements decision D1.

**Fix notes:** Pre-check must not depend on the planner. Plain EXPLAIN folds IMMUTABLE calls, so a 'run plain EXPLAIN first, then inspect' design is itself the AC-02 vector. Parse the text in the agent, resolve names via catalog SELECTs, and walk view bodies through pg_rewrite and pg_depend. Refusing non-pg_catalog functions is not enough: v_kill is a user view that wraps only a pg_catalog function. Name resolution must follow the parser (see the overload caveat in AC-02). Docs (LIMITS.md section 4, README security bullets) must change with the fix.

Status: open

### AC-02 — Plain EXPLAIN (default path) runs a planted IMMUTABLE function with side effects at plan time (CONFIRMED, agent-commands)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:101`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Plain EXPLAIN (no ANALYZE) is enabled by default (commands.enabled defaults to true, config.go CommandsEnabled()) and runs with no function check. The planner constant-folds calls to IMMUTABLE functions without arguments, so the body of an IMMUTABLE plpgsql function runs during planning even without ANALYZE. Declared volatility is not enforced by PostgreSQL, so IMMUTABLE is no safety signal.

**Failure scenario:** A role with CREATE on any schema of a monitored database creates an IMMUTABLE function with side effects. Any T1 plan request for a queryid whose statement calls it (pg_stat_statements records the text) runs the side effect under the default configuration, with allow_explain_analyze off. The monitoring role does not verify the function.

**Evidence:**

```text
Function imm_kill() LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE that calls pg_terminate_backend over non-superuser sessions. EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) SELECT imm_kill() on PG18 and PG19rc1 terminated 2 sessions (2 to 0). The statement is constant-free, so it passes the keyword gate.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on postgres:19rc1-alpine (session kill) and postgres:18.6-alpine (session kill). A dblink variant on postgres:19rc1-alpine performed a remote DELETE with ANALYZE off. Plain EXPLAIN runs planning inside BEGIN READ ONLY (exec_explain.go:89-101), and the planner constant-folds the zero-argument IMMUTABLE call, so the function body runs. No function check exists anywhere. The claim's wording is off in one respect: the default config is T0 (commands.enabled defaults to true, but gate.go:11-12 refuses EXPLAIN below T1). The exposure is therefore every T1 deployment, not the default install. Preconditions: T1 is an opt-in grant (pg_read_all_data), a non-superuser role must hold CREATE on a schema (PG15+ does not grant it to PUBLIC by default), and the statement must be recorded in pg_stat_statements. The dblink variant also needs dblink installed (superuser-only) and password credentials in the function body. Because the function's side effect reached the monitored database's own rows, I rate it critical rather than the reported high.

**Repro:**

```text
Image postgres:19rc1-alpine (session-kill case also on postgres:18.6-alpine). Roles: pglens_t1 with pg_monitor and pg_read_all_data (no pg_signal_backend); dev with CREATE on schema public (GRANT CREATE ON SCHEMA public TO dev). As dev: CREATE FUNCTION public.imm_kill() RETURNS int LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$ DECLARE n int; BEGIN SELECT count(*) INTO n FROM (SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type='client backend' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND usename = current_user) s; RETURN n; END $$; As superuser: SELECT imm_kill(); once, with no victims, to record the statement. Start two pglens_t1 sessions (pg_sleep(600)). T1 session: SET default_transaction_read_only=on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='15s'; EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS) SELECT imm_kill(); ROLLBACK; Plan: Node Type Result, Output ["2"], so the body ran during planning. Victims: 2 before, 0 after. dblink variant (PG19rc1, dblink installed by superuser, remote role app_rw with DELETE on public.victim_rows, function dev.imm_delete() IMMUTABLE whose body does PERFORM dblink_exec('host=<non-loopback address> port=5432 dbname=postgres user=app_rw password=<redacted>', 'DELETE FROM public.victim_rows WHERE id = (SELECT min(id) FROM public.victim_rows)') and RETURN 1): T1 plain EXPLAIN SELECT imm_delete() inside BEGIN READ ONLY, as above. Rows in public.victim_rows: 1 before, 0 after.
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the pre-check from AC-01 to plain EXPLAIN as well. Refuse any non-pg_catalog (user-defined) function regardless of its declared provolatile, and refuse the deny-list functions. Add a regression test with a planted IMMUTABLE plpgsql function that asserts refusal and that the sessions survive.

**Fix notes:** Same fix as AC-01, plus the plain EXPLAIN path must get the same function check: refuse any user-defined function regardless of declared volatility, and refuse extension functions outside an allowlist (dblink, dblink_exec, dblink_send_query, pg_terminate_backend, pg_advisory_*, pg_logical_emit_message, and similar). Folded calls are invisible in the plan output, which showed only Output ["2"] and ["1"], so the check must run before EXPLAIN. Unverified caveat, worth a test: a function in a writable schema can shadow a pg_catalog one through a better type match (the CVE-2018-1058 pattern), so name resolution must follow the parser, not a name-based deny-list. Add a regression test with a planted IMMUTABLE plpgsql function that asserts refusal and that the target sessions survive.

### AC-03 — EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a view calling dblink_exec performs a remote write (CONFIRMED, agent-commands)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:101`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The READ ONLY transaction is local only. dblink opens a separate connection and transaction on a remote server, so a remote DML commits regardless. dblink_exec is executable by PUBLIC by default, and the view that wraps it carries the remote connection string and credentials. A constant-free SELECT from that view under ANALYZE performs the remote DML.

**Failure scenario:** A view or function in a monitored database that calls dblink_exec, or that reads through a foreign table whose remote side is volatile, is run by ANALYZE of a monitoring query. Rows in a database pglens is meant to only read are deleted or altered, with no permission error because dblink_exec is granted to PUBLIC.

**Evidence:**

```text
PG18 and PG19rc1 with dblink installed in the monitored database. A view wrapping dblink_exec with a DELETE statement, read via EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) inside the READ ONLY transaction: row count of the target table went from 99999 to 99998. The write was not blocked by default_transaction_read_only.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on postgres:19rc1-alpine. EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) of a constant-free SELECT from a view that calls dblink_exec performed a remote DELETE that committed on the remote connection. The READ ONLY transaction is local only, and dblink_exec is executable by PUBLIC (has_function_privilege true for pglens_t1). The gate is ANALYZE opt-in plus T1, and the stored statement text is constant-free. The application's own run of the statement had already done the remote write once, and ANALYZE repeats it. The docs (LIMITS.md section 4) list 'remote work through dblink' as a known effect. That is disclosure, not a guard, and it contradicts D1 (ANALYZE must not be able to alter data). Preconditions: installing dblink needs a superuser, and the view must embed remote write credentials. A non-superuser dblink connection must use a password, and the server must ask for one: the image's loopback rule is trust, and that connection was refused, so the target address has to be scram.

**Repro:**

```text
Image postgres:19rc1-alpine, started with POSTGRES_PASSWORD (scram for non-loopback host connections). As superuser: CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements; CREATE EXTENSION dblink; CREATE ROLE pglens_t1 LOGIN PASSWORD ...; GRANT pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data TO pglens_t1; CREATE ROLE app_rw LOGIN PASSWORD 'app_pw'; CREATE TABLE public.victim_rows AS SELECT generate_series(1,5) AS id; GRANT SELECT, DELETE ON public.victim_rows TO app_rw; CREATE VIEW public.v_remote_del AS SELECT dblink_exec('host=<container non-loopback IP> port=5432 dbname=postgres user=app_rw password=<redacted>', 'DELETE FROM public.victim_rows WHERE id = (SELECT min(id) FROM public.victim_rows)') AS remote_result; Recording: SELECT * FROM v_remote_del; once as superuser (rows 5 to 4). T1 control: SET default_transaction_read_only=on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='15s'; EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS) SELECT * FROM v_remote_del; ROLLBACK; leaves 3 rows. T1 attack: same, with SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s' and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT * FROM v_remote_del; ROLLBACK; rows go from 3 to 2.
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the AC-01 pre-check with dblink, dblink_exec, dblink_send_query and similar extension functions in the deny-list. Refuse ANALYZE for any plan that touches foreign tables (relkind 'f') or functions owned by extensions outside an allowlist. Add an integration test with dblink installed that asserts refusal and an unchanged row count.

**Fix notes:** Same ANALYZE pre-check as AC-01, plus refuse foreign tables (relkind f) and any call to dblink or dblink_exec or dblink_send_query and similar functions. The docs must change with the fix: they currently call remote dblink work a known effect.

Status: open

### AC-13 — No test proves EXPLAIN ANALYZE refuses side-effecting statements; D1 hardening is not implemented (CONFIRMED, agent-commands)

**Location:** `internal/command/gate.go:14`

**Category:** test-gap · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The gate checks only AllowExplainAnalyze (gate.go:14-15). TestINTCMD007 (internal/agent/exec_explain_integration_test.go:52-100) proves refusal of a plain UPDATE by keyword only, and that refusal depends on the read-only transaction. gate_test.go covers the gate matrix only. Nothing covers pg_terminate_backend, dblink, advisory locks, notify, stats resets, logical messages, view or SQL-function wrappers, or a planted IMMUTABLE function. Decision D1 in docs/plans/004_plan-FullReview/overview.md requires exactly this refusal and says Tests prove the invariant; the hardening is absent.

**Failure scenario:** A refactor or new function in a monitored database reintroduces a write or kill path while every current test stays green.

**Evidence:**

```text
AC-01 through AC-05 reproduced on PG18 and PG19rc1 against the current code. A search of the test files finds no side-effect cases.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The gate (gate.go:9-16) checks only the tier and AllowExplainAnalyze for KindExplain. The executor refuses only non-read keywords (exec_explain.go:52-63) and relies on BEGIN READ ONLY for everything else. TestINTCMD007 (exec_explain_integration_test.go:56-100) refuses an UPDATE in the keyword pre-check (exec_explain.go:61-63) before any SQL runs. It therefore does not exercise the read-only transaction, and the finding's claim that the refusal 'depends on the read-only transaction' is wrong. No explain test covers pg_terminate_backend, dblink, advisory locks, logical messages or planted functions. test/pgtest/perm_test.go checks only role permissions. Reproduced on PostgreSQL 18.6 with the monitoring role (pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data, pg_signal_backend, so tier T2) and allow_explain_analyze=true, allow_signal=false. (a) Allowed(terminate) returned 'signal gate is closed', but EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a constant-free SELECT pg_terminate_backend(...) passed the gate, returned a plan, and ended the victim session with FATAL 57P01. (b) As pglens_t1, through the executor's exact transaction pattern, EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT review.touch() ran a dblink_exec UPDATE on its own connection. It changed one row of the monitored database (count with v=-1: 0 before, 1 after), and the outer ROLLBACK did not undo it. That breaks the read-only invariant under the opt-in setting. Default-off limits exposure but does not change the breach, so critical per the rubric. Preconditions for (b): dblink installed in the monitored DB, a function calling dblink with a writing role's credentials, and a non-loopback address, since PostgreSQL refuses dblink for non-superusers over trust auth. The D1 text (docs/plans/004_plan-FullReview/overview.md) is absent from this worktree and from every branch in git log --all, so its wording could not be checked.

**Repro:**

```text
(a) Temporary Go test in internal/agent against postgres:18.6-alpine. Role pglens_t1 holds pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data and pg_signal_backend. Statement recorded via mgr.ConnFor('') then queryid read from pg_stat_statements. A victim pgx session runs pg_sleep(60). command.Allowed(KindExplain, {QueryID, Analyze:true}, Gates{TierSignal, AllowExplainAnalyze:true, AllowSignal:false}) returned true. Allowed(KindTerminate, {PID}, same gates) returned 'signal gate is closed'. NewExplainExecutor().Execute returned plan bytes=3645. Victim: 'FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command (SQLSTATE 57P01)'. (b) psql as pglens_t1 in db app: SET default_transaction_read_only=on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s'; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT review.touch(); ROLLBACK. review.touch() calls dblink_exec('host=<bridge-ip> port=5432 dbname=app user=writer password=<redacted>', 'UPDATE public.t_app SET v=-1 WHERE v=1'). With host=localhost the call failed with 'password or GSSAPI delegated credentials required', because loopback is trust.
```

**Suggested fix:** Implement the pre-check from AC-01 and add integration tests per effect class (signal, dblink, advisory lock, notify, stats reset, logical message, view and SQL-function wrappers, planted IMMUTABLE function). Each test should assert the rejection and that the side effect did not happen. Run them on PG15 to PG19.

**Fix notes:** A read-only transaction cannot stop pg_terminate_backend, pg_cancel_backend, dblink connections or session advisory locks, as docs/LIMITS.md section 4 says. Hardening must refuse EXPLAIN ANALYZE of statements that call functions outside an allowlist. pg_stat_statements does not record the call graph, so this needs a planner-level or function-level check. Alternatively, gate kill-capable calls separately. Note the current gate lets allow_explain_analyze=true bypass allow_signal=false, which is a policy bypass in itself. Add integration tests per effect class (signal, dblink, advisory lock, notify, stats reset, planted function) that assert the refusal and that the effect did not happen. Run them on PG15 to PG19.

Status: open

### CR-05 — Plaintext role passwords from utility DDL are shipped as pg_stat_statements query text (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/stat_statements.go:128`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The aggregate uses min(query) and LEFT(query, 8192), and the text is cached and shipped in QueryTexts (lines 303-309, returned at 317). Nothing redacts credentials. Other checks do redact: settings.go:198-210 (redactSetting) strips passwords from archive_command and conninfo.

**Failure scenario:** A DBA runs CREATE ROLE or ALTER ROLE with a password on a monitored cluster. pglens stores that literal in query text (the store.QueryTextRow path) and exposes it through the query-text UI to every viewer with that access. The secret persists long after the statement.

**Evidence:**

```text
Live on PG17 with the pg_monitor role: pg_stat_statements text contains "CREATE ROLE tmp_secret_probe LOGIN PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe'" and "ALTER ROLE tmp_secret_probe PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe-2'" in plaintext. The statements query returns both rows, with query text not masked.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on PG 17.11 with the real stat_statements Scrape under a T0 role. QueryTexts held plaintext: CREATE ROLE tmp_secret_probe LOGIN PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe'; ALTER ROLE tmp_secret_probe PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe-2'; and CREATE ROLE pglens_t0 LOGIN PASSWORD (the review fixture role). The provisioning script deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:33 runs ALTER ROLE pglens LOGIN PASSWORD :'<redacted>'; psql sends the literal, so re-running the documented provisioning step places the monitoring credential into pg_stat_statements and then into pglens's query-text store. No redaction on the path: stat_statements.go Scrape (QueryTexts around lines 303-309), readStatements, store.WriteQueryTexts (internal/store/write.go around 615-640), the api.go query-text select (around 1113) and api_ash.go (around 605). redactSetting in settings.go covers only *_command and *conninfo settings. Severity: the rubric lists security hole as critical; credential disclosure into a central store served to every viewer qualifies. The counter-argument (pg_monitor can already read the texts on the host) does not cover the wider audience of the central UI. Scope: PG 17.11 only.

**Repro:**

```text
Container as in CR-01. Setup as super: CREATE ROLE tmp_secret_probe LOGIN PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe'; ALTER ROLE tmp_secret_probe PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe-2'. Command: PGLENS_REVIEW_DSN_T0=postgres://pglens_t0:<redacted>@<ip>:5432/app?sslmode=disable go test -tags reviewrepro -count=1 -v -run TestReviewCR05 ./internal/check/. Output: CR05 stat_statements(T0) err=nil texts=30; CR05 LEAK queryid=... text=CREATE ROLE pglens_t0 LOGIN PASSWORD 'pglens_t0_pw'; CR05 LEAK ... text=CREATE ROLE tmp_secret_probe LOGIN PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe'; CR05 LEAK ... text=ALTER ROLE tmp_secret_probe PASSWORD 'hunter2-probe-2'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Before shipping, redact PASSWORD '...' (and other string literals in utility statements) from the text, and never ship texts from utility credential DDL. Add a unit test with a PASSWORD literal, mirroring settings_test.go.

**Fix notes:** Redact before caching and shipping in stat_statements.go (before the QueryTexts assignment and the LRU add), so the redacted text is also what the cache holds. Cover CREATE and ALTER ROLE and USER PASSWORD, quoted and unquoted forms, ENCRYPTED and UNENCRYPTED, and PASSWORD NULL. Also review conninfo or OPTIONS password literals in CREATE and ALTER SUBSCRIPTION, SERVER and USER MAPPING (not verified here). Add a unit test mirroring settings_test.go. Existing query_texts rows already contain these texts and persist; a purge or redaction migration is needed, or the fix leaves the secrets stored. The text cache suppresses resends for an hour, so do not rely on re-scrapes to overwrite old rows.

### AT-21 — ASH connection can be re-dialled after Close and leak a pooled connection (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/agent/ash.go:151`

**Category:** leak · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** ashConn has no closed flag. Close() (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:166-174) releases the connection, but an in-flight sampler tick that is still running can call Query and then connectLocked (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:139-164), which dials again using the agent context. Nothing releases that connection, so it stays checked out until the pool closes.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** During shutdown a tick that started before cancellation is still inside Query when Close runs. It dials once more and holds one of the four pool slots until the pool closes.

**Correction (from verification):** Corrections to the finding: the file is cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go, since internal/agent/ash.go does not exist.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:139-174; stop order in startASH (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:95-101): cancel, then sampler.Stop, then conn.Close.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The core leak is real. ashConn has no closed flag: Query after Close re-dials through connectLocked (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:132-164), keeps a pool slot, and nothing releases it. Escalated to critical because the held connection makes pgxpool.Close block. Production shutdown in runAgentCommand calls mgr.Close() at run.go:333-335 after cancel (run.go:314) and the flush. The ASH stop() closures are deferred (run.go:184-188) and run only after mgr.Close returns, so the dedicated ASH connection is still held at that point. Any SIGTERM with an ASH-connected target therefore hangs until SIGKILL. Corrections to the finding: the file is cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go, since internal/agent/ash.go does not exist. The in-flight case is wrong: ashConn.Query holds c.mu, so Close waits for it. The real trigger is a Query issued after Close, enabled because sampler.Stop (sampler.go:120-137) does not wait for run() to return.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway postgres:17.11-alpine on 127.0.0.1:55439, with temporary package-main tests that were deleted afterwards. Control with the connection released before Close: 4 of 4 other callers acquired slots. Late Query after Close: 3 of 4 acquired, and the 4th failed with 'context deadline exceeded'. Manager.Close with the leaked connection blocked more than 8s. The goroutine dump showed puddle v2.2.2 pool.go:195 in sync.WaitGroup.Wait, reached from pgxpool v5.10.0 pool.go:457-459, reached from internal/agent/conn.go:377. Production order, with the base context cancelled first: the connection held blocked Manager.Close for more than 8s, while releasing it first returned at once.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add a closed flag under c.mu, set it in Close, and check it in Query and connectLocked before dialling.

**Fix notes:** (1) Release the ASH connection before mgr.Close: stop ASH explicitly before the flush and Close sequence at run.go:314-335 instead of relying on the defer. stop() is already idempotent through sync.Once, so this is safe. Flush the final ash window before cancelling the flush loop, or that data is lost. (2) Make Sampler.Stop wait for run() to return, for example with a done channel, so no Query follows Close. (3) Add a closed flag to ashConn, set under c.mu in Close and checked in Query and connectLocked before dialling. (4) Consider bounding mgr.Close with a timeout, because pgxpool.Close waits for acquired connections; conn.go:190-192 documents this contract.

Status: open

### DR-01 — Rerun leaves a pre-existing pglens role superuser, owner of objects and write-capable (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:26`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The DO block only creates the role when it is missing, then runs ALTER ROLE pglens LOGIN PASSWORD. It never clears SUPERUSER, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE, REPLICATION or BYPASSRLS, never resets NOINHERIT, never revokes write-capable memberships or direct ACLs, never checks object ownership, and never clears per-database overrides of default_transaction_read_only. deploy/sql/README.md says the script is safe to run again.

**Failure scenario:** An operator who created pglens earlier as superuser (the storage image with POSTGRES_USER=pglens does this) or for another purpose reruns the documented script. The monitoring role keeps SUPERUSER and write memberships. The agent's tier check reports T0 while the role can write, drop or alter data.

**Evidence:**

```text
monitoring_user.sql L26-33 (IF NOT EXISTS ... CREATE ROLE pglens LOGIN; ALTER ROLE pglens LOGIN PASSWORD :'<redacted>';), L82 ALTER ROLE pglens SET default_transaction_read_only = on; deploy/sql/README.md L3-5 'It is safe to run again: it adds the requested memberships and reapplies the session limits without creating an extension or changing database objects.' Verified on PostgreSQL 15.19, 16.15, 17.11, 18.6 and 19rc1: after a rerun over a pre-existing pglens with SUPERUSER CREATEDB CREATEROLE REPLICATION BYPASSRLS, an owned table, pg_write_all_data (and pg_maintain on 17+) membership, a direct INSERT grant and a per-database default_transaction_read_only=off, all attributes stayed true, the owner stayed pglens, the memberships stayed, and the script exited 0.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on PostgreSQL 17.11. The script only runs CREATE ROLE inside an IF NOT EXISTS and then ALTER ROLE ... LOGIN PASSWORD. It never demotes SUPERUSER, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE, REPLICATION or BYPASSRLS, never resets INHERIT, never revokes memberships or ACLs, and never clears per-database overrides. The script exits 0, and the resulting role is a write-capable superuser that owns a table. Nothing elsewhere guards this: the agent does not check rolsuper, and the agent's tier probe reports T0 for this superuser, so the tier reporting is also wrong. The read-only invariant is violated by the documented, idempotent path, so critical per the rubric.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-dr-7f3a-17 (postgres:17.11-alpine). As postgres: CREATE ROLE pglens LOGIN SUPERUSER CREATEDB CREATEROLE REPLICATION BYPASSRLS PASSWORD 'old'; CREATE TABLE public.owned_by_pglens(id int); ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO pglens; GRANT pg_write_all_data TO pglens; ALTER ROLE pglens IN DATABASE postgres SET default_transaction_read_only=off. Then psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v pglens_password=newpass -v dbname=postgres -f /tmp/monitoring_user.sql gives EXIT=0. After the run: rolsuper=t rolcreatedb=t rolcreaterole=t rolreplication=t rolbypassrls=t; tableowner=pglens; pg_has_role('pglens','pg_write_all_data','MEMBER')=t. As pglens: INSERT INTO public.owned_by_pglens VALUES (42) gives INSERT 0 1, and CREATE TABLE / DROP TABLE succeed. The agent's direct-membership probe from internal/agent/conn.go queryCapabilities, run as that superuser with no tier memberships, returns f and f, so it reports T0.
```

**Suggested fix:** After creating the role, always run ALTER ROLE pglens NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS INHERIT and ALTER ROLE pglens RESET ALL, then re-apply the session limits; also ALTER ROLE pglens IN DATABASE :"dbname" RESET default_transaction_read_only. Add a fail-closed guard (RAISE EXCEPTION, so ON_ERROR_STOP fails the run) when pg_shdepend has owner rows (deptype 'o') or non-whitelisted ACL rows for pglens, or when pg_auth_members lists a write-capable predefined role. Whitelist only the CONNECT grant and the two pg_control EXECUTE grants the script itself makes. Correct the 'safe to run again' claim until this exists. Add an integration test for the rerun scenario.

**Fix notes:** After CREATE ROLE, run ALTER ROLE pglens NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS INHERIT, then ALTER ROLE pglens RESET ALL. RESET ALL does not clear pg_db_role_setting rows that are scoped IN DATABASE, so reset each database separately (one ALTER ROLE ... IN DATABASE <db> RESET default_transaction_read_only per pg_database row, which needs per-database psql runs or a fail-closed check). Do not auto-REASSIGN OWNED; RAISE EXCEPTION when pg_shdepend has deptype 'o' rows for pglens, or when non-whitelisted ACLs or write-capable predefined roles (pg_write_all_data, pg_maintain, pg_write_server_files, pg_execute_server_program and similar) are present, so ON_ERROR_STOP fails the run. The README sentence 'safe to run again' (deploy/sql/README.md L3-5) must stay false until this exists.

Status: open

### DR-04 — PUBLIC can call lo_create and lo_from_bytea, which write pg_largeobject under default read-only on PG15 (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:38`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The script never revokes EXECUTE on the large-object write functions, which PostgreSQL grants to PUBLIC. On PostgreSQL 16 to 19 the default read-only GUC blocks them ('cannot execute lo_from_bytea() in a read-only transaction'). On PostgreSQL 15 with the default GUC on, lo_from_bytea succeeds and writes pg_largeobject. On every version, SET default_transaction_read_only = off re-enables them, and that SET is allowed for the role. The opt-in EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) path executes a caller-supplied statement, so pglens can reach this path.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A T0 or T1 role with allow_explain_analyze enabled runs a statement that calls lo_from_bytea on PG15. A row is written to pg_largeobject in the monitored cluster. On 16 to 19 any session can SET default_transaction_read_only off and write the same way.

**Correction (from verification):** Correction: the statement text comes from pg_stat_statements via queryid, not from the command payload (exec_explain.go L20-21 and L38), so 'caller-supplied' is inaccurate.

**Evidence:**

```text
Verified on postgres:15.19-alpine with role pglens after the script ran, no extra grants: with the default GUC on, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT lo_from_bytea(...) raised pg_largeobject_metadata count from 0 to 1. On 16.15, 17.11, 18.6 and 19rc1 the same call was blocked by default. With SET default_transaction_read_only=off, lo_create and lo_from_bytea succeeded on 15 through 19.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Confirmed on PostgreSQL 15.19. With the script's default tiers and no extra grants, an autocommitted lo_from_bytea run as pglens with the role default default_transaction_read_only=on succeeds, and the pg_largeobject_metadata count goes from 0 to 1 and persists. The EXPLAIN ANALYZE path shape used by internal/agent/exec_explain.go (BEGIN READ ONLY, EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a literal-free SELECT calling lo_create, ROLLBACK) also writes inside the transaction (count 1 to 2), so the read-only guard fails on PG15. On 16.15, 17.11, 18.6 and 19rc1 the default guard blocks the call, and SET default_transaction_read_only=off re-enables it on 17, 18 and 19. Critical per the rubric because the monitoring role itself can durably write data on PG15 with default settings. Mitigations, which do not remove the finding: the agent's own ROLLBACK removes the EXPLAIN-path write, and on 16+ the agent cannot issue a SET. Correction: the statement text comes from pg_stat_statements via queryid, not from the command payload (exec_explain.go L20-21 and L38), so 'caller-supplied' is inaccurate.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-dr-7f3a-15 (postgres:15.19-alpine). Script run as postgres with default tiers gives EXIT=0. As pglens: SHOW default_transaction_read_only gives on; SELECT has_function_privilege('pglens','lo_from_bytea(oid,bytea)','EXECUTE') gives t; count(pg_largeobject_metadata) gives 0; SELECT lo_from_bytea(0,'\x41'::bytea) gives oid 16389; the count afterwards is 1. Agent-shaped transaction: BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s'; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) SELECT lo_create(oid) FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database(); count gives 2 inside; ROLLBACK; count gives 1 after. 16.15: SELECT lo_from_bytea(...) gives ERROR: cannot execute lo_from_bytea() in a read-only transaction, and BEGIN READ ONLY; SELECT lo_create(0) gives ERROR: cannot execute lo_create() in a read-only transaction. 18.6 and 19rc1: default blocked, and after SET default_transaction_read_only=off the write succeeds (oid 16395 and 16391). 17.11: default blocked, and GUC off succeeds (oid 16397).
```

**Suggested fix:** In the script, REVOKE EXECUTE FROM PUBLIC for lo_create(oid), lo_from_bytea(oid,bytea), lo_put(oid,bigint,bytea), lo_unlink(oid), lo_truncate(oid,integer), lo_truncate64(oid,bigint), lowrite(integer,bytea) and lo_import variants, in every monitored database (pg_proc is per database, so the script must run in each one). Document the per-database step. Add a test that a monitoring role cannot write pg_largeobject with the GUC set off.

**Fix notes:** REVOKE EXECUTE ON the lo_* write functions FROM PUBLIC must run in every monitored database, because pg_proc is per database. A DO block in the script's own database will not cover the others, so the fix needs a per-database step that is documented and checked. Verify after the fix with SET default_transaction_read_only=off plus lo_from_bytea, which must fail. Adjacent, not verified end to end through the agent: exec_explain.go L83-88 claims a READ ONLY transaction rejects writes from volatile functions. That is overbroad. On 19rc1, SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid) inside BEGIN READ ONLY returns t and cancels the other session. A T2 role with allow_explain_analyze could therefore reach signal side effects through EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a stored statement, bypassing the allow_signal gate. Confirm before fixing.

Status: open

### RO-01 — EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs attacker-authored SELECT under the monitor identity (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:57`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The ANALYZE gate checks only the first SQL keyword (must be SELECT/VALUES/WITH/TABLE) and the absence of $n placeholders. The executed text is the normalised pg_stat_statements query, which is written by any role that runs SQL in the monitored database. ANALYZE runs that text under the monitor's own identity inside BEGIN READ ONLY. The READ ONLY transaction blocks data writes but not side effects: session-level function calls, WAL emission and termination of other sessions all still work.

**Failure scenario:** A role that can run SQL on the monitored instance plants a constant-free statement that calls pg_terminate_backend. An operator, or a server-side request, asks for EXPLAIN ANALYZE of its queryid on a target with allow_explain_analyze=true and a signal-capable monitor role. The agent executes it: the application's sessions are terminated, and advisory locks it takes are kept (see RO-03). This breaks the hard rule that pglens only reads.

**Evidence:**

```text
exec_explain.go:57-67: `if args.Analyze { if !readOnlyExplainKeyword(keyword) {...}; if hasParams {...} }`; line 89 `BEGIN READ ONLY`; line 101 `explainSQL := fmt.Sprintf("EXPLAIN (%s) %s", options, statement)`. Verified on PG17 and PG19 in throwaway containers: an app role ran `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename = current_user AND pid <> pg_backend_pid();` (no constants, so pg_stat_statements stored it verbatim). Then the monitor role (pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data, pg_signal_backend) ran BEGIN READ ONLY; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS, BUFFERS) on the same text; ROLLBACK; and its own sleeping session was terminated. pg_try_advisory_lock and pg_logical_emit_message also executed inside the READ ONLY transaction.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The gate at internal/agent/exec_explain.go:57-67 checks only the first keyword and placeholders. BEGIN READ ONLY does not block side-effecting function calls. Reproduced through the real Execute() path (NewExplainExecutor().Execute with Analyze=true): (a) a T1 monitor with pg_monitor+pg_read_all_data and no pg_signal_backend ran a constant-free statement planted by the app role, SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid() AND usename = current_user, and its own sleeping backend was terminated (57P01). (b) The same kind of statement planted with datname IS NOT NULL, run by a monitor with pg_signal_backend, terminated an app-role backend (57P01). The same run by the T1 monitor failed with 42501 and the victim survived. The bypass is real: SignalExecutor refuses pglens-own backends (exec_signal.go:60-62) and requires T2 plus allow_signal (command/gate.go:18-24), but the EXPLAIN path reaches the same function under allow_explain_analyze only. docs/LIMITS.md section 4 and README discuss pg_terminate_backend only for the pg_signal_backend case, not T1 self-termination or attacker-authored text. Severity stays critical because a read-only tier role produces a non-read effect on the monitored instance. Mitigations: opt-in (default false), an explicit analyze request, and a planting role that needs SQL access. Reproduced on PG17.11 and PG19rc1.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run -d --name pglens-review-ro-17-7f3a -p 127.0.0.1:55417:5432 postgres:17.11-alpine -c shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements (same for postgres:19rc1-alpine on 55419). Roles: app (CREATE on public), monitor (pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data, pg_signal_backend), monitor_t1 (pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data). Temporary Go test in internal/agent calling NewExplainExecutor().Execute(ctx, mgr, command.Args{QueryID, Datname:"postgres", Analyze:true}). Output PG17: 'Execute(analyze) as monitor_t1: err=<nil> resultBytes=3488' then '[T1 own-session] sleeping backend pid=102 ended with: FATAL: terminating connection due to administrator command (SQLSTATE 57P01)'. Foreign case: '[monitor-with-pg_signal_backend] Execute(analyze) err=<nil>' then 'app victim ... ended with: ... 57P01'; '[monitor-T1-no-signal] Execute(analyze) err=ERROR: permission denied to terminate process (SQLSTATE 42501)' and 'app victim ... still running'. Same results on PG19rc1. Test file and containers removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Do not treat the keyword gate plus READ ONLY transaction as the security boundary. (1) Run the command under SET LOCAL ROLE to a dedicated NOLOGIN role that has pg_read_all_data only and no pg_signal_backend. At startup, refuse the command path if that role has write, CREATE or signal privileges. A role switch alone is not enough: advisory-lock functions stay callable through PUBLIC EXECUTE (verified), so either the DBA revokes them or the agent refuses statements that call them. (2) Allow ANALYZE only when every function call in the plan resolves, via pg_proc, to a read-only allowlist with provolatile in ('i','s'). (3) Run on a dedicated non-pooled connection that is closed afterwards (RO-03). (4) Keep the gate default-off and log queryid, a statement hash and the requesting identity.

**Fix notes:** Do not rely on READ ONLY plus the keyword gate. Apply the same own-session refusal as exec_signal.go:60-62 and the allow_signal gate on the EXPLAIN path, or run under a dedicated role with no signal membership (SET ROLE is untested; PUBLIC EXECUTE on pg_terminate_backend means the role check is what protects it). Restrict function calls to provolatile in ('i','s') via pg_proc. The fix must cover both the self-kill (T1, no signal grant) and the foreign-kill cases.

### AR-04 — server.url with trailing slash makes every push 404 and get dropped (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `internal/agent/pusher.go:352`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** buildRequest builds the URL as p.serverURL + "/api/v1/push" with no normalization. A server.url ending in / produces the path //api/v1/push. The chi router returns 404 for that path. The command dispatcher (command.go:67) does strings.TrimRight on the same URL, so the two components disagree. The 404 falls into the pusher's default branch (see AR-05) and the envelope is dropped.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** An operator writes url: http://pglens-server:8080/ (a common style). Every envelope is dropped. Only a dropped counter and a last_error line show it, and the healthz state stays ok.

**Correction (from verification):** Correction to the finding: the status is not always 404.

**Evidence:**

```text
Verified: the raw request line captured by a fake receiver is POST //api/v1/push. chi returns 404 for //api/v1/push and 202 for /api/v1/push. The agent logs push returned 404, the dropped counter increments, and healthz still reports state ok. Code: pusher.go:352, command.go:67, internal/server/http.go:14-60.
```

**Verification reasoning:** pusher.go:352 builds p.serverURL + '/api/v1/push' with no normalisation. config.validate (config.go:183-188) only checks non-empty, and the PGLENS_SERVER_URL override (config.go:154-156) runs before validate, so both paths are affected. The dispatcher trims the slash (command.go:18, NewDispatcher), so the components disagree. Correction to the finding: the status is not always 404. With the UI enabled, the request is exempt from RequireCredential (session.go:184-187, path not under /api/) and reaches the SPA fallback, which returns 405 for any non-GET (webui.go:22-24). With the UI disabled it is chi's 404. Both are non-202 and take the default drop branch (pusher.go:304-316), so the core claim holds. The router-side repro shows the correct path /api/v1/push reaches IngestHandler (400 invalid gzip), while the double-slash path does not. healthz stays ok.

**Repro:**

```text
Temp test internal/server/zz_review_server2_test.go (TestZZReviewAR04PusherEndToEnd): real NewRouter with UI enabled, agent.NewPusher(srv.URL+'/'), Queue a valid envelope, Push. Command: go test ./internal/server -run TestZZReviewAR04PusherEndToEnd -v. Output: 'AR-04 pusher server.url="http://127.0.0.1:33875/" pushErr=<nil> acked=0 dropped=1 health=ok lastErr="push returned 405: method not allowed"'. Also TestZZReviewAR04TrailingSlashRoute, same router, raw POST with a valid bearer and gzip header: '/api/v1/push' gives 400 invalid gzip body (route matched), '//api/v1/push' gives 405 with UI on and 404 with UI off. Test files deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Normalize server.url in validate() (strings.TrimRight of /) and again in the Pusher constructor. Treat a 404 from the push endpoint as a configuration error that flips health to a visible failed state rather than a silent drop.

**Fix notes:** Normalise server.url with strings.TrimRight(url, "/") in validate() (config.go:183-188). That also covers PGLENS_SERVER_URL, because the env override is applied before validate. Also normalise in NewPusher. Treat a 404 or 405 from the push endpoint as a visible configuration failure that changes health, not a silent drop.

### AR-06 — Target unreachable at startup for over 60s means checks are never scheduled (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:148`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** waitForTarget gives up after 60s and logs scheduling checks anyway (run.go:588-600). addScheduleEntries then runs exactly once (run.go:148), while role, server version, extensions and database discovery are still unknown. Gating via check.Requirements.Supports rejects version 0, and replication_streaming requires role primary. Database-scoped checks depend on Discover, which also failed at startup. None of these is ever scheduled again for that run.

**Failure scenario:** A database starts a minute late, or the network is flaky at boot. The agent runs indefinitely with only the basic checks for that target, silently. Operators see a partial dataset with no error.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reproduced: a target started about 10 minutes after the agent never got replication_streaming, io (PG16+), stat_statements, table_stats, bloat_estimate or index_stats. A control target that was up from the start got them all. Skip results are lost because flushEnvelope drops the batch for an unreachable target (run.go:468-472). Code: run.go:148, 588-600, 641-695.
```

**Verification reasoning:** run.go:141 calls waitForTarget, which gives up after 60s (run.go:588-600). run.go:148 then calls addScheduleEntries once. That function reads Role, PGVersion, PermTier and LocateStatements once and gates through Requirements.Supports (check.go:34-66). The scheduler's AddEntry panics after Start (scheduler.go:125-126), and there is only one call site, so no re-scheduling path exists. Consequences confirmed: role-gated (replication_streaming, replication_receiver), version-gated (io, PG16+) and extension-gated (stat_statements) checks are skipped with a reason. Database-scoped checks (bloat_estimate, index_stats, table_stats) get no entry and no skip result, because Discover failed and the database loop is empty. Nuance: reportScheduled (run.go:627-637) later labels those databases skip_reason 'discovered_after_start', which misattributes the cause. The skip results from addScheduleEntries are lost when the target is unreachable at the first flush (run.go:468-472 continue). Instance checks without role or version gates (activity, locks, wal and so on) are scheduled normally, so 'silently' applies to the gated ones. Control: with a live PG19 primary, io, replication_streaming, table_stats, bloat_estimate and index_stats are scheduled.

**Repro:**

```text
Temp test cmd/pglens-agent/zz_review_test.go (TestZZReviewAR06LateTarget): static Supports() table at role unknown, version 0. Then, for a down target (127.0.0.1:1) with the 60s waitForTarget and addScheduleEntries, versus a live target. Command: AR01_DSN='postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:32787/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test ./cmd/pglens-agent -run TestZZReviewAR06LateTarget -v (about 60s). Output: 'AR-06 target=down PGVersion=0 Role=unknown monitoredDBs=0' with io and replication_streaming SKIPPED and bloat_estimate, index_stats and table_stats NOT SCHEDULED. 'AR-06 target=live PGVersion=190000 Role=primary monitoredDBs=1' with io, replication_streaming, table_stats, bloat_estimate and index_stats scheduled. Note: a first live control run without PGLENS_IDENTITY_PATH gave PGVersion=0, which was an invalid control caused by the identity store. I fixed it by setting the identity path in the test and re-ran. Only the valid run is reported.
```

**Suggested fix:** Re-run addScheduleEntries for a target when it first becomes ready (role, version and discovery known), or schedule entries lazily and gate each tick on Supports. Retry Discover on every reconcile pass instead of only at startup. Surface a per-target status for missing check coverage.

**Fix notes:** Pitfall: Scheduler has no add-after-Start API (scheduler.go:125-126 panics), so the fix needs either per-tick gating on Supports and a Discover refresh in runEntry or scrapeEntry, or a reconcile pass that adds entries to a fresh scheduler. Retry Discover on every reconcile pass, not only at startup. The 'discovered_after_start' label in reportScheduled is misleading for the down-at-startup case and should be distinguished from the real cause.

### AR-07 — DSN with host in query string (or unix socket) makes identity fingerprinting fail (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `internal/identity/fingerprint.go:33`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Fingerprint parses the DSN and returns fingerprint: missing host when u.Host is empty (fingerprint.go:33). That happens for postgres://user:<redacted>@/db?host=127.0.0.1&port=5432 and for unix socket forms such as postgres:///db?host=/var/run/postgresql. TargetIsLocal (config.go:104) already reads the host query parameter, so the code is inconsistent with itself. The fingerprint failure feeds localIdentity (conn.go:575-589), so identity is never initialised.

**Failure scenario:** An operator configures a socket or host-in-query DSN. Every envelope carries a zero instance id, zero cluster id, manual id source and unknown role. The server cannot correlate instances, and cluster_id_changed logic misbehaves. The agent reports ok throughout.

**Evidence:**

```text
Observed error text: fingerprint DSN: fingerprint: missing host. Code: fingerprint.go:21-44, conn.go:575-589, config.go:104. Envelope consequences (role unknown, pg_version 0, cluster_id_source manual, zero instance and cluster id) follow from the identity path (conn.go:620-629) but were only confirmed statically, not via a captured envelope.
```

**Verification reasoning:** fingerprint.go:32-34 returns 'missing host' whenever u.Host is empty. Host-in-query and unix-socket DSNs are valid for pgx (pgx_host 127.0.0.1 and /var/run/postgresql) and are treated as local by TargetIsLocal (config.go:102-104, which reads the host query parameter). So the code is internally inconsistent. The failure cascades: conn.go:461-462 localIdentity() fails, so ensureCache returns before publishing the cache. PGVersion is 0, Role unknown, PermTier T0, ClusterIDSource manual, InstanceID zero, and AgentID nil (conn.go:557-563). A nil AgentID makes Dispatcher.Run return at once (command.go:103-106), so commands are silently disabled. Reproduced against a live server reached through a host-in-query DSN. ensureCache has no latch, so it fails again on every call.

**Repro:**

```text
Temp test internal/agent/zz_review_agent_test.go (TestZZReviewAR07HostInQueryDSN) with AR07_DSN='postgres://postgres:<redacted>@/postgres?host=127.0.0.1&port=32787&sslmode=disable' against the local PG19 container. Command: go test ./internal/agent -run TestZZReviewAR07HostInQueryDSN -v. Output: the control DSN fingerprints fine. Host-in-query and socket DSNs give 'fingerprint_err=fingerprint: missing host' while pgx parses them (pgx_host 127.0.0.1 and /var/run/postgresql). Manager output: 'PGVersion=0 Role=unknown PermTier=T0 ClusterID=0 ClusterIDSource=manual', then 'InstanceID=00000000-... AgentID=00000000-... AgentID-is-Nil=true'. Test file deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Make Fingerprint use the effective host from the query parameter when u.Host is empty, and handle unix sockets as a stable identity string. Reuse the same host resolution as TargetIsLocal. Add unit tests for both DSN shapes.

**Fix notes:** Fall back to the host query parameter (or the socket directory) only when u.Host is empty, and reuse TargetIsLocal's resolution. Keep the canonical form unchanged for DSNs that already have a host, or instance IDs will re-mint on upgrade. Add unit tests for both shapes in internal/identity, and an integration test through NewManager.

### AR-08 — Duplicate target names silently merge results across instances (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:256`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** validate() does not reject duplicate target names. The run loop keys the pending map by target name (run.go:120, 169, 256, 678), and results are attributed by Entry.TargetName. Two targets with the same name therefore share one bucket, and each instance in the envelope carries results from the other.

**Failure scenario:** A copy-pasted config with a repeated target name stores wrong data for both instances. The server has no way to detect that the values belong to different servers, so dashboards show one server's numbers under another's name.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reproduced: two targets both named dup (PG19 and PG18). Both instances in the same envelope carry identical activity, locks and replication_streaming data, and each shows the other's pg_version. Code: config.go validate (no uniqueness check), run.go:120, 256.
```

**Verification reasoning:** validate() in internal/agent/config.go (lines 265-286) never checks target-name uniqueness, so LoadConfig accepts two targets both named dup. Manager.Database() returns the target name (conn.go:739-741). pending is keyed by res.Entry.TargetName (run.go:256) and each manager reads batch[mgr.Database()] (run.go:427), so both managers receive the same results slice. End-to-end with the real agent binary, targets dup->PG17.11 and dup->PG15.19, ash disabled: envelope 000001.json has two instances with identical result lists (host twice, plus the io skip 'requires PG >= 16.0, got 15.19' appearing on the PG17 instance). Per-instance pg_version is correct (170011 / 150019), so the reviewer's claim that each instance shows the other's pg_version is NOT reproduced; the mixing is in results. The breaker is also shared, because AddEntryWithInterval keys breakers by target.Database() (scheduler.go:133). No guard found.

**Repro:**

```text
Unit: a YAML config with two targets named dup (DSN ports 1 and 2) returns a nil error from LoadConfig. E2E: agent run with two same-named targets against local postgres:17.11-alpine (127.0.0.1:32790) and postgres:15.19-alpine (127.0.0.1:32781), checks.ash.enabled=false, fake receiver on 127.0.0.1:19189. Envelope 000001.json: both instances carry the same results (host x2, io skip with 'got 15.19' on the PG17 instance).
```

**Suggested fix:** Reject duplicate target names in validate() with an error naming both entries. Key pending and envelope instances by a stable target id rather than the display name, or enforce uniqueness at the config layer.

**Fix notes:** (none recorded)

### AR-09 — Health reports ok while the server is unreachable (CONFIRMED, agent-runtime)

**Location:** `internal/agent/pusher.go:467`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Health state changes only when an HTTP response arrives. doRequest returns the network error directly (pusher.go:368-369) without touching the state that HealthzHandler (pusher.go:467-495) reads. Connection refused, timeouts and DNS failure therefore leave state ok and last_error empty, while the disk buffer keeps growing.

**Failure scenario:** The pglens server is down or unreachable for hours. Container healthchecks stay green, nothing is delivered, and the disk buffer grows until it fills. Operators get no alert.

**Evidence:**

```text
Reproduced: server URL pointing at a closed port for 30s. healthz returned HTTP 200 with state ok, last_error empty, dropped 0, and the buffer grew to 12K. The docker HEALTHCHECK exited 0. Code: pusher.go:365-374 and 467-495.
```

**Verification reasoning:** pusher.go:250-255 treats a network error as transient and does 'continue' without touching p.health or p.lastError. HealthzHandler (pusher.go:467-495) only returns 503 for incompatible/revoked/unauthorized. The docker healthcheck (main.go:58-75) passes on any HTTP response. No guard in the agent. Server-side staleness and agent_self alerts require the server to be reachable, so they cannot cover this scenario (the server is the thing that is down). Severity high because the health state and HTTP code report ok while nothing is delivered and the disk buffer grows.

**Repro:**

```text
Go test in internal/agent: NewPusher pointed at a closed loopback port, Queue one envelope, Push with a 4s context. Output: HealthState=ok, LastError='', LastSuccessfulPush=nil; HealthzHandler returns HTTP 200 with body {"state":"ok","last_successful_push":null,"last_error":"",...}.
```

**Suggested fix:** Track the time of the last successful push and the last network error. Report degraded or failed when no successful push has happened within a threshold, and set last_error on network failures.

**Fix notes:** Set p.lastError and a last-network-error timestamp in the doRequest error path (pusher.go:250-255). Degrade state when no successful push has happened within a threshold, using the existing lastSuccessfulPush field (pusher.go:261-262, exposed in the body but not used for state). Side effect to consider: pushOne retries network errors without a bound (pusher.go:228-255), and Push is called synchronously in the 1s goroutine (run.go:284) before the clock-skew and revocation checks (run.go:289-305). Those checks therefore do not run while the server is unreachable. UNLISTED SEPARATE ISSUE found while verifying, not one of the seven findings: agent shutdown on SIGTERM hangs forever when ASH is enabled (default). run.go:333-335 calls mgr.Close(), which calls pgxpool Close (conn.go:374-381) and waits for acquired connections. The ASH dedicated connection (DedicatedConn, conn.go:141-151; released only by the stop closure in ash.go:95-101) is released only by the deferred ashStops (run.go:184-188), which runs after mgr.Close(). SIGQUIT goroutine dump: main blocked in pgxpool.(*Pool).Close via run.go:334. Control: with checks.ash.enabled=false the same agent exits with code 0 within 20s. Suggested severity: critical per the hang rubric. Fix by releasing ASH before mgr.Close() (or calling stop before Close).
