### WU-14 — Query detail drops the statement database for EXPLAIN and plan history (CONFIRMED, web-ui)

**Location:** `web/src/routes/pages.tsx:61`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The list row carries datname, but queryPath() builds /instances/:id/queries/:queryid without it. QueryDetailPage renders ExplainPanel and PlanHistory without datname, and without the normalized flag from the statement. The EXPLAIN command is sent without datname, so the agent runs it in the target DSN's own database (openapi CommandArgs.datname description). Plan history is not filtered by database, so plans for the same queryid in different databases are shown together.

**Failure scenario:** A query listed under app_db is opened from the list. The EXPLAIN runs in the DSN database, where the referenced tables may not exist (error) or resolve to other objects (wrong plan). The plan history mixes entries from other databases.

**Evidence:**

```text
routes/pages.tsx:61-66 '<ExplainPanel ... instanceId={instanceId} queryid={queryid} />' and '<PlanHistory instanceId={instanceId} queryid={queryid} />'. QueryListPage.tsx:64-66 queryPath (no db). QueryListPage.tsx:86 Link to queryPath. ExplainPanel.tsx:152-160 args omit datname when undefined. api/openapi.yaml CommandArgs description: 'datname is the database the command runs in; without it, the target DSN's own database.'
```

**Verification reasoning:** EXPLAIN half (the high-severity part): routes/pages.tsx:61-66 passes instanceId and queryid to ExplainPanel and PlanHistory, with no datname and no normalized. QueryListPage.tsx:64-66 (queryPath) and :86 drop the database from the link. Server: commands.go enqueue (lines 138-196) stores the args exactly as sent, and command/types.go Validate and gate.go do not require datname for explain, so the server never fills it in. Agent: exec_explain.go:32 calls ConnFor with an empty datname, so it runs in the DSN's own database. lookupStatement (lines 222-226) filters pg_stat_statements by dbid = current_database(), so a queryid recorded under another database returns ErrNoRows and is rejected with 'queryid N is unknown on this instance' (lines 38-41). This applies to both plan-only and ANALYZE, and the detail page is the only EXPLAIN entry point, so the feature is broken for every statement outside the DSN database. Plan-history half (not a current defect from the UI): persistCommandArtifact stores Datname: args.Datname (commands.go:450). UI-initiated plans therefore get '' and cannot mix databases today. Mixing needs plans requested with a datname by another client, so it is latent until datname is sent. Normalized half (unsupported): the Statement schema in openapi has no normalized field, no UI data source sets it, and no caller passes normalized to ExplainPanel. The flag the finding wants does not exist.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary vitest file wu-verify-a.test.tsx, cases WU-14. (1) List: a statement with datname app_db renders the link with href /instances/<id>/queries/123, with no db. (2) Detail page: clicking 'Run plan only' sends POST /api/v1/instances/<id>/commands with body {kind:'explain', args:{analyze:false, queryid:'123'}}. The plan history request is GET /api/v1/plans?queryid=123&instance_id=<id>&limit=20, with no datname. Server and agent path verified by reading commands.go, command/types.go, command/gate.go, store path commands.go:450, and exec_explain.go lines 32, 38-41 and 222-226.
```

**Suggested fix:** Carry db in the list link (for example ?db=), read it on the detail route, and pass datname and normalized to ExplainPanel and PlanHistory.

**Fix notes:** Carry db in the list link (for example ?db=<datname>), read it on the detail route, and pass datname to ExplainPanel and PlanHistory. Derive normalized from the query text (the placeholder regex \$[0-9]+, as the agent does), or add it to the API. Pitfalls: (a) historical plans are stored with datname '' (they came from the DSN database), so filtering the detail page by the DSN database name would hide them. Treat '' as the DSN database. (b) QueryListPage does not display the row's datname, so users cannot see which database a row belongs to except through the db filter. Consider a column.

### WU-33 — parseLargeIntStrings is defined and tested but never applied (CONFIRMED, web-ui)

**Location:** `web/src/api/client.ts:83`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The int64-preserving parser is exported but no production code calls it; only api/client.test.ts uses it. Any int64 field that arrives as a JSON number above 2^53 is silently rounded. The contract currently makes queryid a string, so there is no present data loss, but the safety net is dead.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A future endpoint returns an int64 id as a number; the UI renders a rounded id and an EXPLAIN or plan lookup targets the wrong query.

**Correction (from verification):** The premise 'no present data loss' is REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
api/client.ts:83 'export function parseLargeIntStrings(raw: string): unknown'. Only reference outside the definition is api/client.test.ts:3 and :94-112.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The dead-code part is confirmed: parseLargeIntStrings (client.ts:83) is referenced only by client.test.ts. The premise 'no present data loss' is REFUTED. The command-audit path carries queryid as a JSON number: commands.go:163 json.Marshal(command.Args) stores it as a number (no MarshalJSON in internal/command/types.go), and command_audit.args is jsonb. api_audit.go:71 decodes args into map[string]any (float64) and re-encodes it, so the audit API returns a rounded queryid. CommandAudit.tsx:150 displays args JSON in the Settings audit table. Real pg_stat_statements queryids are signed 64-bit hashes, so almost all exceed 2^53 and nearly every explain audit row shows a wrong id. Root cause is server-side, outside web-ui scope. Severity raised from low to high (wrong data shown).

**Repro:**

```text
Go mirror of command.Args tags plus the api_audit.go decode path (scratch program, deleted): sent queryid 1234567890123456789 -> stored {"queryid":1234567890123456789} -> audit API {"queryid":1234567890123456800}; 9007199254740993 -> 9007199254740992. Static: git grep parseLargeIntStrings -- web (only client.ts:83 and client.test.ts).
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the parser in the fetch wrapper for responses, or delete it.

**Fix notes:** Fix at the source too: in api_audit.go decode with json.Decoder.UseNumber() (or keep args as json.RawMessage) so existing jsonb rows are not rounded; make command.Args encode queryid as a decimal string so new rows store a string. Web: openapi-fetch parses bodies with response.json(), so applying parseLargeIntStrings needs a fetch wrapper that reads text first; the regex only rewrites keys named queryid with 16+ digits. Note: UI-LOCK-036 and CommandAudit tests may need updating if the wire shape changes.

Status: open

### DR-02 — Shipped example monitors the storage cluster as its superuser (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/agent.example.yaml:25`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** deploy/docker-compose.yml creates the monitored Postgres with POSTGRES_USER=pglens, which is a superuser, and points the agent at it with the DSN postgres://pglens:<redacted>@timescaledb:5432/pglens?sslmode=disable. monitoring_user.sql is never applied in this stack. The agent's read-only guard is a client-side SET default_transaction_read_only = on (internal/agent/conn.go L78), which a superuser can SET off. The opt-in cancel, terminate and EXPLAIN ANALYZE paths therefore run with full privileges.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The example is used as-is or copied to a real environment. The agent connects as superuser. Any bug or misconfiguration in pglens, or a compromise of the agent host, can read, write or drop any data in the cluster, which violates the rule that every monitoring role is read-only.

**Correction (from verification):** The sub-claim that the opt-in cancel, terminate and EXPLAIN ANALYZE paths run with full privileges is REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
deploy/agent.example.yaml L25 DSN; deploy/docker-compose.yml L9 POSTGRES_USER: ${PGLENS_DB_USER:-pglens}, L10 POSTGRES_PASSWORD default pglens, L36 PGLENS_DSN default. Verified with timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17 and POSTGRES_USER=pglens: rolsuper=t and rolbypassrls=t for pglens.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The core claim holds: postgres:17 with POSTGRES_USER=pglens makes pglens a superuser with BYPASSRLS, deploy/docker-compose.yml never applies monitoring_user.sql, and the example DSN in agent.example.yaml uses this role. Nothing in internal/agent or cmd/pglens-agent refuses a superuser. The sub-claim that the opt-in cancel, terminate and EXPLAIN ANALYZE paths run with full privileges is REFUTED. Command gating in internal/command/gate.go Allowed() uses g.Tier, which comes from direct pg_auth_members membership. The superuser reports T0, so those commands are rejected with 'permission tier T1/T2 is required'. Severity is high rather than critical because the shipped file is an example that says 'Replace for production', and the command-level gates still hold.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-dr-7f3a-17pl (postgres:17.11-alpine, POSTGRES_USER=pglens, POSTGRES_DB=pglens). Before any script run: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname='pglens' gives t, t. The agent probe as pglens gives agent_probe_t1=f, agent_probe_t2=f (T0). Code reading: internal/command/gate.go Allowed() rejects KindExplain below TierExplain and KindCancel/KindTerminate below TierSignal. Searching the deploy and compose files for monitoring_user shows no reference in deploy/docker-compose.yml, only test/compose/topo-*.yml.
```

**Suggested fix:** Give the example a dedicated non-superuser monitoring role, created by deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql in an init script, and a separate storage role. Remove the superuser DSN from agent.example.yaml. Make the agent refuse to start when the connected role has rolsuper=true unless an explicit override is set.

**Fix notes:** Any init script that applies monitoring_user.sql to the example cluster would collide with the storage role of the same name (see DR-03), so give the example a distinct monitoring role such as pglens_monitor, or a separate cluster. The product gap is real: add a rolsuper check in the agent (no check exists today) and refuse or warn unless an explicit override is set. The tier gates do not protect against a superuser DSN, so keep this as a credential-exposure fix, not a command-gate fix.

Status: open

### DR-03 — Running the monitoring script on the storage cluster makes the storage role read-only and time-limited (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:78`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The script applies ALTER ROLE pglens SET default_transaction_read_only=on, statement_timeout=15s, lock_timeout=1s and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s to whatever role is named pglens. When the pglens server's storage database on the same cluster uses the role pglens (the timescaledb example), the storage role loses write ability and gets short timeouts. The server's writes then fail. Only a header comment (L9-12) warns about this, and nothing enforces it.

**Failure scenario:** An operator follows README quick start step 1 against the cluster that hosts pglens storage, as the example stack does. Storage writes through the pglens role fail with read-only errors, and long migrations or ingest transactions are cancelled by the 15 s statement timeout. The server loses ingestion.

**Evidence:**

```text
monitoring_user.sql L9-12 header comment, L78-88 settings. Verified with timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17 and POSTGRES_USER=pglens: after running the script with dbname=pglens as that role, setconfig became default_transaction_read_only=on, statement_timeout=15s, lock_timeout=1s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s, and a CREATE TABLE in a new session failed with 'cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction'. Before the script, create and drop table succeeded.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced exactly. When the script runs against the same cluster and database where pglens is the storage role, ALTER ROLE pglens SET default_transaction_read_only=on, statement_timeout=15s and the other session limits apply to that storage role. A fresh storage session then cannot CREATE TABLE. Nothing enforces the refusal; only the SQL header warns (L9-12). Severity stays high: the README quick start tells the operator to run the script on each target instance, and the example's target is the storage cluster, so the broken-storage path is reachable through documented steps.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-dr-7f3a-17pl (postgres:17.11-alpine, POSTGRES_USER=pglens, POSTGRES_DB=pglens). As pglens, CREATE TABLE public.storage_probe / DROP succeed. Run psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v pglens_password=pglens -v dbname=pglens -f /tmp/monitoring_user.sql as pglens gives EXIT=0. In a new session as pglens: SHOW default_transaction_read_only gives on; SHOW statement_timeout gives 15s; CREATE TABLE public.storage_probe_after (x int) gives ERROR: cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction.
```

**Suggested fix:** Refuse to run when the target role is a superuser, when it owns objects in its own database (pg_shdepend deptype 'o'), or when dbname is the storage database. Alternatively require a distinct monitoring role name such as pglens_monitor and document it. Add a test for the refusal.

**Fix notes:** The script cannot know which database is the storage database, so an in-script check has to be heuristic. An ownership check (pg_shdepend deptype 'o' rows for pglens in dbname) would catch the storage case because the storage role owns the tables. Refusing superuser targets would also catch the example. Recovery for an affected cluster is ALTER ROLE pglens RESET default_transaction_read_only, RESET statement_timeout, RESET lock_timeout and RESET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, plus the IN DATABASE rows.

Status: open

### DR-06 — Tier flags are tested for definedness, so tier1=0 or false grants T1, and tier2 works without tier1 (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:52`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** \if :{?tier1} tests whether the variable is defined, not its value. -v tier1=0 and -v tier1=false still grant pg_read_all_data and pg_read_all_stats, and -v tier2=0 still grants pg_signal_backend. -v tier2=1 without tier1 grants pg_signal_backend without pg_read_all_data, and the agent then classifies the role as T2. README describes T2 as T1 plus signal.

**Failure scenario:** An operator passes -v tier1=0 meaning no T1 and gets read access to all table data in the monitored cluster. Another operator passes only tier2=1 and gets a signal-capable role with no read access, which the agent reports as T2.

**Evidence:**

```text
monitoring_user.sql L52-55 (tier1 block) and L60-62 (tier2 block). Verified on 15 to 19: tier1=0, tier1=false and tier2=0 each granted the flagged role. tier2=1 alone granted pg_signal_backend and the agent reported T2 (internal/agent/conn.go L503 and cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L257-277 check direct membership). README L168-170 documents the tiers.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Confirmed. In psql, \if :{?tier1} is true whenever the variable is defined, whatever its value, so -v tier1=0 and -v tier2=0 each grant their roles. tier2=1 without tier1 grants pg_signal_backend and no pg_read_all_data, and the agent's direct-membership probe then reports signal, which per code is T2. The script header (L7) and README (L168-170) say tier2 needs tier1, and nothing enforces it. Only the privilege grant is affected, not data, so high rather than critical.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-dr-7f3a-16 (postgres:16.15-alpine). Run with -v pglens_password=pw16 -v dbname=postgres -v tier1=0 -v tier2=0 gives EXIT=0. SELECT the granted roles for pglens: pg_monitor, pg_read_all_data, pg_read_all_stats, pg_signal_backend. Then DROP OWNED BY pglens and DROP ROLE pglens. Run with -v tier2=1 only gives EXIT=0. Granted roles are then pg_monitor and pg_signal_backend. The agent's direct probes give has_read_all_data_direct=f and has_signal_direct=t. Code reading: internal/agent/conn.go queryCapabilities sets TierSignal regardless of TierExplain, and cmd/pglens-agent/main.go determinePermTier does the same.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compare the value, not the definedness (for example select :'tier1' = '1' as t1 \gset and branch on it, or reject any value other than 1). Require tier1=1 when tier2=1, and fail the run with a non-zero exit otherwise. Keep the manual downgrade REVOKE steps documented.

**Fix notes:** Compare values, not definedness. Guard with \if :{?tier1} first, because :'tier1' stays unsubstituted when the variable is undefined. Then SELECT (:'tier1' = '1') AS t1, (:'tier2' = '1') AS t2 \gset and branch on :t1 and :t2. Reject tier2 without tier1 with \quit non-zero. Keep the downgrade REVOKE steps documented in deploy/sql/README.md.

Status: open

### DR-08 — PostgreSQL 19 is absent from the test matrix, and unknown majors silently fall back to 15 and 18 (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `test/pgtest/versions.go:41`

**Category:** pg-version · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The request was to support PostgreSQL 19 (release candidate). The images map has only 15 to 18. Versions() drops unknown majors and returns [15, 18] when nothing matches, so PGLENS_PG_VERSIONS=19 silently runs 15 and 18 and reports success. The CI integration matrix and the Makefile loop also stop at 18, and the docs say 15 to 18.

**Failure scenario:** A release claims PG19 support. The PG19 integration run never happens, PGLENS_PG_VERSIONS=19 exercises 15 and 18 and passes, and a PG19-only regression ships unnoticed.

**Evidence:**

```text
versions.go L11-16 images map (15, 16, 17, 18 only); L21-41 Versions() drops unknown majors; L41 return []int{15, 18}. ci.yml L221 pg: ["15", "16", "17", "18"]. Makefile L134 for pg in 15 16 17 18. README L36 and L1732 state PostgreSQL 15 to 18. Verified that the role script runs on postgres:19rc1-alpine with grants identical to 18.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Confirmed by code reading and a local postgres:19rc1-alpine run. test/pgtest/versions.go L11-16 maps only 15-18, L33 silently drops unknown majors, and L41 falls back to []int{15, 18}, so PGLENS_PG_VERSIONS=19 runs 15 and 18 and reports success. Makefile L134 and .github/workflows/ci.yml L221 stop at 18, and README L36 and L1732 say 15-18. The finding understates the scope: internal/pgtype/version.go L25-27 Supported() is `major >= 15 && major < 19` (decision D11), and cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L176-180 prints NOT SUPPORTED for PG19. Supported() has no other non-test caller, so it is a label, not a gate. The role script and both fixtures run cleanly on 19rc1, so the gap is in the matrix and the label, not SQL incompatibility. High is kept because the user explicitly asked for PG19 support and the product labels it unsupported. Process note: the tokensave MCP refused (it serves branch main while the worktree is on another branch), so I used Read, awk and psql instead.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run postgres:19rc1-alpine; `psql -U postgres -d app -Atc "select p.oid::regprocedure from pg_proc p where proname='pg_logical_emit_message'"` lists 4-argument overloads (boolean,text,text,boolean) and (boolean,text,bytea,boolean). `cat deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql | psql -U postgres -d app -v pglens_password=secret -v dbname=app -v tier1=1 -v tier2=1 -f -` gives exit=0 and rolconfig {default_transaction_read_only=on,statement_timeout=15s,lock_timeout=1s,idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30s,application_name=pglens}. `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f test/fixtures/sql/00_extensions.sql` gives exit 0, and 01_schema.sql gives exit 0.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add 19: "postgres:19rc1-alpine" to images (move to a final 19.x image when GA). Make Versions() fail on an unknown major instead of falling back. Add 19 to the ci.yml matrix and the Makefile loop. Update README and deploy/sql docs to 15 to 19 once green.

**Fix notes:** Add postgres:19rc1-alpine to images in test/pgtest/versions.go (the image is present locally). Remove the silent fallback at L33 and L41 so an unknown major errors. Add 19 to Makefile L134 and ci.yml L221. Update README L36 and L1732 and deploy/sql docs. Also change Supported() in internal/pgtype/version.go L27 and the D11 comment at L24, and the agent check label at cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L176. Only the label reads it, so no runtime refusal needs to be undone.

### DR-13 — Example stacks publish a superuser database, a default API token and the agent healthz port on all interfaces (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/docker-compose.yml:9`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** deploy/compose/timescaledb.yml publishes "5432:5432" and deploy/docker-compose.yml publishes ${PGLENS_POSTGRES_PORT:-5432}:5432 without host_ip, which binds 0.0.0.0. The superuser password defaults to pglens and sslmode=disable is used. PGLENS_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN defaults to dev-token and is also the API and ingest bearer, published on port 8080. The agent healthz port 9187 is also published.

**Failure scenario:** A developer runs the quick start on a laptop on a shared network, or on a VM with a public address. An attacker logs in to 5432 as superuser with the default password, or calls the API with dev-token and reads or ingests data. Severity rises to critical on an internet-facing host.

**Evidence:**

```text
deploy/docker-compose.yml L9-12, L10 POSTGRES_PASSWORD default, L40 and L61 token and port, L88 healthz port. deploy/compose/timescaledb.yml L8-9. docker compose config shows the published port 5432 with no host_ip. internal/server/auth.go L27-35: the bootstrap token is the API and ingest bearer, compared in constant time.
```

**Verification reasoning:** `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config` lists the published ports 5432, 8080 and 9187 without a host_ip, which binds all interfaces. The defaults are at L8-10: POSTGRES_USER pglens is the cluster superuser, with password default pglens. The bootstrap token defaults to the literal dev-token at L40 and L79. The Go server no longer falls back silently (internal/server/config.go L33-38, L39-62 refuses an empty token), but the compose literal still supplies dev-token. The credential gate covers every route (internal/server/http.go L25, session.go L145-153), and Auth.Validate (internal/server/auth.go L17-35) is a constant-time bearer compare. The agent healthz (internal/agent/pusher.go L466-494) is unauthenticated JSON that includes last_error, so publishing 9187 also leaks state. Severity: high rather than critical. The compose file marks itself as a local example needing replacement (L39), and the product refuses an unset token. Exposure needs an operator to run it on a reachable host, but the default superuser password is still a serious security hole.

**Repro:**

```text
`docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml config` prints the three ports blocks with published values and no host_ip. Compose lines and code locations are as stated above. I did not start a container bound to 0.0.0.0, to avoid exposing a host port.
```

**Suggested fix:** Bind published ports to 127.0.0.1 (for example 127.0.0.1:5432:5432). Require PGLENS_DB_PASSWORD and PGLENS_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN with compose's ${VAR:?must be set} syntax instead of defaults. Do not use a superuser for the monitored database (DR-02). Keep healthz on localhost.

**Fix notes:** Bind 127.0.0.1 host IPs for 5432, 8080 and 9187 (deploy/docker-compose.yml L12, L61, L88; deploy/compose/timescaledb.yml L8-9 also publishes 5432). Replace the defaults with ${VAR:?must be set} for POSTGRES_PASSWORD (L10) and PGLENS_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN (L40, L79). Keep the superuser out of the monitored role (DR-02). Keep healthz on loopback.

### RO-02 — Plain EXPLAIN, which is default-on, executes IMMUTABLE user functions during planning (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:69`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Plain EXPLAIN is not gated by allow_explain_analyze. It runs for any T1 target with commands enabled, which is the default. The planner constant-folds IMMUTABLE functions with constant arguments, so a function body executes under the monitor identity without ANALYZE.

**Failure scenario:** A function is declared IMMUTABLE but has a side effect, which is common when volatility is not checked. A statement that calls it appears in pg_stat_statements. A server-issued plain EXPLAIN for that queryid runs the function under the monitor role with no opt-in.

**Evidence:**

```text
exec_explain.go:69 `options := "FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS"`; line 101 `EXPLAIN (%s) %s`. gate.go:10-17 gates only `a.Analyze`. Verified on PG17 and PG19: `CREATE FUNCTION public.lock_on_plan() RETURNS int IMMUTABLE LANGUAGE sql AS $$SELECT pg_advisory_lock(777)::int$$`, then `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, COSTS) SELECT public.lock_on_plan()` inside BEGIN READ ONLY / ROLLBACK leaves advisory lock 777 held. Negative control: the VOLATILE variant is not run by plain EXPLAIN but is run by EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Plain EXPLAIN (Analyze=false, default-on at T1) runs a no-argument IMMUTABLE SQL function at plan time. Reproduced via Execute(Analyze=false): after the call, pg_locks shows advisory lock 777 granted to the monitor backend. Control: a VOLATILE function with the same body does not take its lock under plain EXPLAIN (only 777 present) but does under ANALYZE (778 taken). The effect is session state only: the READ ONLY transaction still blocks data writes, so the impact is locks and other non-data side effects, not data changes (writes were not directly tested). Preconditions: a function mis-declared IMMUTABLE with side effects, created by a role with CREATE in the monitored database. The statement must be recorded constant-free in pg_stat_statements. Default-on exposure with a session-level effect, so high rather than critical. No guard elsewhere: gate.go gates only Analyze. docs do not mention planner folding.

**Repro:**

```text
Same containers and roles as RO-01. As app: CREATE FUNCTION public.lock_on_plan() RETURNS void IMMUTABLE LANGUAGE sql AS $$SELECT pg_advisory_lock(777)$$ and the VOLATILE twin lock_volatile (778); plant SELECT public.lock_on_plan() and SELECT public.lock_volatile() in short-lived sessions. Then Execute(Analyze=false) on the IMMUTABLE queryid. PG17 and PG19rc1 output: 'plain EXPLAIN of IMMUTABLE-calling statement: err=<nil>' then 'locks after plain EXPLAIN (immutable): [pid=122 usename=monitor classid=0 objid=777 granted=true]'. Volatile control: plain EXPLAIN leaves only 777; Analyze adds 778. Extra check, psql as monitor: BEGIN READ ONLY; EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN, FORMAT JSON) SELECT public.lock_on_plan(); ROLLBACK; then pg_locks shows 777 granted (PG17).
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the RO-01 function policy to plain EXPLAIN as well, since folding happens at plan time without ANALYZE. Run it in the dedicated read role on a dedicated connection. GENERIC_PLAN (PG16+) avoids folding for parameterised statements, but I did not verify whether it still folds no-argument IMMUTABLE calls.

**Fix notes:** Plain EXPLAIN needs the same function-volatility policy as ANALYZE, because folding happens at plan time. GENERIC_PLAN does not prevent folding for no-argument calls (verified: lock 777 held after GENERIC_PLAN explain on PG17), so the reviewer's mitigation does not work for these statements. Only parameterised calls escape folding.

Status: open

### RO-03 — Session state left by on-demand commands survives ROLLBACK and returns to the pool (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_explain.go:36`

**Category:** leak · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The command path borrows a pooled connection, runs work in a READ ONLY transaction, rolls back and releases the connection. ROLLBACK reverts transactional state only. Session-level effects, such as advisory locks, LISTEN, dblink connections, temp objects and session SETs, persist into the next check or ASH sample that receives that connection.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** An ANALYZE, or plain EXPLAIN over a folded IMMUTABLE function (RO-02), takes advisory locks. The lock is held for as long as that pooled connection lives, and application code waiting on the same advisory lock blocks in the meantime.

**Correction (from verification):** Minor correction: NewManager does not set MaxConnIdleTime on the shared pool, so pgxpool's default applies there.

**Evidence:**

```text
exec_explain.go:36 `defer conn.Release()`; line 92 `defer func() { _, _ = conn.Exec(ctx, "ROLLBACK") }()`. Verified on PG17 and PG19: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) SELECT pg_advisory_lock(oid::bigint) FROM pg_database` and `pg_try_advisory_lock(999)` inside READ ONLY transactions. After ROLLBACK, pg_locks still lists them (count 1). Idle pooled connections are recycled only after IdleTimeout (5 minutes by default), and a busy one is reused without reset.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: exec_explain.go:36 defers conn.Release() and line 92 defers only ROLLBACK. conn.go has no DISCARD ALL, no AfterRelease reset, and no connection close, so session-level state persists on a pooled connection. Reproduced via Execute(Analyze=true) of a constant-free SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(oid::bigint) FROM pg_database WHERE datname=current_database(): after Execute returned and ROLLBACK ran, pg_locks still showed advisory objid=5 granted to the monitor backend. The next ForDatabase on that pool returned the same backend pid, which still held the lock. The lock was released only on mgr.Close(). Trigger: ANALYZE (opt-in) or RO-02. An application's own session-level advisory lock would also be left held once an operator ANALYZEs its query. Minor correction: NewManager does not set MaxConnIdleTime on the shared pool, so pgxpool's default applies there. The 5-minute IdleTimeout applies only to per-database pools.

**Repro:**

```text
Same containers. Plant as app: SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(oid::bigint) FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database(). Execute(Analyze=true) with monitor DSN. Output PG17 and PG19rc1: 'EXPLAIN ANALYZE of advisory-lock SELECT: err=<nil> resultBytes=1107' then 'locks after Execute returned (ROLLBACK already done): [pid=130 usename=monitor classid=0 objid=5 granted=true]' and 'locks after mgr.Close(): []'. Pool reuse check in the RO-02 test: 'next check reuses pooled backend pid=122; locks now: [... objid=777 granted=true ...]'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Use a dedicated connection for command execution and close it, either by hijacking it from the pool and calling Close or by closing the pooled connection. DISCARD ALL before Release clears advisory locks, GUCs and temp objects, but it does not close open dblink connections, so closing is preferred.

**Fix notes:** Release is not enough. Run command work on a dedicated, non-pooled connection that is closed afterwards (Hijack or Close), or close the pooled conn on command exit. DISCARD ALL clears advisory locks and GUCs but not open dblink connections. The shared-pool idle claim in the finding should read pgxpool default, not 5 minutes.

Status: open

### RO-05 — Target scheduling is decided once at startup, so a discovery failure disables database-scoped checks for the process lifetime (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:646`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** addScheduleEntries runs once per target. If mgr.Discover or LocateStatements fails at that moment, the database list is empty and no database-scoped entry is ever scheduled. The envelope path later marks those databases as discovered_after_start with no data.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The agent starts while the target is reachable, but Discover fails once (or LocateStatements times out after 10 seconds). table_stats, index_stats, bloat_estimate and stat_statements never run for that target until the agent restarts, while the server shows those databases as monitored.

**Correction (from verification):** Correction to the finding: the failure scenario says the server shows those databases as monitored.

**Evidence:**

```text
run.go:646-649 `dbs, err := mgr.Discover(ctx); if err != nil { fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "warning: discover databases for %s: %v\n", ...) }`; lines 653-654 `locateCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)` and `exts := map[string]bool{"pg_stat_statements": mgr.LocateStatements(locateCtx, dbs)}`; lines 656-661 build `scheduled` only from `db.Monitored`; lines 684-690 add database-scoped entries only for those. run.go:627-634 (reportScheduled) turns later-discovered databases into discovered_after_start.
```

**Verification reasoning:** run.go:646-661: addScheduleEntries calls mgr.Discover once; on error dbs is nil and scheduled is empty, so no database-scoped entry (table_stats, index_stats, bloat, stat_statements per DB) is ever added. Nothing re-runs it: the only call site is run.go:148, and scheduler.AddEntryWithInterval panics after Start (scheduler.go:125-127). Reproduced with a live primary and a cancelled context for the scheduling pass: the database-scoped set was 'map[] (len=0)' even though a live Discover returned 1 database. Correction to the finding: the failure scenario says the server shows those databases as monitored. That is wrong. flushEnvelope's reportScheduled (run.go:627-637) rewrites them to Monitored=false with SkipReason 'discovered_after_start'. The bug is still real: no checks run for the process lifetime. The same applies to LocateStatements failure, which drops stat_statements via the startup exts map.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in cmd/pglens-agent calling addScheduleEntries(sched, mgr, cancelledCtx, &agent.Config{}, &mu, pending) against the live PG17 monitor DSN. Output: 'warning: discover databases for ro05: get shared connection: context canceled'; 'live Discover: err=<nil> databases=1'; 'database-scoped scheduled set after one failed Discover: map[] (len=0)'. Test removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Retry discovery and LocateStatements with backoff, and reconcile the schedule when the database set or extension set changes. This needs a scheduler that accepts entries after Start (RO-06 needs the same change).

**Fix notes:** Retry Discover and LocateStatements with backoff, and reconcile when the database or extension set changes. This needs a scheduler that accepts entries after Start (AddEntry currently panics). Correct the failure scenario: the server sees skip_reason discovered_after_start.

### RO-06 — Role, version and tier are frozen at startup, so role-restricted checks never run after a failover (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:642`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** addScheduleEntries reads Role(), PGVersion(), PermTier() and the extension set once and uses them for the lifetime of the process. Checks restricted to a role (replication_streaming: primary; replication_receiver: standby) are either scheduled or skipped permanently. A standby that is promoted, or a target whose role changes, does not get the matching checks until restart.

**Failure scenario:** The agent starts against a standby. replication_streaming is skipped with 'role standby not allowed'. The standby is promoted to primary, and the envelope now reports role=primary, but no replication_streaming samples are ever collected (no sender lag) until the agent restarts. Failover is the scenario where that data matters most.

**Evidence:**

```text
run.go:575-579 comment: `addScheduleEntries below reads mgr.Role()/PGVersion()/PermTier()/HasExtension() exactly once, at startup, to decide which checks ever get scheduled for this target's entire lifetime`; run.go:642-644 `role := mgr.Role()`, `version := mgr.PGVersion()`, `tier := mgr.PermTier()`; run.go:676 `if ok, reason := req.Supports(role, version, tier, exts); !ok {` records a SkipReason and continues. replication_streaming.go:17-18 `Roles: []pgtype.Role{pgtype.RolePrimary}`; replication_receiver.go:17 `Roles: []pgtype.Role{pgtype.RoleStandby}`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The role, version, tier and extension gate is evaluated once in addScheduleEntries via req.Supports(role, version, tier, exts) (run.go:642-644, 676). Requirements.Supports (internal/check/check.go:34-66) checks Roles, PG bounds, PermTier and Extensions, so a skipped check is never revisited. replication_streaming.go:16-18 declares Roles primary, and its Scrape does not check role. RefreshRole (conn.go:677-693) refreshes the cached role each envelope, but nothing re-schedules, and AddEntry panics after Start. Live evidence of schedule-time gating: on the primary, the check CLI and agent both show replication_receiver 'disabled — role primary not allowed'. The promotion scenario was not run live (no standby); the verdict rests on the code path, which has no guard. Tier- and extension-gated checks are frozen the same way, and the RefreshCapabilities comment saying grants take effect on the next scrape is inaccurate for scheduling.

**Repro:**

```text
Live: pglens-agent check --dsn <primary monitor DSN> lists replication_receiver as 'disabled — role primary not allowed'. Code: run.go:642-644 and 676; check.go:34-47 role check; replication_streaming.go:16-18; scheduler.go:125-127 panic after Start; conn.go:677-693 RefreshRole updates only the cache.
```

**Suggested fix:** Schedule role-dependent checks for every role and gate them at Scrape time against the current role, or reconcile on role change. Both need the add-after-start support that the scheduler currently forbids.

**Fix notes:** Schedule role-dependent checks for every role and gate at Scrape time against the current role (or reconcile on role change). Both need add-after-start support. Also review the RefreshCapabilities comment about grants taking effect on the next scrape.

Status: open

### RO-07 — Shutdown flush races the push ticker on lastEdgeState, which is an unsynchronised map (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:563`

**Category:** race · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** flushEnvelope runs from the push-ticker goroutine and again from the shutdown path. Both call buildTopologyEdges, which writes lastEdgeState without a lock. Only pending is guarded by mu.

**Failure scenario:** SIGTERM arrives while the push ticker is inside flushEnvelope, which can block up to 5 seconds per target on network calls. Both goroutines write lastEdgeState, and the Go runtime aborts the agent with 'concurrent map writes' during its final flush, so the batch already taken from pending is lost.

**Evidence:**

```text
run.go:270 `flushEnvelope(ctx, managers, &mu, pending, lastEdgeState, ashEnabled, scheduledDBs, pusher)` inside the ticker goroutine; run.go:330 the same call on shutdown with shutdownCtx; run.go:563 `lastEdgeState[name] = state` inside buildTopologyEdges (called from flushEnvelope at run.go:473). The only lock in flushEnvelope is `mu` around pending (run.go:397-403).
```

**Verification reasoning:** The push ticker goroutine (run.go:264-273) is not joined before the shutdown flush (run.go:314-330), so two flushEnvelope calls can overlap at shutdown. buildTopologyEdges (run.go:535-573) writes lastEdgeState at line 563 with no lock. The only lock in flushEnvelope is mu around pending (run.go:397-403). Reproduced with -race: two goroutines calling buildTopologyEdges concurrently produce 'WARNING: DATA RACE' with writes at run.go:563 and reads/writes at run.go:539. Caveat: a flushEnvelope-level two-goroutine test did not trip the detector, because RefreshRole's cache.mu happens to order the flushes. The race is real and the Go memory model gives no guarantee. The practical crash window at shutdown is narrow, since the ticker's flush fails fast once ctx is cancelled, so the realistic likelihood is low. Severity follows the rubric's race entry.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in cmd/pglens-agent, ZZ_MON_DSN=postgres://monitor:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:55417/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -race ./cmd/pglens-agent/ -run TestZZ_RO07_Direct -count=1 -v. Output: 'WARNING: DATA RACE ... Read at ... buildTopologyEdges run.go:539 ... Previous write ... buildTopologyEdges run.go:563'. Test file removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Protect lastEdgeState with a mutex, or wait for the push goroutine to exit (WaitGroup or done channel) before the shutdown flush. Either one removes the race. Run the agent tests under -race to confirm.

**Fix notes:** Either guard lastEdgeState with a mutex, or join the push goroutine (done channel or WaitGroup) before the shutdown flushEnvelope. Verify with a test that calls buildTopologyEdges from two goroutines under -race, not only flushEnvelope, which the cache mutex can mask.

Status: open

### RO-08 — Unix-socket DSN without a host in the authority is rejected by Fingerprint, so the target is never reported (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/identity/fingerprint.go:32`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Fingerprint requires a non-empty URL host. Socket DSNs in the form postgres:///db?host=/var/run/postgresql or postgres://user@/db?host=... have an empty authority host, so localIdentity fails. InstanceID() then silently returns the zero UUID, and RefreshRole failure makes flushEnvelope omit the target every cycle.

**Failure scenario:** An agent running on the database host, configured with a local socket DSN (common), never reports that target. There is no clear error, only a warning on each push cycle, and the instance id for the target is the zero UUID in any path that does not check the error.

**Evidence:**

```text
fingerprint.go:32-34 `if u.Host == "" { return "", fmt.Errorf("fingerprint: missing host") }`. Offline reproduction using the function verbatim: `postgres:///app?host=/var/run/postgresql` -> err=fingerprint: missing host; `postgres://pglens@/app?host=/var/run/postgresql` -> err=fingerprint: missing host; `postgres://pglens@db.internal:5432/app` -> ok. conn.go:565-571 `InstanceID()` returns `pgtype.InstanceID{}` on error without logging. conn.go:580 calls `identity.Fingerprint(m.target.dsn)`. run.go:468-471 omits the target when RefreshRole fails.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Fingerprint rejects a URL DSN with an empty authority host (internal/identity/fingerprint.go:32-34), so postgres:///db?host=... fails. That is a documented, supported shape: config validation accepts the postgres:// prefix (internal/agent/config.go:262-272), TargetIsLocal treats the host query parameter as local (config.go:94-115), README.md:789 and docs/plans/002_plan-AnalysisBackend/phase_07.md:42 document Unix-socket DSNs, and internal/agent/host_test.go:12-14 pins TestHostLocal_InferredFromUnixSocketDSN. The finding's omission mechanism is wrong. RefreshRole (internal/agent/conn.go:677-693) never calls ensureCache or localIdentity, so it succeeds and the target IS pushed. What actually happens: ensureCache always fails (conn.go:461), so InstanceID() is the zero UUID (conn.go:565-571), ClusterID is 0 with source manual, PGVersion is 0, Role() stays unknown even after RefreshRole updated the cache (conn.go:654-663), PermTier stays T0, and extensions are never refreshed (RefreshCapabilities fails before queryCapabilities). At startup waitForTarget (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:588-600) waits the full 60s because PGVersion stays 0, and addScheduleEntries (run.go:641-695) skips io, replication_streaming and stat_statements for the process lifetime, where the host-form DSN skips only replication_receiver and stat_statements. The warning on every flush (run.go:436-437) makes it visible, so it is not silent. Dispatcher: run.go:206 registers each manager under InstanceID(), and command.go:90-91 overwrites by key, so two socket targets in one agent collapse to one binding. The dispatch lookup at command.go:171 then sends a command for sock-a to sock-b. Cross-agent collapse is inferred, not run: the server does not reject the zero instance_id on ingest, and inventory upserts with ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO UPDATE. Kept at high: the wrong identity and role are stored for every socket target, and a misrouted cancel or terminate needs allow_signal, which is opt-in.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in internal/agent calling the real NewManager, RefreshCapabilities, RefreshRole, InstanceID, ClusterID, PGVersion, Role, PermTier and check.All() with Requires().Supports(). Against postgres:19rc1-alpine (container pglens-review-ro-main, since removed), socket-form DSN postgres://postgres@/postgres?host=127.0.0.1&port=32789&sslmode=disable. Output: RefreshCapabilities err=fingerprint DSN: fingerprint: missing host; RefreshRole err=<nil>; InstanceID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000; ClusterID=0 ClusterIDSource=manual; PGVersion=0.0 Role=unknown PermTier=T0; skipped_names=[io replication_receiver replication_streaming stat_statements]. Host-form postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:32789/postgres?sslmode=disable: InstanceID=1909dec5-9411-4873-ade7-1be9691ba54a; ClusterID=7699670645724893224 system_identifier; PGVersion=19.0 Role=primary; skipped_names=[replication_receiver stat_statements]. Dispatcher repro, two socket-form managers passed to AddTarget(mX.InstanceID(), mX, true, true): instanceA=... equal=true; dispatcher targets map size=1; command for sock-a's instance resolves to sock-b? true. Command: RO_PORT=<port> go test ./internal/agent -run TestZZVerifyRO08 -v.
```

**Suggested fix:** When the URL host is empty, take the host from the host query parameter (or from pgconn.ParseConfig, which resolves libpq defaults), and keep dropping the password. Return an error instead of the zero InstanceID from InstanceID().

**Fix notes:** (1) TestFingerprint_Errors (internal/identity/fingerprint_test.go:88) pins postgres:///db as an error. That test must change deliberately, because postgres:///db?host=<socket> is valid and must map to a stable identity. (2) Derive the host the way endpoint() already does (pgxpool.ParseConfig, or the host query parameter, as TargetIsLocal does), and keep dropping the password. (3) Role() (conn.go:654) reads through ensureCache, so it ignores the role RefreshRole just stored. Fix that as well. (4) Never register uuid.Nil in the dispatcher (run.go:206, command.go:90). Also check waitForTarget (run.go:588) for a socket target.

Status: open

### RO-09 — A torn ENOSPC write makes every later record in the segment undeliverable (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/buffer/buffer.go:634`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Segment.Append writes the length, the CRC and the payload with three separate writes. If a write fails after the header is on disk, the torn bytes stay in the file, and fileSize is not advanced. Later records are appended after the garbage. The reader then either stops at the size guard, which returns io.EOF, or skips to a misaligned offset, so later records are never offered.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The volume fills while a record is being appended. That is the bounded-volume case the buffer exists to handle. Telemetry written after the torn write is not delivered until retention removes the segment, and it is then counted as dropped samples. Delivery stays stuck across restarts.

**Correction (from verification):** Corrections: the reader does not wedge across segments.

**Evidence:**

```text
buffer.go:655-660 `if _, err := s.file.Write(data); err != nil { return err }` followed by `s.fileSize += int64(len(lenBuf) + len(creBuf) + len(data))` only on success. buffer.go:716-718 `if size := s.fileSize; size > 0 && int64(length) > size-int64(offset)-8 { return nil, offset, io.EOF }`. Reproduced with a scratch harness that compiles buffer.go unchanged except for the clock import: Open, Append("rec-A"), write a torn record (header length=1000 plus 100 bytes) directly to the segment file, Append("rec-B"), Append("rec-C"), Close, Open, Next(). Result: delivers "rec-A", then io.EOF. rec-B and rec-C are never delivered and stay on disk until retention drops the segment, at which point they are counted as dropped.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Segment.Append (internal/agent/buffer/buffer.go:634-663) issues three separate writes. On failure it returns without truncating and without advancing fileSize, and nothing in Open (56-161) or openSegment (569-631) recovers a torn tail. ReadAt (692-752) returns io.EOF when the declared length runs past the end (lines 716, 722-737). Reproduced for the same segment: after a torn header (len=1000) plus 100 payload bytes, rec-B and rec-C are never delivered, in-process or after Close/reopen, with CorruptRecords=0. The loss is wider than the finding says: the active segment keeps taking appends until it reaches 8 MiB or segmentAgedOut fires at MaxAge/4 (buffer.go:440-442), which is about 90 minutes by default. Corrections: the reader does not wedge across segments. With a second segment present, rec-LAST and the big records in segment 1 are delivered, one push tick late. Only segment 0's records after the torn point are lost (rec-B and big-0..big-6). The loss is not counted: SamplesDropped stayed empty, because dropAckedSegments (buffer.go:449-452) calls removeOldestSegment with reason "" (470-494), which counts nothing. A separate defect: in Next() (227-291) the corrupt-record branch (267-271) uses continue inside the segment loop, so after a corrupt record in a non-last segment the reader reads segment i+1 at the corrupt record's offset and returns io.EOF once. Severity high, not critical: this is degraded agent telemetry under ENOSPC, silently discarded, which breaks the I-7 counting contract. It causes no hang and does not touch stored data.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary in-package tests in internal/agent/buffer. The torn write is simulated by writing an 8-byte header (length=1000, crc) plus 100 bytes directly through b.segments[last].file, so the segment's own fd is used. Same-segment case: Open(dir, Options{}); Append(rec-A); torn write; Append(rec-B); Append(rec-C); drain; Close; reopen; drain. Output: [same-seg] in-process delivered=["rec-A"] eof=true corrupt=0; [same-seg] after reopen delivered=[] eof=true. Roll case: Options{MaxSize:16<<20}, then nine 1 MiB records and rec-LAST, drained with four push ticks. Output: [roll-ticks] segments=2; delivered(4)=[rec-A big-7 big-8 rec-LAST]; SamplesDropped=map[] CorruptRecords=2 segments_left=1. Command: go test ./internal/agent/buffer -run TestZZVerifyRO09 -v (debug variant with drainWithTicks). Files deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** After any failed write in Segment.Append, truncate the file back to the pre-append size and fsync. Write header and payload as one buffer so a record is one write. In ReadAt, treat a length that runs past the true end of file as a torn tail and resynchronise on the next valid record. Recompute fileSize from the file size on recovery.

**Fix notes:** In Segment.Append, record the pre-append size and, on any write error, truncate back to it and fsync. Write header and payload as one buffer so a record is one write. In Next(), the corrupt branch must restart the outer loop, not continue the segment loop, so the next segment is not read at the wrong offset. Count records lost to a torn tail or skipped segment instead of dropping them with reason "" (removeOldestSegment and dropAckedSegments). recordsFrom can also count a torn record as valid and jump past the real end, so it needs the same bounds check as ReadAt.

Status: open

### XU-01 — Timestamps shown shifted by the browser UTC offset (CONFIRMED, metric-unit-catalogue)

**Location:** `web/src/lib/format/timestamp.ts:41`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** formatTimestamp rebuilds a UTC Date from the Intl wall-clock parts and then formats it with date-fns format(), which reads local-time getters. In any browser that is not on UTC the displayed wall clock is shifted by the browser offset, while the label still says UTC. The unit tests hide this because package.json:15 runs vitest with TZ=UTC and vitest.config.ts:19 sets env TZ UTC.

**Failure scenario:** An operator in Italy reads an audit entry, a finding last_seen or a setting changed_at one or two hours later than the stored UTC instant, under a UTC label. A New York browser shows the previous day.

**Evidence:**

```text
timestamp.ts:26-41: const wallClock = new Date(Date.UTC(Number(parts.year), Number(parts.month) - 1, Number(parts.day), Number(parts.hour), Number(parts.minute), Number(parts.second))); ... return `${format(wallClock, 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss', { locale: dateFnsLocale(locale) })} ${offset}`. Probe with web/node_modules/date-fns, same logic, input 2026-01-02T03:04:05Z and tz UTC: TZ=UTC gives 2026-01-02 03:04:05; TZ=Europe/Rome gives 2026-01-02 04:04:05; TZ=America/New_York gives 2026-01-01 22:04:05. Callers passing 'UTC': FindingCard.tsx:57, InstanceHeader.tsx:35, EventTimeline.tsx:22, RelationsSection.tsx:95 and 134, SettingsSection.tsx:126, PlanHistory.tsx:68, CommandAudit.tsx:78, ServerInfo.tsx:37.
```

**Verification reasoning:** web/src/lib/format/timestamp.ts rebuilds a UTC Date from the Intl wall-clock parts (lines 26-35), then date-fns format() (line 41) reads local-time getters. In any browser that is not on UTC, the printed wall clock is shifted by the browser offset while the label says UTC. No guard exists: formatTimestamp has no other path. All named callers pass 'UTC' (FindingCard.tsx:57, InstanceHeader.tsx:35, EventTimeline.tsx, RelationsSection.tsx:95 and 134, SettingsSection.tsx:126, PlanHistory.tsx:68, CommandAudit.tsx:78, ServerInfo.tsx:37). The unit test is blind to it because package.json:15 (TZ=UTC test script) and vitest.config.ts:19 (env TZ UTC) pin the zone. Reproduced outside vitest by running the real module under different browser zones.

**Repro:**

```text
cd web && TZ=UTC ./node_modules/.bin/tsx <scratch>/xu01_repro.ts  (script calls formatTimestamp('2026-01-02T03:04:05.000Z', tz) for tz UTC, Europe/Rome, America/New_York). Output with TZ=UTC: 'UTC' -> '2026-01-02 03:04:05 UTC'. With TZ=Europe/Rome: 'UTC' -> '2026-01-02 04:04:05 UTC' (one hour late); 'Europe/Rome' -> '2026-01-02 05:04:05 UTC+1' (one hour late). With TZ=America/New_York: 'UTC' -> '2026-01-01 22:04:05 UTC' (previous day). The same module under TZ=UTC prints the correct value.
```

**Suggested fix:** Build the string from the parts only, for example `${parts.year}-${parts.month}-${parts.day} ${parts.hour}:${parts.minute}:${parts.second} ${offset}`, and drop the date-fns format() call. Add a test that runs under a non-UTC zone (TZ=Europe/Rome in a dedicated test file or a second vitest project) so the masking is caught.

**Fix notes:** Location: timestamp.ts lines 26-41. Drop the Date.UTC rebuild and the date-fns format() call; build the string from the Intl parts (year, month, day, hour, minute, second) with hourCycle h23 already set. Keep the exact 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' layout: EventTimeline.tsx eventTime() takes formatted.slice(11, 19). Its check formatted === 'Unknown' can never match because UNKNOWN is '—' (shared.ts line 3), so an invalid timestamp renders as an empty time; fix that as well. Test: TZ=UTC is pinned for the whole suite (package.json:15, vitest.config.ts:19), so the regression test needs its own vitest project or a child process started with TZ=Europe/Rome.

### XU-02 — Range totals integrate one sampled rate per bucket (CONFIRMED, metric-unit-catalogue)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:807`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** /api/v1/metrics/query keeps one raw value per bucket, the last row in ts order (last value wins). The overview then multiplies each counter-rate bucket by the full bucket width, so the in-range tiles are one scrape's rate extrapolated across the step. Steps come from chooseStep: 24h gives 5m, 7d gives 15m, 30d gives 1h (STEP_LADDER 15s to 1d, timerange.ts:15-24 and 158-164). The checkpointer and database_stats checks scrape every 30 s (checkpointer.go:18, database_stats.go:20), so a bucket holds 10 to 120 samples and only the last survives.

**Failure scenario:** A week with one deadlock shows 'Deadlocks in range' as 0 or as 20 depending on which scrape closes its 15-minute bucket. A 30-day WAL or temp-bytes tile moves by the ratio of step to scrape interval, not by the real volume.

**Evidence:**

```text
api.go:789-807: '// Map bucket index -> value (last value wins if multiple per bucket)' ... bucketValues[idx] = val. metrics.ts:70-72: const seconds = previous === null ? stepSeconds : (timestamp - previous) / 1_000; total += point.value * seconds. OverviewSection.tsx:138-139 and 220-232 feed checkpointRate, deadlockRate, tempByteRate and walRate into integrateRate for the 'in range' tiles. Arithmetic: one checkpoint in one 30 s scrape is a rate of 1/30 per second; on a 15m bucket the tile reads 30 if that scrape is the last sample of the bucket and 0 otherwise; on a 1h bucket it reads 120 or 0.
```

**Verification reasoning:** api.go handleMetricsQuery keeps one value per bucket: bucketValues[idx] = val over rows ordered by ts, so the last scrape wins (lines 789-807). OverviewSection.tsx feeds deadlockRate, tempByteRate and walRate into integrateRate (lines 138-139, 220-232). integrateRate (lib/metrics.ts 59-79) multiplies each measured bucket by the time since the previous measured bucket (the step for the first). A stored counter value is one scrape's rate (pipeline.go line 472 stores pt.Rate), so each in-range tile equals one scrape's rate times the bucket width. InstancePage.tsx line 95 renders the overview. No guard found. Steps come from chooseStep (timerange.ts 158-164): 1h range uses 15s, 24h uses 5m, 7d uses 15m, 30d uses 1h. Handler logic verified by reading; the handler was not run against a database.

**Repro:**

```text
Ran the real integrateRate (web/src/lib/metrics.ts) with tsx on four 15-minute buckets: one deadlock sampled at 1/30 per second on the last scrape of bucket 2 gives 30, and the same rate on a non-last scrape gives 0. The true count in that window is 1. Command: cd web && ./node_modules/.bin/tsx <scratch>/xu02_repro.ts. Output: 'deadlock rate sample in bucket 2 (last scrape of bucket): integrateRate = 30' and 'no sampled deadlock in range: integrateRate = 0'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Aggregate per bucket on the server: for counter-kind rates return the bucket average, or persist the per-point interval (delta Point.Seconds) and return the exact increase per bucket. Integrate by summing bucket totals, not by multiplying one sample by the bucket width.

**Fix notes:** Location: api.go 789-807 (one row per bucket, last wins) and lib/metrics.ts integrateRate. Persisted metrics carry no per-point interval: pipeline.go 430-473 keeps sampleSeconds only for the metrics_statements route (row.SampleSeconds, migration 0014), so an exact per-bucket increase needs a schema change that stores the interval for metrics, or a server-side bucket average of rates. The fix must also cover the 1h range (15s step, so a bucket holds 0 or 1 scrape). Pitfall: with database empty (api.go 774-781), rows from every datname share one bucket and last-wins still applies.

### XU-04 — Disconnected standby reports zero replay lag, so lag alerts never fire (CONFIRMED, metric-unit-catalogue)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_receiver.go:54`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** When the walreceiver is gone, pg_stat_wal_receiver has no row, the status falls back to 'disconnected', and the lag CASE returns 0 whenever pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() equals pg_last_wal_replay_lsn(). A standby that has replayed all WAL it received therefore reports zero lag for as long as it stays disconnected, while the primary keeps writing. At the same moment the primary's sender row for that standby disappears. The alert source then falls back to the receiver row (source_sql.go:199-214 admits a receiver row when the upstream has no sender row in the window), and applyReplicationMetric keeps replay_lag_sec and drops the status (pipeline.go:1184).

**Failure scenario:** An asynchronous standby loses its network path. metrics_replication records lag 0 for it. replica.lag_high (pg_replication_lag_seconds above 30 for 120 s, migration 0006) and replica.all_standbys_lagging never fire, because the only standby row they see reads 0. The sender view that would show the standby has gone, and nothing else raises an alarm.

**Evidence:**

```text
replication_receiver.go:53-56: CASE WHEN pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() = pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() THEN 0 ELSE EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()) END. Container test on a postgres:19rc1-alpine primary and streaming standby: while streaming, the receiver check returned 'streaming|pglens-review-xu-prim|5432||0' and the primary had one sender row (walreceiver, streaming, async). After primary_conninfo was pointed at a closed port, the primary had 0 sender rows, and the standby receiver check returned 'disconnected||0||0' with pg_stat_wal_receiver empty. The primary LSN was 67,109,904 bytes ahead of the standby replay LSN (pg_wal_lsn_diff).
```

**Verification reasoning:** Mechanism confirmed. replication_receiver.go 53-56 returns replay lag 0 whenever pg_last_wal_receive_lsn() = pg_last_wal_replay_lsn(), which keeps holding after the walreceiver exits. A disconnected standby 16,778,256 bytes behind reported 0. Alert path: source_sql.go 199-214 admits the receiver row only when the upstream has no sender row in the lookback window, and pipeline.go applyReplicationMetric (1136-1194) stores replay_lag_sec and drops status (no status case). Qualifications for the fixer and the verdict: (a) for about the first 2 minutes the primary's pre-disconnect sender row is the newest and wins, so the alert input shows the old reading and then 0; (b) with another standby still streaming from the same primary, the disconnected standby's receiver row is excluded, so it drops out instead of reading 0; (c) the topology engine does emit orphan_standby after 60 s for a standby whose edges are all low-confidence (topology/engine.go 188-213; the wire Edge comment says low means not currently connected), but no built-in rule (builtin.go) and no seeded rule (migration 0006) consumes it, so no alarm fires by default. Severity stays high: the displayed and stored lag is 0 and no default alert fires.

**Repro:**

```text
postgres:19rc1-alpine primary and standby on private network pglens-review-xu04-b71e. Standby cloned with pg_basebackup -R -X stream into a named volume; the primary needed 'host replication all all trust' in pg_hba.conf. While streaming, the verbatim replication_receiver query returned 'streaming | pglens-review-xu04p-b71e | 5432 |  | 0'; the primary's pg_stat_replication showed walreceiver, streaming, async. After ALTER SYSTEM SET primary_conninfo = 'host=pglens-review-xu04p-b71e port=1 user=repl' and pg_reload_conf(): standby pg_stat_wal_receiver row count 0, primary pg_stat_replication row count 0. After pg_switch_wal() on the primary: the verbatim query returned ' disconnected |  | 0 |  | 0'. LSNs on standby: receive 0/04000060 = replay 0/04000060; pg_wal_lsn_diff(primary 0/05000470, standby replay 0/04000060) = 16778256. Cleanup note: I removed only my containers, network and volume. Three pglens-review-* containers (xd05sig, xp-18-a7c3, xp-19-a7c3) that were running when I started were already gone when I checked; I did not remove them.
```

**Suggested fix:** When the walreceiver row is absent (status not streaming or catchup), emit no replay-lag sample so the metric is omitted, keep the status and map it server-side. Alert when a known standby's sender row has aged out or its receiver status is disconnected. Add an integration test that disconnects a standby and asserts the alert input is not zero.

**Fix notes:** Locations: replication_receiver.go 53-56 (the CASE), pipeline.go 1136-1194 (only lag columns stored; the receiver 'status' label and metric are never stored in metrics_replication), source_sql.go 199-214 (latestStandbys admission rule). Fix: emit no replay-lag sample when the walreceiver row is absent, and carry the status server-side (needs a new column or series). Alert on a known standby whose sender row has aged out, or whose receiver status is disconnected. Also cover the multi-standby case, where the standby drops out of the input instead of reading 0. A default orphan_standby alert rule would give a built-in alarm.
