### CR-10 — replication_streaming is gated to primaries, so cascading middle nodes never report downstream lag (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_streaming.go:18`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Requires() sets Roles to RolePrimary only. pgtype/role.go:14-19 derives the role from pg_is_in_recovery(), so a cascading middle node is RoleStandby and never runs this check. The SQL's pg_is_in_recovery branch (lines 67-69, pg_last_wal_receive_lsn) can therefore only run on a standby, which means it is unreachable. The server expects sender rows from cascading standbys: pipeline.go:577-579 says 'a cascading standby has one [upstream]' for sender rows.

**Failure scenario:** In primary to A to B, B's write, flush and bytes lag and sync_state are never collected from A. The server falls back to B's own receiver replay-time row, which carries the CR-04 zero-while-disconnected problem.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code-level only; a cascade was not built live in this run. The gate is at replication_streaming.go:17-19, the SQL branch at 67-69, and the role derivation at role.go:14-19. The alert engine (internal/alert/source_sql.go, latestStandbys) uses a receiver row only when the upstream has no sender rows.
```

**Verification reasoning:** replication_streaming.go Requires() sets Roles to RolePrimary only. The agent derives role from pg_is_in_recovery() via pgtype.RoleFromRecovery (agent/conn.go ensureCache), so a cascading middle node is RoleStandby and Supports returns false with 'role standby not allowed', confirmed by a unit run. replication_receiver is standby-only. The recovery branch of the check's SQL is therefore effectively unreachable, and the check's own comment ('A cascading standby's own position is what it has received') describes a case the gate excludes. No other producer creates sender rows for a cascade: sender rows come only from a monitored instance's own pg_stat_replication. The alert path (alert/source_sql.go latestStandbys) falls back to the standby's receiver row, which carries only replay lag. Not reproduced with a live cascade; the verdict rests on unambiguous code reading with no guard elsewhere.

**Repro:**

```text
go test -count=1 -run TestVerifCR10 -v ./internal/check/ (temporary file internal/check/zz_verif_cr_test.go, deleted). Output: replication_streaming Supports(standby)=false reason='role standby not allowed'; replication_streaming Supports(primary)=true; replication_receiver Supports(standby)=true. Role source: agent/conn.go ensureCache sets m.target.cache.role = pgtype.RoleFromRecovery(inRecovery).
```

**Suggested fix:** Allow replication_streaming on RoleStandby as well (the SQL already handles recovery), or add a cascade-aware role. Add a downstream-lag assertion to the SYS-REPL-006 e2e scenario.

**Fix notes:** Dropping the Roles restriction makes the recovery branch live; re-check that the primary-side SQL still behaves (pg_is_in_recovery false, pg_current_wal_lsn). Pitfall, pre-existing, by reading and not run live: addScheduleEntries (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go, called once at line ~148) evaluates Requires() once at startup. A node that starts as a standby and is promoted later never gets replication_streaming scheduled until the agent restarts, and the same holds for any role-gated check. Any role-based gate needs re-evaluation on role change, and SYS-REPL-006 should cover downstream lag plus a failover. pipeline.go's comment at ~577-579 already assumes sender rows from cascading standbys.

### AT-02 — Topology transitions are permanently lost when the envelope transaction rolls back after Apply (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/server/pipeline.go:293`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** p.topo.Apply mutates the in-memory engine (instance role, lastPrimary, lastFailoverTime) inside the per-instance loop (pipeline.go:293-309). The transaction can still fail afterwards: the writes at pipeline.go:692-729 return errors, and tx.Commit is at line 730. Ingest maps a Process error to HTTP 500 (ingest.go:163-167), and the agent pusher retries 5xx with the same envelope (pusher.go:305-307, `continue`). On retry, Apply sees the role it already recorded, so it emits no role_change or failover_detected for that transition, and the rolled-back event row is never written.

**Failure scenario:** A standby is promoted. The envelope with role=primary reaches Process, Apply records failover_detected in memory, and a later write (for example WriteEvents at pipeline.go:707, or any transient DB error) fails. The transaction rolls back, so the event is gone. The agent retries the same envelope, Apply now sees role=primary already recorded, and no failover is ever persisted.

**Evidence:**

```text
pipeline.go:293-309 (Apply inside the loop); pipeline.go:692-731 (error returns before commit); pipeline.go:730 (Commit); topology/engine.go:163 (`inst.role = obs.Role`) and 168-172 (lastPrimary update); ingest.go:163-167; pusher.go:305-307.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Pipeline.Process calls p.topo.Apply inside the per-instance loop (internal/server/pipeline.go:293-309), which mutates engine state (instance role, lastPrimary, lastFailoverTime) before the transaction commits (pipeline.go:730). The writes at pipeline.go:692-729 can fail after that, and Process then returns an error. Ingest maps it to HTTP 500 (internal/server/ingest.go:163-167) and the agent pusher retries 5xx (internal/agent/pusher.go:305-307). On retry, Apply sees the role already recorded and emits no failover_detected. Inventory.Upsert runs before Process and writes role_change through inv.pool outside the pipeline transaction (internal/server/inventory.go:143-153), so role_change is still persisted; what is lost is failover_detected and its old_primary/new_primary payload. Scope is an edge case: it needs a failed write or commit. The probe mocks only the pipeline, not the full ingest path, and models transaction rollback with a wrapper that commits only on success. No guard found; the deferred Rollback (pipeline.go:112-114) does not reset topology state.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe internal/server/zz_probe_at02_test.go (since deleted): mockPool plus a wrapper tx that records the type argument of INSERT INTO events and copies it to committed only on successful Commit. Envelope A: old primary and standby. Clock +5s. Envelope B: standby promoted, commit fails. Clock +5s. Envelope C: same as B, commit succeeds. Command: cd into internal/server and run go test -run ZZProbeAT02 -v -count=1 . Output: 'B err=commit tx: simulated transient write failure staged-events=[failover_detected] committed-so-far=[role_change role_change]'; 'C committed events (cumulative)=[role_change role_change]'; 'failover_detected never persisted'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compute events without mutating engine state, commit the transaction, and only then apply the state transition. Alternatively, snapshot and restore the engine state on rollback, or derive transitions from the persisted last-known role so replays are idempotent.

**Fix notes:** Compute events without mutating engine state and apply the state transition only after commit, or snapshot and restore engine state when Process fails. The same mutate-before-commit problem affects the throttles: lastSplitBrain (internal/topology/engine.go:246) and orphanedAt (engine.go:204) are set at emission, so a rolled-back emission suppresses the retry for 60s and split_brain or orphan_standby is lost too.

### AT-05 — Partial rows from a failed tick still count toward AAS (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/ash/sampler.go:223`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** doSample delivers each row to onSample during rows.Next() (sampler.go:223-231) and checks rows.Err() only afterwards (sampler.go:233-235). If the query fails mid-stream, run() records a failed tick (sampler.go:185-187 via onTick; cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:53-56 calls agg.TickFailed), but the rows already delivered stay in the aggregator. Their samples are kept while the failed tick is excluded from the denominator.

**Failure scenario:** A tick returns one active row and then a network error. The reported AAS is above the true sampled value.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/ash/probe_test.go): one partial row in a failed tick gives AAS 1.11, true value 1.00. Code: sampler.go:223-235; cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:53-56.
```

**Verification reasoning:** doSample delivers each row to onSample during rows.Next() (internal/ash/sampler.go:223-231) and checks rows.Err() only afterwards (sampler.go:233-235). run() then calls onTick(false), which calls agg.TickFailed (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:53-56). TickFailed increments nothing (internal/ash/aggregator.go:93-100). The partial rows stay in counts while the failed tick is excluded from ticks, so AAS is inflated. The Scan-error branch (sampler.go:215-217) has the same leak, since rows delivered before the failing row are already counted. TestSampler_DoSample_ScanError passes a nil callback, so it cannot catch this. No guard found.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe internal/ash/zz_probe_at05_test.go (since deleted): nine successful ticks with one row each, then a tenth tick where the stream delivers one row and Err returns 'connection reset', then TickFailed and Flush. Command: cd into internal/ash and run go test -run ZZProbeAT05 -v -count=1 . Output: 'doSample err=connection reset window ticks=9 samples=10 avg=1.11'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Buffer each tick's rows and deliver them to onSample only after rows.Err() returns nil.

**Fix notes:** Buffer each tick's rows and deliver them to onSample only after rows.Err() returns nil. Apply the same buffering to the Scan-error branch at sampler.go:215-217, and extend TestSampler_DoSample_ScanError with a non-nil callback so the leak is covered.

### AT-09 — Sampler failures are invisible, so a dead sampler looks like an idle instance (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/ash/sampler.go:46`

**Category:** ux · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Sampler.TicksMissed() (sampler.go:139-141, counter at 46 and 179) has no production consumer, and failed ticks never reach the wire as an error or a metric. A sampler that fails every tick produces no windows and no error, which looks exactly like an idle instance. Combined with AT-01, the gap is indistinguishable from real idle time.

**Failure scenario:** The DSN becomes unreachable for a dedicated ASH connection. The dashboard shows zero load with no warning, and nobody notices that ASH has stopped.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: sampler.go:46, 139-141, 179; cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:53-56 (TickFailed only updates the aggregator). No production reader of TicksMissed was found.
```

**Verification reasoning:** TicksMissed() has no non-test reader: the only non-test occurrences are the counter and its accessor in internal/ash/sampler.go:46,139-141,179. The tick callback (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:51-57) only feeds TickSucceeded/TickFailed. The flush loop skips any window whose metrics are empty (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:76-78, 'if len(metrics) == 0 { continue }'). A doSample error goes back to run() and is not logged (sampler.go:177-187). Partial failure is partly visible: ashWindowToMetrics attaches window_ticks to each bucket of a window that has samples (ash.go:180-205), so a window with 6 of 10 ticks shows window_ticks=6. Total failure and genuine idle both produce zero metrics for the window, so they cannot be told apart. The finding's failure mode is real and is plausible under load: with statement_timeout = 400 (ashStatementTimeout), a heavily loaded pg_stat_activity scan can time out on every tick, which shows zero load exactly at peak. The ASH check never reports an error, and ASHEnabled stays true. Medium fits the rubric (misleading UI).

**Repro:**

```text
Static, not executed. grep over non-test Go files for TicksMissed returns only internal/ash/sampler.go:139-141. Relevant code: internal/ash/sampler.go:177-187 (err -> ticksMissed++ and onTick(false), no log), cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:51-57 and 76-78, and ash.go:180-205 (window_ticks is a per-bucket label).
```

**Suggested fix:** Surface tick-failure counts as a check error or metric in each envelope, and represent failed windows explicitly rather than as absent data.

**Fix notes:** Emit an explicit per-window tick count, including windows with zero buckets, so a window with Ticks == 0 is represented rather than dropped. Log or metric-count sampler errors (ticksMissed is never read). Keep window_ticks as the honest partial-failure signal; it is already correct.

### AT-10 — Password passed as a query parameter is hashed into the instance fingerprint (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/identity/fingerprint.go:57`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The ignore list (fingerprint.go:57-62) drops application_name, connect_timeout, statement_timeout and sslmode, but not password. Only userinfo passwords are removed (fingerprint.go:36-40). A `?password=<redacted> query parameter is therefore included in the SHA-256 fingerprint (qparts, fingerprint.go:63-80), even though pgx treats it as the real password. The doc comment at fingerprint.go:13-20 says passwords are ignored. Two consequences: rotating a password passed this way changes the instance identity, and the fingerprint is a hash over a password-bearing string, so it allows offline guessing if it ever leaves the host.

**Failure scenario:** An operator rotates the password in the DSN. On the next agent start the fingerprint changes, the identity store registers a new instance, and the old instance's history is orphaned.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/identity/probe_test.go): `?password=<redacted> and `?password=<redacted> give different fingerprints. internal/identity/pgxprobe confirms pgx.ParseConfig sets password=<redacted> from the query parameter. Code: fingerprint.go:36-40, 57-62, 63-80.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Probe run in a scratch test file (deleted afterwards). Fingerprint('postgres://u@h:5432/d?password=<redacted>') and ...?password=<redacted> differ, because the query-form password is not in the ignore list (fingerprint.go:57-62) and is hashed through qparts (fingerprint.go:63-80). pgx.ParseConfig gives Password='<redacted>' from the query parameter, so the hashed value is the real password. The userinfo form is stable, since the password is dropped at fingerprint.go:36-40. The doc comment at fingerprint.go:13-20 says passwords are ignored, which is false for this form. Impact: a rotated query-form password creates a new instance id, which orphans history. The 'leaves the host' concern is conditional: the fingerprint is only a map key in the local identity file (identity.go:14-16, mode 0600), and I did not find it sent on the wire. This is a rare DSN form plus rotation, so medium holds.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe test in internal/identity (go test -count=1 -run TestVerifierProbeAT10 -v ./internal/identity/): output 'zz_verifier_probe_test.go:12: query-password fingerprints equal=false', 'zz_verifier_probe_test.go:17: pgx effective Password="<redacted>"', 'zz_verifier_probe_test.go:20: userinfo-password fingerprints equal=true'. Probe file deleted.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add password (and other credential-bearing keys such as sslpassword) to the ignore list, compare keys case-insensitively, and add a test that asserts the fingerprint is stable across password changes in both userinfo and query form.

**Fix notes:** Add 'password' and 'sslpassword' to the ignore map at fingerprint.go:57-62. Case folding already exists (ignore[strings.ToLower(k)] at line 66), so the finding's case-insensitivity suggestion is already met. Pitfall: removing the password changes the fingerprint of existing query-form DSNs once, which re-registers those instances on upgrade. Handle that by keeping the old fingerprint as an alias in identity.json, or document it. Update the comment at fingerprint.go:13-20.

Status: open

### AT-14 — Self-failover emits failover_detected with old and new primary equal (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/topology/engine.go:117`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The failover branch (engine.go:117-131) fires for any standby-to-primary transition with a recent primary, without checking that the recent primary is a different instance. An instance that goes primary to standby and back to primary within 120s is reported as failing over to itself.

**Failure scenario:** A primary restarts as a standby during a brief network event and is promoted again 40s later. The events table records a failover from the instance to itself, which misleads alert and dashboard consumers.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/topology/probe_test.go): failover_detected with old_primary equal to new_primary. Code: engine.go:117-131.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Engine reproduction: a primary P goes standby at t=10 (role_change), then primary again at t=50, and the engine emits failover_detected with old_primary equal to new_primary (the same P). The branch at engine.go:117-131 has no check that lastPrim.instanceID differs from obs.InstanceID, and lastPrimary still points at P from before the demotion (engine.go:168-173). Severity raised from the finding's low: the event type is wrong and failover_detected is a default-enabled critical alert (internal/alert/builtin.go:14: Tier0, Enabled true, SeverityCritical, 'A failover was observed'), so a self-transition pages operators falsely. The trigger is an edge case (demote and re-promote the same instance within 120s), which keeps it below high.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe in internal/topology (go test -count=1 -run TestVerifierProbeAT14SelfFailover -v ./internal/topology/): 't=0 P primary: [role_change]', 't=10 P standby: [role_change]', 't=50 P primary again: [failover_detected]' with payload new_primary and old_primary both equal to 25e518b8-121f-45d9-8e00-4bea2171be01. Probe file deleted.
```

**Suggested fix:** Require lastPrim.instanceID != obs.InstanceID before emitting failover_detected; otherwise emit role_change.

**Fix notes:** Add lastPrim.instanceID != obs.InstanceID to the condition at engine.go:118. When it is equal, emit role_change, and do not set lastFailoverTime (engine.go:130). Consider whether the alert rule should also ignore self-failovers.

### AT-15 — Container memory available is limit minus current, so page cache is counted as used (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/host/cgroup.go:36`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** applyV2 reads memory.max and memory.current (cgroup.go:36-37) and derives available memory as limit minus current (applyV2, cgroup.go:34-45). memory.current includes page cache, which the kernel can reclaim, so available memory is understated. cgroup_test.go:46-49 (TestCgroup_AvailableIsLimitMinusCurrent) pins this behaviour, so the test locks in the bug.

**Failure scenario:** A container with a 1GB limit reads 150MB of file-backed cache. The agent reports about 850MB available when about 1GB is reclaimable, which triggers memory alerts for a healthy workload.

**Evidence:**

```text
Container test: after writing 150MB to a file, memory.current=163MB, inactive_file=157MB, anon 57KB; computed available is 93MB against roughly 250MB real. Code: cgroup.go:36-45; cgroup_test.go:46-49.
```

**Verification reasoning:** cgroup.go:34-45 (applyV2) sets available = memory.max - memory.current and never reads memory.stat, so page cache (inactive_file) is counted as used. cgroup_test.go:46-49 asserts 768, which is limit minus current from the fixture (memory.max=1024, memory.current=256 under internal/host/testdata/cgroup_v2/fs/cgroup). No guard elsewhere: run.go:376-377 (hostWireResult) passes the value straight to host_mem_available_bytes, which HostSection.tsx shows as 'Memory available'. Severity stays medium because the error is bounded to page cache charged to the agent's own cgroup; it becomes high when a monitored database shares that cgroup, since its file cache would dominate.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway postgres:17.11-alpine container with --memory 1g; wrote 150MB to a file and ran sync. Results: memory.max=1073741824, memory.current=162877440, memory.stat inactive_file=157286400, anon=98304. The code's formula gives 1073741824-162877440=910864384 bytes available, while subtracting inactive_file gives about 1068150784. The understatement equals the reclaimable cache.
```

**Suggested fix:** Subtract inactive_file (from memory.stat) from memory.current, as the kernel does for MemAvailable, and update cgroup_test.go to assert that page cache is excluded.

**Fix notes:** Subtract memory.stat inactive_file from memory.current, falling back to memory.current when memory.stat is absent. The testdata cgroup_v2 directory has no memory.stat, so add one with an inactive_file line and update TestCgroup_AvailableIsLimitMinusCurrent to expect 1024-(256-inactive_file). Keep the fallback so the v1 path and fixtures without memory.stat still work.

Status: open

### AT-16 — Host CPU ratio is host-wide while CPUCount reflects the cgroup quota (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/host/collector.go:77`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** CPUUsedRatio is computed from the host-wide CPU counter delta (collector.go:77-80), while CPUCount comes from the cgroup quota (cgroup.go:47-58). The two are reported side by side but do not describe the same resource.

**Failure scenario:** A container limited to 2 CPUs on a 16-core host runs at full quota. The ratio shows about 12%, against a CPUCount of 2, so the value reads as if the container is nearly idle.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: collector.go:71-90 (delta math, which is correct on its own); cgroup.go:47-58 (quota to CPUCount).
```

**Verification reasoning:** collector.go:62 reads cpu.TimesWithContext(ctx,false), an aggregate over all host CPUs, so the ratio at collector.go:77-80 is host-wide. cgroup.go:47-58 sets CPUCount from the cgroup quota. The UI shows both under a cgroup source: HostSection.tsx:117-121 prints 'Source: cgroup_v2' above 'CPU used' (host_cpu_used_ratio) and 'CPU count' (host_cpu_count) with no label tying the ratio to the host. A container at its quota on a 16-core host reads 12.5% with CPU count 2. The metric name carries a host_ prefix, but the source label implies container scope, so the mismatch is misleading.

**Repro:**

```text
Code and UI reading only. The arithmetic is the host-wide formula: 2 busy cores out of 16 gives 0.125, which the UI renders as 12.5% beside 'CPU count 2' under 'Source: cgroup_v2'. No live sampling was run.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compute the ratio against effective CPUs (quota, when present) and label the field, or report host and cgroup utilisation as separate fields.

**Fix notes:** Lowest-risk fix: relabel the tile (for example 'Host CPU used') and the wire metric description so it is not presented as container CPU. A container-scoped ratio would need cpu.stat usage_usec deltas over wall time divided by the quota, with the host ratio as fallback. Renaming host_cpu_used_ratio touches the wire contract, server and UI, so do not rename it casually.

Status: open

### AT-17 — Cgroup detection fails under cgroupns=host, so container limits are ignored (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/host/cgroup.go:14`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Cgroup version and root detection looks for memory.max and cpu.max directly at the cgroup mount root (cgroup.go:14-23). With --cgroupns=host, the container sees the host root cgroup, where those files are absent, so limits are not detected and the agent falls back to host totals.

**Failure scenario:** A container with a 512MB limit runs under --cgroupns=host. The agent reports host RAM as the container total, so the container memory percentage and the memory total stated in README.md:1729 are wrong.

**Evidence:**

```text
Container test with --cgroupns=host: /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max and cpu.max are absent at the root, and limits are not detected. Code: cgroup.go:14-23.
```

**Verification reasoning:** applyCgroup (cgroup.go:14-23) detects v2 by the cgroup.controllers file at the mount root, which exists under both cgroup namespace modes. Under --cgroupns=host the root cgroup has no memory.max, memory.current or cpu.max, so applyV2 sets nothing and Source stays 'host'. The default cgroupns on cgroup v2 hosts is private, so this needs an explicit host namespace setting. No guard exists, and README.md:1729 promises the cgroup total inside a limited container.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway postgres:17.11-alpine containers with --memory 512m. With --cgroupns=host, /sys/fs/cgroup lists cgroup.controllers and cpu.stat but no memory.max, memory.current or cpu.max. /proc/self/cgroup reads '0::/system.slice/docker-<id>.scope', and /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-<id>.scope/memory.max holds 536870912. With --cgroupns=private, memory.max, memory.current and cpu.max are present at the root.
```

**Suggested fix:** Resolve the process's own cgroup path from /proc/self/cgroup and read its limit files there, falling back to the mount root only when that fails.

**Fix notes:** Parse the '0::<path>' line from /proc/self/cgroup and read the limit files under root+path, falling back to root when that fails. In private mode the path is '/', so the same files are read and behaviour is unchanged. Keep the cgroup.controllers check for v2 detection. Add a fixture with a nested path to cgroup_test.go.

### SI-02 — Inventory turns database errors into per-instance rejects; agent consumes the 202 (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/inventory.go:62`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Upsert returns (res, nil) on every path (inventory.go:69), and any upsertOne error, including PostgreSQL connection failures, becomes a per-instance rejection (inventory.go:62-64). IngestHandler filters the instance and answers 202 with rejected greater than zero (ingest.go:154-162, 176-178). The IngestHandler error branch at ingest.go:147-152 is unreachable for database errors. The agent treats any 202 as consumed (internal/agent/pusher.go:258-271 returns pushConsumed), so the whole envelope is dropped. The pipeline path behaves differently: a DB error in Process returns 500 and the agent retries (ingest.go:163-168). A transient database outage during the inventory phase therefore silently and permanently drops samples, while the same outage during storage is retried.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** PostgreSQL restarts for 20 seconds. Every envelope in that window fails at upsertOne for each instance, Upsert returns Rejected=N, the handler answers 202 with accepted 0 and rejected N, and the agent marks the envelope consumed. No retry happens and no event is recorded; the data is simply missing.

**Correction (from verification):** However, the finding's headline scenario is refuted: if the pipeline's own Begin also fails (a full outage), the handler returns 500 'pipeline error', and the agent retries.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/inventory.go:62 `if err := inv.upsertOne(ctx, tenantID, agentUUID, inst); err != nil {`; inventory.go:63-64 `res.Rejected++` / `res.Errors[inst.InstanceID] = err`; inventory.go:69 `return res, nil`; internal/server/ingest.go:177-178 `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusAccepted)` after rejected counting; internal/agent/pusher.go:271 `return pushConsumed, nil`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: Upsert always returns nil error (inventory.go:69), and any upsertOne error, including DB errors, becomes a per-instance reject (62-64). IngestHandler then filters the instance and answers 202 with rejected>0 (ingest.go:154-162, 176-178) when the pipeline call succeeds, and the agent treats 202 as consumed (pusher.go 202 branch). Reproduced: with the inventory lookup failing, a healthy pipeline Begin gives 202 {accepted:0,rejected:1}. However, the finding's headline scenario is refuted: if the pipeline's own Begin also fails (a full outage), the handler returns 500 'pipeline error', and the agent retries. The 202 drop needs statement- or connection-level failures in the inventory phase while Begin succeeds (for example stale pooled connections right after a restart, or a statement timeout). That is an edge case, hence medium.

**Repro:**

```text
Harness: mockPool with a QueryRow failure injected for SQL containing 'SELECT id_source FROM clusters' (connection reset). Handler: IngestHandler(NewAuth('token'), &Inventory{pool}, pipeline) with pipeline.pool set to the same pool, valid envelope with one instance and a non-empty agent_id. Outputs: (1) Begin ok: status=202 body={"accepted":0,"rejected":1}. (2) Begin fails with 'connection refused': status=500 body={"error":"pipeline error","detail":"begin tx: connection refused"}. (3) healthy control: status=202 body={"accepted":1,"rejected":0}. Command: go test -run TestVF_SI02 -v ./internal/server/ (temporary file, deleted).
```

**Suggested fix:** Return the error from Upsert for infrastructure failures and keep Errors only for validation rejections (for example cluster_id_changed). Let IngestHandler answer 500 or 503 so the agent retries. Add a test that a failing pool yields a non-202 status.

**Fix notes:** upsertOne returns plain fmt errors, so validation rejects and infrastructure failures cannot be told apart. Return a typed or sentinel error for infrastructure failures and keep Errors for validation. Do not map every error to 500: a deterministic DB error (for example a constraint violation) would then make the agent retry forever and wedge its buffer, which is the same risk pusher.go's encode-error comment describes. inventory_test.go:239 (TestInventory_MockPool_UpsertCluster_LookupError_Rejected) asserts the current reject behaviour and must change with the fix. The IngestHandler error branch at ingest.go:147-152 is dead for DB errors because Upsert never returns non-nil.

### SI-03 — instances.last_seen is refreshed before data commits; instance reads up with no data (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/inventory.go:156`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Inventory.Upsert sets instances.last_seen=now() for existing rows (inventory.go:156) and for new rows (inventory.go:178-179) before Pipeline.Process runs. Staleness and the alert up metric read last_seen as the liveness signal (internal/server/staleness.go:490-493, internal/alert/source_sql.go:115). If Process then fails (500, ingest.go:163-168) or the instance is rejected inside the pipeline (instErr, pipeline.go:631-634), last_seen stays fresh while no metrics or self-metrics were stored for that instance. A deterministic per-instance rejection therefore keeps the instance up indefinitely with no data, and the agent drops the envelope on the 202.

**Failure scenario:** An instance whose check output fails a pipeline validation on every push: last_seen is refreshed every push, pglens_up stays 1, the agent_down alert never fires, the instance shows no metrics, and the only signal is a rejected count in the 202 body.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/inventory.go:156 `UPDATE instances SET role=$1, pg_version=$2, perm_tier=$3, addr=$4, port=$5, target_name=$6, last_seen=now(), ash_enabled=$7 WHERE instance_id=$8`; internal/server/pipeline.go:631-634 `if instErr != nil {` / `res.Rejected++`; internal/server/ingest.go:163-168 pipeline error returns 500.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: the instances UPDATE with last_seen=now() (inventory.go:156) runs before Process, and staleness reads last_seen (staleness.go:436 query, 490-493 up gauge), as does the alert up SQL (alert/source_sql.go:113-117). Reproduced: (a) pipeline Begin failure gives 500 with the UPDATE already executed, and (b) an instance rejected inside the pipeline (unknown metric kind) gives 202 {accepted:0,rejected:1} with the UPDATE executed. Case (a) on its own is weak, because the agent retries and the fresh last_seen then matches a live agent. The defensible defect is (b): selfMetricRows (pipeline.go:636) runs after the instErr continue (631-634), so a rejected instance gets no pglens_check_error_rate row, check_failing cannot fire, and nothing durable records the rejection beyond the 202 body. That keeps the instance up with no data indefinitely.

**Repro:**

```text
Harness: mockPool with an existing instance row returned by QueryRow for 'SELECT cluster_id, role FROM instances WHERE instance_id' (same cluster, role primary). (a) Begin error 'connection refused' gives status=500, and an Exec whose SQL contains 'UPDATE instances SET' with the instance id as an argument is recorded (update_ran=true). (b) Envelope instance with a result metric of kind 'bogus' gives status=202 body={"accepted":0,"rejected":1}, update_ran=true. Command: go test -run TestVF_SI03 -v ./internal/server/ (temporary file, deleted).
```

**Suggested fix:** Move the last_seen update into the same transaction as the pipeline commit, or run it only after tx.Commit succeeds. Do not refresh last_seen for instances the pipeline rejected.

**Fix notes:** Case (b) is the one to fix. Options: write last_seen only after tx.Commit, and only for instances that were not rejected; and/or emit a durable self-metric or fact for a rejected instance so check_failing and the UI can see it. Inventory.Upsert runs on the pool, not the pipeline tx, so moving last_seen into the pipeline transaction requires passing the tx through. Note that the pipeline's resolveAddr also reads instances, so ordering matters.

### SI-04 — Shared bootstrap token authorizes command enqueue and queue polling for any agent (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/session.go:160`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** RequireCredential accepts the shared bootstrap agent token on every /api/ route (session.go:160-162), and the gate is installed globally (http.go:25). The command routes are therefore reachable with the agent token: <redacted> /api/v1/instances/{id}/commands (commands.go:93) enqueues explain, cancel or terminate for any instance. The poll handler authenticates the caller with the token alone and takes the agent identity from the self-declared X-PGLENS-Agent-ID header (commands.go:239, 256-257), so any token holder can read and claim another agent's queue. requesterOf labels these requests 'api-token' (commands.go:340), so the audit cannot tell which host acted. README:343 documents agent-token access to the API as intended, so this is a design gap, not a bypass of documented behavior. The agent executes commands only when its commands.enabled is on (README:367, 420-421), which limits the impact. Every monitored host holds the shared secret.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A compromised monitored host, which holds PGLENS_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN, POSTs a cancel or terminate command for an instance on another host. Or it GETs /api/v1/agents/<other-agent>/commands with X-PGLENS-Agent-ID set to <other-agent> and receives that agent's queued commands.

**Correction (from verification):** Mitigation correction: README.md says the pull channel is available by default, and that only targets[].allow_signal and allow_explain_analyze are deny-by-default.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/session.go:160 `if auth != nil && auth.Validate(r) {` / `next.ServeHTTP(w, r)`; internal/server/commands.go:93 `r.Post("/api/v1/instances/{id}/commands", s.enqueue)`; internal/server/commands.go:239 `agentID := r.Header.Get(commandAgentIDHeader)`; internal/server/commands.go:257 `if authenticatedID != requestedID {`; README.md:343 `requests still need the agent token or a session cookie`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: RequireCredential (session.go:160) accepts the bootstrap token on every /api/ route. Enqueue (commands.go:93, 138-197) has no principal check and labels any token request 'api-token' (requesterOf, 339-352). Poll (246-260) takes its identity from the self-declared X-PGLENS-Agent-ID header (239-243, with X-Agent-ID fallback) and compares it to the path (257), so any token holder can read or claim another agent's queue. Reproduced: enqueue with the bootstrap token gives 202, and polling another agent's queue with the header gives 204, versus 403 without the header and 401 with a wrong token. Mitigation correction: README.md says the pull channel is available by default, and that only targets[].allow_signal and allow_explain_analyze are deny-by-default. So plain explain and pgstattuple run on default targets, and the finding's 'only when commands.enabled is on' is weaker than stated (the agent-side gate code was not read). Documented token access (README.md:343) makes the enqueue part a design question. The header-derived identity is a real isolation flaw that does not reach the monitored database. session.go and commands.go are outside the declared scope; verified anyway.

**Repro:**

```text
Harness: chi router with r.Use(RequireCredential(UIConfig{}, NewAuth('token'), nil)) and NewCommandService(mockPool, auth).RegisterRoutes(r); the mock QueryRow returns (agent_id, cluster_id, tenant_id) for the instance lookup. Outputs: POST /api/v1/instances/<id>/commands with Bearer token and body {"kind":"cancel","args":{"pid":4242}} gives 202 {"command_id":...}. GET /api/v1/agents/<other>/commands with Bearer token and X-PGLENS-Agent-ID=<other> gives 204. Same without the header gives 403 'agent identity header is required'. Wrong token gives 401. Command: go test -run TestVF_SI04 -v ./internal/server/ (temporary file, deleted).
```

**Suggested fix:** Limit the bootstrap token to /api/v1/push. Use per-agent credentials for poll and result routes, derive the agent identity from the credential rather than a header, and require a UI session for enqueue. Record the authenticating principal in command_audit. Confirm intent with the commands area owner, since the commands file is outside this review's scope.

**Fix notes:** Derive the agent identity from a per-agent credential or the stored instances.agent_id, not from the header; drop the X-Agent-ID fallback (commands.go:241). Record the authenticating principal in command_audit (requesterOf). Consider restricting enqueue to UI sessions. Coordinate with the commands owner, since session.go and commands.go are outside this review's scope. README.md:343 documents agent-token API access, so update the docs with whatever is decided.

### SI-07 — Staleness state advanced before event insert; a failed insert permanently loses transition events (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/staleness.go:512`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** On an up/down transition the evaluator stores the new state before emitting events: staleness.go:512 (`s.instanceUp[iidStr] = up`) and staleness.go:497 for the first observation. If emitEvent fails (pool exhaustion, DB restart), Evaluate returns the error (staleness.go:523-525 and 526-528). The next pass sees prevUp == up, so the missing instance_unreachable or agent_up or instance_reachable event is never retried. For slot_inactive, decideSlotInactiveEmissions sets emitted[key]=true (staleness.go:642) before the insert at staleness.go:690, so a failed insert suppresses that slot's event for the whole spell. The metric-driven agent_down alert is not affected because it reads last_seen; the event-driven rules (instance_unreachable, builtin.go:8) and the event rows are.

**Failure scenario:** Agent H goes silent. At the transition staleness sets instanceUp=false and inserts agent_down, but the instance_unreachable insert fails on a transient error. The next pass sees no transition, so no instance_unreachable event exists for this outage and event-driven alerting never fires.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/staleness.go:512 `s.instanceUp[iidStr] = up`; internal/server/staleness.go:523-528 agent_down then instance_unreachable emits with early return on error; internal/server/staleness.go:642 `emitted[key] = true`; internal/server/staleness.go:690 `if emitErr := s.emitEvent(ctx, "slot_inactive", ...`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: on a transition, instanceUp is set before the emits (staleness.go:512 for up/down, 497 for first observation). Each emitEvent failure returns an error (523-528, 502-507) and leaves the state changed. The next pass sees prevUp==up and never retries. Nothing reloads instanceUp inside Evaluate. Start() (726) discards the Evaluate error, so the loss is also never logged. The slot path (decideSlotInactiveEmissions sets emitted at 642, before the insert at 690) has the same defect, confirmed by reading only. Reproduced against real PostgreSQL: after an injected instance_unreachable insert failure, Evaluate returns an error, instanceUp=false, agent_down=1 and instance_unreachable=0. After the fault is cleared and three more passes run, instance_unreachable is still 0. A control instance with no fault emits both events. The metric-driven agent_down alert is unaffected because it reads last_seen; the event-driven rule (builtin.go instance_unreachable) is not.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway local container pglens-review-wfea87-si07 (postgres:17.11-alpine, removed afterwards). Schema is a minimal hand-written one, not the repo migrations: instances(instance_id, cluster_id, last_seen, role, agent_id NOT NULL), events(event_id bigserial, tenant_id, ts, type, cluster_id, instance_id, payload), metrics_replication(...). A BEFORE INSERT trigger on events raises 'injected insert failure' for type 'instance_unreachable'. Test in package server: NewStaleness(pool, nil), Evaluate, then UPDATE last_seen to now()-1h. Outputs: pass 2 err='insert event instance_unreachable: ... injected insert failure'; instanceUp=false; agent_down=1; instance_unreachable=0. After DROP TRIGGER and three more Evaluate calls: instance_unreachable=0 and no error. Control instance Y: agent_down=1, instance_unreachable=1. Command: PGLENS_VERIFY_DSN=postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:<port>/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -run TestVF_SI07 -v ./internal/server/.
```

**Suggested fix:** Update state only after every event of the transition has been inserted, or persist pending emissions and retry them on the next pass. For slots, set emitted only after the insert succeeds.

**Fix notes:** Set instanceUp only after every transition event is inserted (first observation at 497, transitions at 512 with the emits at 516-528), or persist pending transitions and retry them on the next pass. For slots, set emitted[key] only after emitEvent succeeds at 690; decideSlotInactiveEmissions (612-646) currently mutates emitted before the insert. Also log the error in Start (726 currently discards it). A real-DB test is needed because Staleness holds a concrete *pgxpool.Pool; the trigger technique above works.

### SI-11 — Former leader keeps frozen pglens_up gauges; non-leaders expose none (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/staleness.go:492`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** pglensUpGauge and pglensAgentLastSeenGauge are set only inside the leader-only path (staleness.go:492-493). Evaluate returns early when this replica does not hold the lock (staleness.go:429-431) without clearing them. A replica that loses leadership keeps its last values indefinitely, so its /metrics reports pglens_up=1 and a frozen last_seen for instances that have since gone down, while the new leader reports correctly. A non-leader never sets these gauges, so scraping it returns no series.

**Failure scenario:** Replica A is leader when agent H dies, then leadership moves to replica B. A's /metrics keeps reporting pglens_up{instance=H}=1 indefinitely. A Prometheus job scraping both replicas sees conflicting values, and an alert on pglens_up over A's series never fires.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/staleness.go:492 `pglensUpGauge.Set(iidStr, boolToFloat(up))`; internal/server/staleness.go:493 `pglensAgentLastSeenGauge.Set(iidStr, float64(inst.lastSeen.Unix()))`; internal/server/staleness.go:429-431 `if !hasLock {` / `return nil`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The gauges are process-global and are set only on the hasLock path (staleness.go:492-493). Evaluate returns early when !hasLock (429-431) without clearing them, and MetricsHandler snapshots them unconditionally (metrics_handler.go:20-21). A non-leader never sets its series, so it exposes no series for the instances it observes. The frozen-gauge scenario only occurs when the loss is detected through IsClosed() (staleness.go:340). That detection is effectively unreachable, because the leader never does I/O on its pinned connection while it holds the lock. The real failure is worse, and it is a separate finding (SI-11b below).

**Repro:**

```text
Run each test in its own invocation (gauges are process-global). Command: go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI11_ -count=1 -v. Decisive output: 'A first evaluate: hasLock=true gauge(H)=1'; 'A after losing lock: hasLock=false gauge(H)=1 (DB: last_seen 200s old, should be 0)'; 'non-leader C: gauge series for stale H2 present=false'.
```

**Suggested fix:** On leadership loss, delete the gauge series or reset the vectors, and expose a leader indicator so scrapes can select the leader. Alternatively compute the gauge from the database in the handler.

**Fix notes:** On !hasLock, reset pglensUpGauge and pglensAgentLastSeenGauge, and expose a leader indicator. SI-11b (new, verified, not in the list, highest priority): after pg_terminate_backend of the leader's lock session, the old leader still believes it leads, and a second replica also becomes leader. Output: 'terminated A's lock session pid=188 ok=true'; 'A after its session was killed: conn.IsClosed=false hasLock=true'; 'B hasLock=true'; 'agent_down events for H after both replicas evaluated: 2'. Root cause: ensureLeader (staleness.go:340) trusts IsClosed(), which only flips after an I/O failure on the pinned connection. The leader never performs I/O on it while holding the lock. The same pattern is at internal/alert/engine.go:192-195. That was not run, and it probably produces duplicate notifications, so verify it before filing. Fix: re-verify lock ownership each cycle (for example, check pg_locks for this backend's advisory lock, or ping the connection) and drop leadership on mismatch.

Status: open

### SI-12 — Cluster identity is written before the immutability check; phantom cluster rows and an event on every push (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/inventory.go:119`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** upsertCluster runs at inventory.go:119, before the existing-instance cluster_id immutability check (inventory.go:126-141). A push whose cluster_id differs from the stored one first writes the attempted cluster row (inventory.go:211, and the id_source change at inventory.go:230-236), then emits cluster_id_changed (inventory.go:138) and fails. cluster_id_changed and cluster_identity_conflict (inventory.go:217-229) are emitted on every push, with no dedupe. At the default 15s push interval (README.md:772) that is about 5,760 events per day per misidentified instance. The attempted cluster also appears in the clusters listing.

**Failure scenario:** A restored DSN or misconfigured identity reports cluster_id C2 for instance X, which is owned by C1. Every push inserts or touches a C2 cluster row and an event, indefinitely, and the clusters API lists C2 as a monitored cluster.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/inventory.go:119 `if err := inv.upsertCluster(ctx, tenantID, cidDB, inst.ClusterID, inst.ClusterIDSource, instUUID); err != nil {`; internal/server/inventory.go:132 `if existingCID != cidDB {`; internal/server/inventory.go:138 `if emitErr := inv.emitEvent(ctx, tenantID, time.Now().UTC(), "cluster_id_changed", ...`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** upsertCluster runs before the cluster_id immutability check (inventory.go:119 runs before 132). Each push that claims a different cluster writes the attempted cluster row and then emits cluster_id_changed, so the event count grows by one per push. The clusters listing (api.go:276, no join to instances) then shows the phantom cluster. The instance row keeps its original cluster and the rejected instance is filtered out of the pipeline (ingest.go:153-161), so no instance data is corrupted. Medium fits the edge-case trigger and the event flood (about 5,760 per day at the default 15s push interval).

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (deleted), same container. Command: go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI12 -count=1 -v. Decisive output: 'push 1 (cluster 1001): accepted=1 errors=0'; 'push 2 (cluster 2002): accepted=0 rejected=1 cluster_id_changed_total=1'; 'push 3 ... cluster_id_changed_total=2'; 'push 4 ... cluster_id_changed_total=3'; 'clusters listing row: cluster_id=2002 id_source=system_identifier'; 'instance row cluster_id=1001 (unchanged)'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Read the existing instance's cluster_id and reject before calling upsertCluster. Emit cluster_id_changed once per (instance, attempted cluster) using a unique key or a rate limit, and do not change id_source for a rejected attempt.

**Fix notes:** Read the existing instance's cluster_id before calling upsertCluster (inventory.go:119). Deduplicate cluster_id_changed per (instance, attempted cluster). The id_source upgrade branch (inventory.go:230-236) should not run for a rejected attempt.

### SI-15 — Agent retries an envelope forever after its 10s timeout; slow server processing wedges the queue (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/agent/pusher.go:87`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The agent HTTP client has Timeout 10s (pusher.go:86-88). A network error, including client timeout, takes the continue retry path (pusher.go:251-254) with no attempt limit, so the same envelope is re-sent until it succeeds. The server has no processing deadline of its own. When processing an envelope takes more than 10s (lock waits on hypertables, slow inserts, large envelopes), the agent cancels. The server's r.Context is cancelled on client disconnect, and the transaction in Process is bound to that context (pipeline.go:108-114), so it rolls back and the same envelope is retried. The queue head stays blocked and newer envelopes are not sent. Each rollback also triggers SI-01.

**Failure scenario:** A 12-second write stall on a hypertable during a compression job. Attempt 1 times out at 10s and rolls back; attempt 2 is identical and times out again. The queue never drains, and the envelope ages past the 12h sent_at limit (ingest.go:114), after which the server rejects it with 400 'samples too old' and the agent drops it.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/agent/pusher.go:87 `Timeout: 10 * time.Second,`; internal/agent/pusher.go:254 `continue`; internal/server/pipeline.go:108-114 transaction begun with the request context.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Mechanism verified and reproduced. Agent HTTP client has Timeout 10s (internal/agent/pusher.go:87). A doRequest error takes the bare continue path (pusher.go:250-255) with no attempt cap, and 5xx also loops with continue (pusher.go:305-307). Push runs synchronously from the 1-second tick in cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:284 using the agent lifetime context with no deadline, so one stuck envelope blocks the whole queue head (pushFromBuffer returns only after pushOne does). Server side: ingest.go:128 uses r.Context(), which Process uses for pool.Begin(ctx) at pipeline.go:108, so a client-side timeout cancels the request context and rolls the transaction back. No guard found: WriteTimeout is 2m (cmd/pglens-server/main.go:156) and does not cancel the request context. Severity medium is right: the loop is unbounded, but it needs a server stall of more than 10s per attempt.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway Go test in internal/agent (httptest server that stalls attempts 1 and 2 for 12s, then returns 202), run as: go test ./internal/agent -run TestSI15Verify -v -count=1. Decisive output: server attempt 1 at +1ms; request context done: context canceled; server attempt 2 at +11.821s; request context done: context canceled; server attempt 3 at +24.217s; Push returned err=<nil> after 24.217s; total server attempts=3; all attempts carried identical envelope body=true; acked=1 dropped=0 pending-after=0. Test file deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Give the server a processing budget below the agent timeout and return 503 with Retry-After quickly. On the agent, bound retries per envelope or raise the timeout above the server budget, and do not let one envelope block the queue indefinitely.

**Fix notes:** A larger agent timeout only moves the threshold, so bound retries per envelope or add a server-side budget below the agent timeout that returns 503 with Retry-After, and make the agent honour it within a bounded policy. Note the 400 path (pusher.go:273-281, for example 'samples too old') sets HealthIncompatible and returns /healthz 503 as a side effect; the fixer should preserve or consciously change that. Do not use the 10s client timeout as the only backstop.

Status: open

### SI-16 — Agent-supplied check names are unbounded metric labels, written with Go %q escaping (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/metrics_handler.go:60`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** pglensCheckErrorTotal and pglensCheckOKTotal are keyed by the check name the agent supplies (pipeline.go:340-342, IncCheckError(r.Check)), with no validation against the known check set. Every distinct name adds a map entry that is never removed. The exposition at metrics_handler.go:60 formats labels with %q (Go string quoting), not Prometheus label escaping. A name containing a control character produces escapes that Prometheus text parsers reject, which fails the whole /metrics scrape. /metrics is unauthenticated by design (README.md:329), so the names are reachable by anyone who can read the endpoint.

**Failure scenario:** A host pushes envelopes with random check names. Memory and /metrics output grow without bound. A name containing a newline or a 0x01 byte makes Prometheus reject the entire scrape.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/metrics_handler.go:60 `_, _ = fmt.Fprintf(w, "%s{%s=%q} %v\n", name, labelName, k, vals[k])`; internal/server/pipeline.go:340 `IncCheckError(r.Check)`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Mechanism verified, but the finding's escaping example is partly wrong, and severity is raised. There is no check-name validation: the wire package exposes no Result validation (go doc ./internal/wire), and both IncCheckError(r.Check) at pipeline.go:340-342 and the processInstanceNoDB path (pipeline.go:849-851) accept any name. pglensCheckErrorTotal and pglensCheckOKTotal are plain unbounded maps (counterVec with make(map)), so every distinct name adds a permanent entry. /metrics is exempt from the credential gate (sessionRequestExempt returns true for non-/api/ paths; README.md:329 documents this), so anyone who can read it sees the names. Growth needs a holder of the bootstrap token, since Upsert must accept the instance first. Severity raised from low to medium because one credential can grow server memory without bound, and a single malformed name breaks the unauthenticated scrape for everyone. The finding's newline example is wrong: %q renders a newline as backslash-n, which Prometheus accepts. Tab and 0x01 are the failing cases.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway test in internal/server that calls writeVecLines (metrics_handler.go:53-62) with one name at a time and checks each output line against the Prometheus label-escape rule (only backslash-backslash, backslash-quote and backslash-n are valid). Output: name line-break emitted check=backslash-quote-n escape ok=true; name tab-name emitted backslash-t ok=false (invalid escape); name ctrl-0x01 emitted backslash-x01 ok=false (invalid escape); quote and plain names ok=true. github.com/prometheus/common/expfmt could not be imported because go.sum lacks it, so the rule was checked by a local implementation of the documented text-format escape rule. Test file deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Accept only check names from the known registry and bucket others under one label value. Use Prometheus label escaping (backslash, double quote, newline) instead of %q.

**Fix notes:** Fix both call sites: pipeline.go:340-342 and the processInstanceNoDB path around pipeline.go:849-851. The escape must follow Prometheus rules (backslash, double quote, newline only), and other control characters need dropping or replacing, not %q. Bounding is the real fix: the server has no check registry (checks live in internal/check on the agent side), so either use a fixed allowlist of known check names bucketed under one label value, or cap the number of distinct label values.

Status: open

### SI-23 — Per-result timestamps are not bounded; a forward clock step blacks out counter rates (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/pipeline.go:447`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Only env.SentAt is checked (ingest.go:114), and that check is one-sided: a future SentAt passes. Per-result timestamps r.TS are used directly as the delta observation timestamp (pipeline.go:447) and are never compared with server time. If an agent clock steps forward (NTP correction, VM resume), its samples carry future timestamps. The delta engine stores that timestamp as the baseline (engine.go:85), and Rule 2 (engine.go:90-91) then drops every real-time sample until wall clock passes the stored future value. Evict cuts by sample timestamp, so a future baseline is never evicted. Very old r.TS values, which the 12h check on SentAt does not catch, are written into chunks that retention and compression already handled (migrations 0003).

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** An agent clock jumps forward two hours for three minutes, then corrects. Samples in that window carry real time plus two hours, and the baseline becomes T+2h. For the next two hours every real sample is dropped by Rule 2: counter-based rate series are empty and no counter_reset events fire.

**Correction (from verification):** The real samples after the clock correction (B+4m, B+5m, B+6m) are absent.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/ingest.go:114 `if time.Since(env.SentAt) > maxSampleAge {`; internal/server/pipeline.go:447 `TS:         r.TS,`; internal/delta/engine.go:85 `e.prev[o.Key] = state{ts: o.TS, value: o.Value, statsReset: cp}`; internal/delta/engine.go:90-91 `if !o.TS.After(prev.ts) {` / `return nil, nil`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The main claim is confirmed by code and by a repro. ingest.go:114 checks only time.Since(env.SentAt) > maxSampleAge, so a future SentAt passes. r.TS is the agent clock (run.go:223 uses clk.Now()) and goes straight into delta.Observe (pipeline.go:445-451). engine.go:90-91 (Rule 2) returns nil,nil before any baseline update, so a future baseline blocks every real-time sample until wall clock passes it. Evict (engine.go:125-136) compares s.ts against the cutoff, so a future baseline is never evicted. The repro shows the stored counter rate points are only at B+1m and B+2h3m. The real samples after the clock correction (B+4m, B+5m, B+6m) are absent. The blackout lasts as long as the forward step. The second half of the claim is NOT substantiated. The agent stamps each result at scrape time (run.go:223) and SentAt at queue time (run.go:409). Pending results are flushed on every push tick (run.go:262-273), so r.TS is never older than SentAt by more than a flush interval in normal operation. Reaching r.TS older than 12h with a fresh SentAt would need a backward agent clock step undone within one push interval; no normal path produces it. Migration 0003's comment documents the intended 6h buffer / 12h / 48h ordering. Severity medium is right: an edge case with a real blackout affecting every counter series of that instance.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test TestReviewSI23_ForwardStepBlacksOutRates against a throwaway local container pglens-review-si22-24-a1 (timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17, bound to 127.0.0.1:55433, removed afterwards). Command: PGLENS_REVIEW_DSN='postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:55433/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI23 -count=1 -v. Drives the real Pipeline.Process (pool path, store.Migrate applied) with one counter series: B+0 1000, B+1m 1060, agent clock forward B+2h2m 1120 and B+2h3m 1180, corrected real samples B+4m 1240, B+5m 1300, B+6m 1360. Output: stored rate point ts offset 1m0s; stored rate point ts offset 2h3m0s; stored rate points: 2. PASS.
```

**Suggested fix:** Reject or clamp r.TS outside a window around server receive time (for example plus or minus maxSampleAge, or TransmittedAt plus or minus the skew threshold). When a sample jumps forward or backward by more than a threshold, reset that key's baseline instead of dropping every later sample.

**Fix notes:** Rule 2 (engine.go:90-91) is the duplicate and out-of-order guard. It returns before any baseline update, so a future baseline is never corrected. A fix must treat a large backward jump (for example more than maxGap behind prev.ts) as a clock step and rebase the state, not skip the sample. Alternatively, clamp or reject r.TS against TransmittedAt (available only after ingest.go:122) before delta.Observe at pipeline.go:445-451. The same Observe call is also in processInstanceNoDB (pipeline.go:874-880), so both paths need the fix. Evict (engine.go:125-136) keeps future baselines, so it needs no change. Drop the 'very old r.TS' half of the finding, or mark it speculative, since the normal flow does not produce it (run.go:223, run.go:262-273, run.go:409).

Status: open

### SA-02 — Command poll trusts a client-declared agent header; any bootstrap-token holder can read any agent's queue (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/commands.go:258`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** authenticatedAgent takes the agent identity from the request header X-PGLENS-Agent-ID (fallback X-Agent-ID at line 241). poll only checks that this header equals the agent_id in the URL (line 258 returns 403 on mismatch). The bootstrap token used for this route is shared by all agents, so it proves no per-agent identity. result (commands.go:354) accepts the same token plus claim_token.

**Failure scenario:** A holder of the shared bootstrap token (any agent host, or a leaked agent config) sends GET .../agents/<victim>/commands with X-PGLENS-Agent-ID: <victim>. The server returns the victim's queued commands and the attacker can post results for them. The header is attacker-controlled, so the check proves nothing.

**Evidence:**

```text
commands.go:241 agentID = r.Header.Get("X-Agent-ID"); commands.go:258 writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "forbidden", "agent may only poll its own queue"). Overlay test: honest header returns 204; header set to the victim agent id on the victim URL returns 204; a mismatching header returns 403.
```

**Verification reasoning:** authenticatedAgent (commands.go ~236-246) takes identity from the client header X-PGLENS-Agent-ID (fallback X-Agent-ID). poll (~250-258) only compares that header to the URL agent_id. The single bootstrap token (LoadBootstrapToken: one agent bearer token for all agents) passes Auth.Validate. Repro confirms: a forged header equal to the victim URL id yields 204 and the claim UPDATE runs with the victim agent_id. result (~341) checks only the bootstrap token plus claim_token, and claim_token is minted by claim (gen_random_uuid()), so a forged claim lets the caller post results. Severity lowered from high: the attack needs the victim's agent_id UUID, a v4 value that lives on the victim host. I checked every reachable read path and none discloses another agent's UUID: instance list and detail (no agent_id), cluster response (clusterInstanceResp), events payloads from staleness.go and inventory.go (instance_id only), alert subjects (instance_id), command-audit, and OpenAPI response schemas (agent_id appears only in the push request body). The root gap is real (identity is not bound to a credential), and ingest has the same shape: ingest.go trusts env.AgentID under the shared token, with only revocation checked per agent, so a header-only fix does not close the class.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go test in internal/server (deleted afterwards): NewCommandService over a recording mockPool (the existing scripted mock, wrapped to record QueryRow args), NewAuth('shared-bootstrap'), chi router with RegisterRoutes. Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA02PollTrustsHeader -v ./internal/server/ . Decisive output: 'SA02 forged header equal to victim URL id, bootstrap token only: status=204 body=""'; 'SA02 no identity header: status=403 ... agent identity header is required'; 'SA02 header of other agent on victim URL: status=403 ... agent may only poll its own queue'; 'SA02 claim QueryRow[0] args (tenant, agent_id)=[default <victim uuid>]'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Issue a per-agent credential at enrollment and derive the agent identity from that credential server-side. Stop reading identity from request headers, and reject a credential/agent_id mismatch. Update openapi securitySchemes accordingly.

**Fix notes:** Bind identity to a per-agent credential issued at enrollment, not to a request header; reject a credential and agent_id mismatch in authenticatedAgent and poll (commands.go). The same change is needed on ingest (ingest.go and inventory.go Upsert, which take env.AgentID under the shared token), otherwise the header fix alone leaves the class open. poll does not check that agent_id exists, so unknown UUIDs get 204 and no existence oracle is exposed.

Status: open

### SA-04 — updateRule is a read-modify-write without a transaction or version check (lost update) (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_alerts.go:257`

**Category:** race · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** updateRule first reads the rule, then writes every column with a full-row UPDATE (line 257) with no transaction, row lock, or updated_at precondition. Two concurrent PUTs on the same rule can each overwrite fields the other changed.

**Failure scenario:** Operator A disables a rule and operator B changes its threshold at nearly the same time. Whichever write lands second restores the other's field from its stale read, and both requests return 200.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_alerts.go:207-262: the handler decodes the body (216) and then runs UPDATE alert_rules SET enabled=$1,severity=$2,threshold=$3,for_seconds=$4,updated_at=now() WHERE rule_id=$5 (257), using values from the earlier read and request. No WHERE on updated_at and no 409 path.
```

**Verification reasoning:** updateRule (api_alerts.go ~207-262) does a plain SELECT (no lock, no transaction), then a full-row UPDATE of enabled, severity, threshold and for_seconds from that stale read, with no updated_at precondition and no 409 path. Migrations 0006 and 0013 define no trigger or guard on alert_rules. The barrier repro shows the lost update: two concurrent PUTs both read enabled=true, threshold=0.5, and each UPDATE writes all four columns from its own read. Whichever lands last reverts the other's field, and both return 200. Severity: the rubric lists race under high, but I kept medium because the window is one SELECT-to-UPDATE gap, it needs two concurrent operator edits of the same tier-1 rule, and only rule configuration is affected with no corruption of other data. The orchestrator may override to high under the rubric's race category.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go test in internal/server (deleted afterwards): zzBarrierPool wraps the mockPool, with a barrier that holds both requests after their QueryRow until both have read. Two PUT /api/v1/alert-rules/replica.lag_high requests run concurrently, with bodies {"enabled":false} and {"threshold":0.9}. Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA04RuleLostUpdate -v ./internal/server/ . Decisive output: 'SA04 both PUT status codes=[200 200]'; 'SA04 UPDATE[0] args (enabled,severity,threshold,for_seconds,rule_id)=[false warning 0.5 120 replica.lag_high]'; 'SA04 UPDATE[1] args (...)=[true warning 0.9 120 replica.lag_high]'. The second UPDATE restores enabled=true and the first restores threshold=0.5, so either order loses one edit.
```

**Suggested fix:** Make the update a single statement with per-field COALESCE from the request, or lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction. Optionally require an If-Match/updated_at precondition and return 409 on mismatch.

**Fix notes:** Make the write one statement with COALESCE per field, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction. The response body currently echoes the stale values from the read, so return RETURNING values instead. An If-Match or updated_at precondition with 409 is optional.

Status: open

### SA-06 — Settings drift misses asymmetric drift on non-allowlisted settings (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_settings.go:160`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** handleSettingsDrift builds drift only from rows that each instance shipped in its latest scrape (query lines 120-130) and skips any setting with fewer than two rows (line 160). The check ships a non-allowlisted setting only when its value differs from the boot value (internal/check/settings.go:105-107). A setting changed on one instance and left at default on the others therefore produces one row and is never reported.

**Failure scenario:** In a 3-node cluster, the primary sets work_mem (not allowlisted) and both standbys keep the default. The drift endpoint and the config.drift advisor rule report nothing, so the divergence stays hidden.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_settings.go:160: if len(values) < 2 || allDriftValuesEqual(values) { continue }. internal/check/settings.go:105-107 ships non-allowlisted settings only when s.setting != s.bootVal.
```

**Verification reasoning:** handleSettingsDrift (api_settings.go ~160) skips any setting with fewer than two shipped rows. check/settings.go ships non-allowlisted settings only when setting differs from boot_val (lines ~105-107), so a non-allowlisted setting changed on one member and left at default elsewhere produces one row and is never reported. Repro confirms: a single primary row returns []; a control with a differing standby row returns the drift. The advisor config.drift rule (advisor/rules_config.go) loops over the instance's own keys and skips any sibling missing the key, so it has the same gap. The finding's example is wrong: work_mem IS in settingsAllowlist (check/settings.go), so every member ships it and drift on work_mem is reported. The gap applies to non-allowlisted settings such as log_min_duration_statement.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go test in internal/server (deleted afterwards): zzRecPool with queryResults holding drift-query rows (key, value_text, instance_id, role, context), served through registerSettingsRoutes. Case A: only a primary row for log_min_duration_statement='500' (user context). Case B control: primary '500' plus standby '-1'. Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA06AsymmetricDrift -v ./internal/server/ . Decisive output: 'SA06 only-primary-ships: status=200 body=[]'; 'SA06 both-ship-differing: status=200 body=[{"name":"log_min_duration_statement","values":[{...primary..."value":"500"},{...standby..."value":"-1"}]}]'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compare against the full member set: for each setting, treat an instance without a row as its boot/default value (ship the boot value or a presence flag from the agent), and report drift when any member differs.

**Fix notes:** The agent has to ship boot_val or a presence/default flag, because the server cannot infer a standby's default from a missing row. Pitfall: boot_val differs across PostgreSQL majors, so treating a missing row as default in a mixed-version cluster would create false drift. Change config.drift in advisor/rules_config.go in lockstep, since it shares DriftExcludedSettings.

Status: open

### SA-08 — Replication and slots endpoints have no range or point cap and an unbounded per-slot subquery (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_topology.go:211`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** handleReplication (api_topology.go:211-390) accepts any range and point count with no cap. handleSlots (api_topology.go:543-595) runs a correlated subquery per inactive slot that scans instance history with no time bound.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A large cluster with many inactive slots and months of history makes /slots cost O(slots x history) and /replication return an unbounded series, risking the WriteTimeout and DB load.

**Correction (from verification):** CORRECTION to the finding: both handlers wrap the query in context.WithTimeout(5s) (lines 259 and 554), so the failure is a 500 after about 5s of DB work, not a WriteTimeout (cmd/pglens-server/main.go:155-156 sets 2 minutes).

**Evidence:**

```text
api_topology.go:211 handleReplication and :543 handleSlots; the correlated subquery is in handleSlots lines ~543-595 with no time predicate.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code confirmed in the worktree. handleReplication (internal/server/api_topology.go ~211-390) checks only from<to (lines 245-248) and has no step parameter and no point cap; handleMetricsQuery caps points at maxMetricPoints=10000 (api.go:734-744), replication has no equivalent. handleSlots (api_topology.go ~543-595) runs a correlated subquery in the CASE ELSE branch (lines 562-565: SELECT max(h.ts) FROM metrics_replication h WHERE instance_id, slot_name, slot_active) with no ts bound; only the outer DISTINCT ON carries a 5-minute bound (line 571). CORRECTION to the finding: both handlers wrap the query in context.WithTimeout(5s) (lines 259 and 554), so the failure is a 500 after about 5s of DB work, not a WriteTimeout (cmd/pglens-server/main.go:155-156 sets 2 minutes). History is bounded by the 30-day retention policy (migrations/0003_policies.sql:37), not unbounded. Realistic trigger: the web polls useClusterReplication and useClusterSlots every 15s (web/src/api/policy.ts cluster interval 15_000; queries.ts:168-200), and LagSection.tsx:84-87 offers ranges up to 30 days, about 170k rows per series per edge per poll. The only index on metrics_replication is the dedup index (instance_id, COALESCE(upstream_id,...), slot_name, ts) from migrations/0002_hypertables.sql:74-76; the slot subquery omits upstream_id, so it can seek only on instance_id and scans that instance's retained history. Not benchmarked.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only (no benchmark, per reviewer guidance). Decisive lines: api_topology.go:245-248 (only from<to validated), :259 and :554 (5s context timeouts), :562-565 (subquery without ts bound), :571 (5-minute bound on outer query only); api.go:734-744 (metrics cap for contrast); web/src/features/cluster/LagSection.tsx:84-87 (30-day range offered); migrations/0003_policies.sql:37 (30-day retention); migrations/0002_hypertables.sql:74-76 (dedup index shape).
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the same range and point limits used by metrics, and rewrite the slot subquery as one set-based query (DISTINCT ON or LATERAL) with a time bound on the instance history.

**Fix notes:** /replication has no step parameter. A plain 'apply the metrics cap' would make the UI's 7d and 30d views return 422. The fix needs server-side time_bucket downsampling with a step or bucket parameter, default-on for large ranges. For the slot subquery, add a time bound equal to or shorter than retention, or better, keep last_active_at as state, or rewrite as LATERAL ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 1 keyed on the full dedup prefix. A bound equal to the 30-day retention does not reduce the cost much.

### SA-09 — Cluster list issues about 8 queries per cluster (N+1) (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:270`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** handleClusters loops over clusters and, for each one, queries instances, topology edges (api.go:385), sync states via loadStandbyResolver (api_topology.go:403, called from api_topology.go:470), and the max replay lag. That is roughly 8 round trips per cluster on the dashboard's most-hit endpoint. handleInstances (api.go:521) is also unpaginated.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** With 50 clusters the list endpoint issues about 400 queries per refresh, and latency grows linearly with the number of clusters.

**Correction (from verification):** handleInstances (api.go:521-557) has one query and no limit; that sub-claim is minor.

**Evidence:**

```text
api.go:270 handleClusters; api.go:385 topology query inside the loop; api_topology.go:262 and :470 call loadStandbyResolver per cluster; api.go:497 sets MaxReplayLagSeconds per cluster.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Query count verified by reading. handleClusters (internal/server/api.go:270-505) runs per cluster: the instances query (api.go:314), the topology_edges query (api.go:384), currentSyncStates (api_topology.go:469), which calls loadStandbyResolver (api_topology.go:403-462, three queries: instances names, topology_edges, sender names) and then its own sync-state query (line 474), and the max-lag QueryRow (api.go:466). That is 7 round trips per cluster plus 1 for the cluster list, so 7N+1 (N=50 gives 351, not 'about 400'). Instances and topology_edges are each fetched twice per cluster (api.go and loadStandbyResolver). Every query is cluster-indexed or time-bounded, so the cost is round-trip latency, not scan cost. Unlike handleReplication, handleSlots and handleEvents, handleClusters has no context.WithTimeout, so a slow DB is bounded only by the 2-minute server WriteTimeout. The fleet and cluster views poll every 15s (web/src/api/policy.ts). handleInstances (api.go:521-557) has one query and no limit; that sub-claim is minor. No benchmark run.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only. Decisive lines: api.go:314, :384, :466, :496-498; api_topology.go:262 and :470 (loadStandbyResolver called per cluster via currentSyncStates); api_topology.go:409, :428, :444, :474 (the query list); api.go:271 (r.Context() with no timeout); web/src/api/policy.ts lines 2-3 (15_000 polling).
```

**Suggested fix:** Batch the per-cluster queries with ANY($1) over the cluster id set and build the maps in Go. Add limit/cursor pagination to handleInstances.

**Fix notes:** Batch across clusters: one instances query (ORDER BY cluster_id, addr, port) grouped in Go, one topology_edges query, one standby-resolver set, one sync-state query and one max-lag query with GROUP BY cluster_id. The duplicate instances and topology_edges fetches come from loadStandbyResolver re-reading what handleClusters already loaded, so pass the loaded data in. Add context.WithTimeout like the sibling handlers. Pagination for handleInstances is optional and minor.
