### CI-08 — Checkpointer check never reads stats_reset, so counter resets lose their hint (CONFIRMED, checks-instance)

**Location:** `internal/check/checkpointer.go:35`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Neither the pg_stat_checkpointer (PG 17+) nor the pg_stat_bgwriter (PG 15-16) branch reads stats_reset, and the Result has no StatsReset. Sibling checks such as archiver.go:52 and database_stats.go:99-105 do set it, so the delta engine has no explicit reset signal for these counters.

**Failure scenario:** After pg_stat_reset_shared('bgwriter') or ('checkpointer'), if the counters exceed their pre-reset values by the next 30 s scrape, the delta engine's stats-changed rule never fires and the went-backwards rule does not either. One wrong rate point is emitted for that interval.

**Evidence:**

```text
checkpointer.go:36 reads num_timed, num_requested, write_time, sync_time with no stats_reset; checkpointer.go:41 and :46 do the same for pg_stat_bgwriter; the returned Result (checkpointer.go:50-58) has no StatsReset field. Verified stats_reset presence: pg_stat_bgwriter has it on 15-19; pg_stat_checkpointer has it on 17, 18 and 19 only.
```

**Verification reasoning:** internal/check/checkpointer.go never sets Result.StatsReset in either branch (PG17+ pg_stat_checkpointer at lines 35-39, PG15-16 pg_stat_bgwriter at lines 41-45); the returned Result (lines 50-58) has no StatsReset. The agent forwards check.Result.StatsReset unchanged (internal/agent/scheduler.go:354), and the server applies r.StatsReset to every counter metric of the result (internal/server/pipeline.go:445-449). delta.Engine rule 3 fires only when both the previous and the current StatsReset are non-nil (internal/delta/engine.go:95), so a nil value gives no reset hint. Reproduced: no hint, values 3 then 5 thirty seconds apart, gives Point rate 0.0667/s and no event; with a non-nil StatsReset at t0+10s on the second observation and a non-nil first observation, it gives stats_reset_changed. The stats_reset column facts hold on real servers: pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset exists on PG15 and PG17/19; pg_stat_checkpointer.stats_reset exists on PG17 and PG19rc1. On PG17, pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer') moved only pg_stat_checkpointer.stats_reset and left pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset unchanged. The impact is narrow: a manual reset plus a counter that climbs past its pre-reset value within one 30 s scrape, which yields one wrong rate point.

**Repro:**

```text
Read internal/check/checkpointer.go:35-58 (no StatsReset assignment). Temporary Go test in internal/check (deleted): scrapeCheckpointerForTest(t, pgtype.PG16) and (t, pgtype.PG17) both report Result.StatsReset=<nil>. Temporary delta test: Observe{t0,3,nil} then Observe{t0+30s,5,nil} gives Point Rate=0.0666 Event=nil; with StatsReset=t0+10s on the second observation and non-nil on the first, Point=nil Event=stats_reset_changed. Throwaway container: docker run postgres:17.11-alpine, then psql: SELECT pg_stat_reset_shared('checkpointer') moved pg_stat_checkpointer.stats_reset from 01:05:40 to 01:06:01 while pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset stayed 01:05:40. The PG15 and PG19rc1 containers confirmed the column lists above.
```

**Suggested fix:** Read stats_reset in each branch and set Result.StatsReset. On 17+ use the later of pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset and pg_stat_checkpointer.stats_reset, since both views feed this result. On 15-16 use pg_stat_bgwriter.stats_reset.

**Fix notes:** Result.StatsReset is one value shared by every counter in the result (pipeline.go:445-449). Taking the later of the two views' stats_reset values would therefore make a reset of one view register as stats_reset_changed for the other view's counters as well: on PG17 a checkpointer-only reset moves only pg_stat_checkpointer.stats_reset, so max() would drop and skip one valid point for each bgwriter counter and emit a spurious counter_reset_detected event. The fix needs per-view reset handling (for example, separate results per view, or a per-metric reset), not a single max. Remember that the first sample after the fix has no prior StatsReset, so the engine treats it as rule 1.

Status: open

### CI-09 — ApplySessionLimits doc says SET LOCAL but the code issues session-level SET (CONFIRMED, checks-instance)

**Location:** `internal/check/check.go:134`

**Category:** docs · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The doc comment says the function sets timeouts via SET LOCAL. The body explicitly uses session-level SET and its own comment says SET LOCAL would be rejected. The settings persist on pooled connections, so a later borrower inherits them.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A maintainer wraps a check in a transaction assuming SET LOCAL scoping, or assumes the timeouts are reset after use. A later on-demand command on the same pooled connection then runs under the previous check's 2 s statement timeout unless it reapplies its own limits.

**Correction (from verification):** The failure scenario is overstated.

**Evidence:**

```text
check.go:134: "// ApplySessionLimits sets per-check timeouts via SET LOCAL."; check.go:140-146 issue SET statement_timeout, SET lock_timeout = '1s', SET idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '30s' on the connection. The pooled connections in internal/agent/conn.go:154-167 (Shared) and :174-238 (ForDatabase) keep these settings after release.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The doc comment at internal/check/check.go:134 says SET LOCAL, but the body (lines 140-146) issues session-level SET statements, and the existing unit test TestApplySessionLimits_Happy asserts exactly those SET statements. The comment's rationale is also wrong: PostgreSQL does not reject SET LOCAL outside a transaction. It emits a WARNING and has no effect, which I reproduced on PG17. The settings do persist on the pooled session. The failure scenario is overstated. Shared (internal/agent/conn.go:163) and ForDatabase (conn.go:234) reapply ApplySessionLimits with 30 s on every borrow, so a later borrower through those paths gets a fresh limit, not the previous check's 2 s. ExplainExecutor (internal/agent/exec_explain.go:32, 89-97) uses ConnFor and sets its own SET LOCAL inside BEGIN READ ONLY. The only path that inherits the previous limits is DedicatedConn (conn.go:141-151, which sets application_name only), used by the ASH sampler, and the sampler bounds each query with its own 500 ms context (internal/ash/sampler.go:176), so an inherited statement_timeout does not bind it in practice. The doc drift itself is real, so it stays CONFIRMED at low.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway postgres:17.11-alpine container, one psql session: SET statement_timeout = 2000 then SHOW statement_timeout gave 2s; SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '3s' outside a transaction gave 'WARNING: SET LOCAL can only be used in transaction blocks' and SHOW still gave 2s. Code: check.go:134 comment versus check.go:140-146 SET statements; TestApplySessionLimits_Happy in check_test.go asserts the SET statements. Inheritance check: conn.go:163 and conn.go:234 reapply limits; conn.go:141-151 (DedicatedConn) does not.
```

**Suggested fix:** Correct the doc comment to say the settings are session-level and persist on the pooled connection. Optionally reset them on release.

**Fix notes:** Correct the comment at check.go:134 to say session-level SET, and rewrite the rationale comment at check.go:137-139: SET LOCAL outside a transaction is a no-op with a WARNING, not a rejection (verified on PG17). Do not claim a reset-on-release is needed for Shared or ForDatabase, because they reapply 30 s on every borrow. The only real inheritance is DedicatedConn (conn.go:141-151), which does not call ApplySessionLimits. ExplainExecutor's BEGIN READ ONLY plus SET LOCAL (exec_explain.go:89-97) is the correct transactional pattern and should not be changed to match.

Status: open

### CI-10 — Ages and uptime mix the agent clock with database timestamps (CONFIRMED, checks-instance)

**Location:** `internal/check/archiver.go:58`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** archiver and instance_info compute ages and uptime as agent-clock now minus a database timestamp, while activity and locks compute them with the database now(). Clock skew between the agent host and the database therefore biases these values, and nonNegativeAge clamps a database-ahead result to 0, hiding the skew.

**Failure scenario:** An agent host five minutes behind the database understates pg_archiver_last_archived_age_seconds by five minutes, so archive.stalled fires late. An agent five minutes ahead produces a false stall. pg_uptime_seconds is off by the same amount.

**Evidence:**

```text
archiver.go:58 now := t.Clock().Now(); archiver.go:120-126 nonNegativeAge returns 0 for negative differences; instance_info.go:65 and :69 pass t.Clock().Now() into buildInstanceInfoResult; instance_info.go:73 uptime := now.Sub(startTime). activity.go:46-47 uses now() on the database.
```

**Verification reasoning:** archiver.go:58 computes ages as t.Clock().Now() minus a database timestamp (lines 59-64 use nonNegativeAge, lines 120-126). instance_info.go:65 and :69 pass t.Clock().Now() into buildInstanceInfoResult, and line 73 computes uptime from it. activity.go:46-47 and locks.go:77-78 use database now(). Manager.Clock() returns the process clock passed to NewManager (internal/agent/conn.go:824-826), not a database-synchronised clock, so the skew is real whenever the agent host and the database clock differ. Reproduced with clock.WithOffset: the archiver's pg_archiver_last_archived_age_seconds reads 10.0 at offset 0, 310.0 at +5 minutes, and 0.0 at -5 minutes (clamped, where the true age is about 10 s). pg_uptime_seconds for a true uptime of 3600 s reads 3600, 3900, and 3300. The effect needs a real clock divergence between agent and database, which NTP-synced hosts rarely have, so it stays low.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go test in internal/check (deleted) using SimpleTarget.ClockValue = clock.WithOffset(clock.System(), off) with a database-side last_archived_time of now minus 10 s: archiver pg_archiver_last_archived_age_seconds = 10.0 (off 0), 310.0 (off +5m), 0.0 (off -5m). instance_info with start now minus 1 h: pg_uptime_seconds = 3600 (off 0), 3900 (off +5m), 3300 (off -5m). Code: internal/agent/conn.go:824-826 (Clock returns m.clock).
```

**Suggested fix:** Compute the ages and uptime in SQL with the database clock (for example EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - last_archived_time) and now() - pg_postmaster_start_time()), as activity.go already does.

**Fix notes:** Moving to SQL now() means the archiver must select the age expression in the same statement (archiver.go:47 and the metric at lines 59-64), and instance_info must use EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - pg_postmaster_start_time()) (instance_info.go:37, 73). After that change, nonNegativeAge (archiver.go:120-126) would guard only tiny negatives, and the tests in archiver_test.go and instance_info_test.go that feed timestamps through ClockValue would need to feed ages instead. Keep the ages nullable: archiver ages are only emitted when the timestamp is non-null.

Status: open

### CI-11 — Lock-tree snapshot ships every client backend every 10 s (CONFIRMED, checks-instance)

**Location:** `internal/check/locks.go:120`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Every client backend, with up to 2048 bytes of query text, is appended to the sessions list and marshalled into the lock_tree fact on every scrape, even when nothing is blocked. The payload grows linearly with the connection count and is not marked Partial.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** At 1,000 or more backends, each 10 s scrape ships several hundred KB per instance, and the server stores a lock snapshot each cycle. This is scrape and storage cost paid even when no lock is held.

**Correction (from verification):** The finding's storage wording is overstated.

**Evidence:**

```text
locks.go:120: sessions = append(sessions, lockNode(r)) for every row; locks.go:105: query truncated to 2048 bytes; locks.go:182: json.Marshal(lockTree{... Sessions: sessions}) on every scrape. Measured on PG 19: a two-session snapshot was 614 bytes, about 300 bytes per backend.
```

**Verification reasoning:** locks.go:120 appends every client backend to sessions, and locks.go:182 marshals the full tree on every scrape even when nothing is blocked. The result is not marked Partial, which I confirmed by measurement. The payload growth is real: about 260 bytes per backend, so about 260 KB per scrape at 1000 backends, and about 2.27 MB when each backend carries a 2048-byte query. The finding's storage wording is overstated. lock_snapshots is a single upserted row per (tenant, instance) (internal/store/write.go:529-532, DELETE older than 15 minutes plus INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), so storage does not grow. The cost is an agent-to-server bandwidth cost plus a per-cycle JSONB rewrite that causes WAL and TOAST churn. The API serves sessions verbatim (internal/server/api_locks.go:84-85), so bounding the list changes an API contract.

**Repro:**

```text

Storage: internal/store/write.go:529-532 (single-row upsert per instance). The temporary test and its package file were deleted.

### CR-11 — Unreserved slot reports a negative safe_wal_size gauge (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_slots.go:105`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** safe_wal_size is emitted whenever it is non-NULL (lines 105-112). For a slot with NULL restart_lsn, wal_status is NULL and the check reports it as 'unknown', but safe_wal_size is still emitted.

**Failure scenario:** A slot that reserves no WAL shows a negative safe-WAL margin, which reads as already over the limit. Alerts or UI keyed on the margin raise a false critical.

**Evidence:**

```text
Live on PG17 with max_slot_wal_keep_size=32MB: slot sl_unreserved (restart_lsn NULL, status 'unknown') reported safe_wal_size 28339240, then -36340408 after about 60000 rows of WAL.
```

**Verification reasoning:** replication_slots.go emits replication_slot_safe_wal_size_bytes whenever SafeWALSize is non-NULL. The query coalesces wal_status to 'unknown' but not safe_wal_size. Live on PostgreSQL 17.11 (max_slot_wal_keep_size=32MB): a physical slot created without immediate reservation has restart_lsn NULL, wal_status NULL and safe_wal_size 27532616; after about 120 MB of WAL the value is -117440760 with status 'unknown' and retained_bytes 0. Consumers: pipeline applyReplicationMetric stores slot_safe_wal_size_bytes (negative kept); internal/server/api_topology.go handleSlots returns it raw; web SlotsSection.tsx renders it with formatBytes under 'WAL before invalidation', so the UI shows about '-112.0 MiB'. The alert scenario does not occur today: alert/source_sql.go metricTable rejects any pg_replication_* name not in replicationColumns, so no rule can key on the margin. The impact is a misleading display for a slot that retains nothing, hence low.

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-verif-cr-7k2q (postgres:17.11-alpine). SELECT pg_create_physical_replication_slot('sl_unreserved'); then the verbatim slot query: safe_wal_size 27532616, wal_status unknown, restart_lsn NULL. Then INSERT INTO cr11_big SELECT g, repeat('x',800) FROM generate_series(1,150000) g; SELECT pg_switch_wal(); CHECKPOINT; re-run the verbatim query: safe_wal_size -117440760, wal_status unknown, retained_bytes 0.
```

**Suggested fix:** Emit safe_wal_size only when restart_lsn IS NOT NULL, and clamp it at 0 otherwise.

**Fix notes:** Emit replication_slot_safe_wal_size_bytes only when restart_lsn IS NOT NULL (add it to the agent query or a CASE), not merely when non-NULL. UI caution: SlotsSection.tsx renders a NULL safe size as 'Unlimited' (or 'None: required WAL already lost' for status lost), so simply dropping the value would show 'Unlimited' for an unreserved slot. Use a distinct representation for 'not reserved'. Clamping to 0 would read as no margin left, the misreading the existing NULL comment in replication_slots.go warns about.

### CR-12 — Other sessions' temp tables are reported as user tables (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/table_stats.go:61`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The query filters only on relkind='r'. pg_stat_user_tables (verified via pg_get_viewdef) excludes only pg_catalog, information_schema and pg_toast, so pg_temp_N relations are included. bloat_estimate.sql:30 already excludes relpersistence='t', so the two checks disagree.

**Failure scenario:** Short-lived temp tables take up the top-N budget and create series labelled pg_temp_N.<name> that never recur. Their drops can also trigger CR-02.

**Evidence:**

```text
Live on PG17: a temp table in another session appeared as pg_temp_35|tmp_probe in pg_stat_user_tables, and the verbatim table_stats output included a pg_temp row.
```

**Verification reasoning:** table_stats.go filters only c.relkind = 'r' over pg_stat_user_tables joined to pg_class. pg_get_viewdef on PostgreSQL 17 shows pg_stat_user_tables excludes only pg_catalog, information_schema and ^pg_toast, so pg_temp_N schemas pass. The same FROM/WHERE returned another session's temp table as pg_temp_12.tmp_probe (relkind r, relpersistence t). Nothing downstream filters it: store/write.go and pipeline.go write every table row. bloat_estimate.sql:30 already has c.relpersistence <> 't', so the two checks disagree as stated. Consequence: temp tables compete for the top-N budget and produce series labelled pg_temp_N. The linkage to CR-02 was not verified (not in this batch).

**Repro:**

```text
Container pglens-review-verif-cr-7k2q. Session A: CREATE TEMP TABLE tmp_probe(id int); INSERT ...; SELECT pg_sleep(12) in the background. Session B after 4 seconds: SELECT s.schemaname, s.relname, c.relkind, c.relpersistence FROM pg_stat_user_tables s JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = s.relid WHERE c.relkind = 'r' returned 'pg_temp_12 | tmp_probe | r | t' alongside public tables. pg_get_viewdef('pg_stat_user_tables') shows WHERE schemaname <> ALL(ARRAY['pg_catalog','information_schema']) AND schemaname !~ '^pg_toast'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add AND c.relpersistence <> 't' (or exclude schemaname LIKE 'pg_temp%') to the WHERE clause.

**Fix notes:** Add AND c.relpersistence <> 't' to the table_stats WHERE clause, matching bloat_estimate.sql:30. Prefer relpersistence over a schema-name test, since pg_temp schema names are per backend. Excluding temp relations also keeps them out of presentRelations and the relation prune set, so no separate handling is needed.

### CR-13 — def_hash lowercases literals, so predicates differing only in literal case collide (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/index_stats.go:128`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** hashNormalizedDefinition applies strings.ToLower to the whole normalized text, including string literals in predicates. The advisor's index.duplicate groups on DefHash (rules_relation.go:141-170) and reports 'share a definition'.

**Failure scenario:** Two partial indexes whose predicates differ only in literal case are reported as duplicates. Following the advice (after validation) drops a needed index.

**Evidence:**

```text
Ran the verbatim function: WHERE (status = 'ACTIVE') and WHERE (status = 'active') hash equal (equal=true). Quoted-column case ('Name' versus name) does not collide.
```

**Verification reasoning:** index_stats.go hashNormalizedDefinition takes def[start:end+1], from the first '(' to the last ')', and lowercases it with strings.ToLower, so quoted literals are folded too. The hash is emitted as the index_def fact label def_hash (index_stats.go), loaded by advisor/snapshot.go loadIndexFacts into IndexStat.DefHash, and grouped by rules_relation.go index.duplicate (about lines 141-170) on datname, table, access method and DefHash, without comparing predicates. The unit run shows predicates that differ only in literal case hash equal, and quoted identifiers ('Name' versus name) do not collide. No guard found. Low, because it needs two partial indexes on one table that differ only by literal case.

**Repro:**

```text
go test -count=1 -run TestVerifCR13 -v ./internal/check/ (temporary file, deleted). Output: 'CASE-ONLY literal predicates equal=true' for CREATE INDEX i1 ON public.t USING btree (status) WHERE (status = 'ACTIVE'::text) versus the same with 'active'::text; 'QUOTED-column case equal=false' for ("Name") versus (name).
```

**Suggested fix:** Lowercase only outside single-quoted literals, or lowercase only keywords and whitespace.

**Fix notes:** Lowercase only outside single-quoted literals (handle doubled quotes and E'' escapes) and keep double-quoted identifiers case-sensitive, or lowercase only keywords and whitespace. Pitfall: changing the hash invalidates stored values, and index.divergence (rules_relation.go about lines 214-247) compares hashes across siblings. Mixed-version agents in one cluster would report spurious 'Index topology diverges' until all agents are upgraded, so plan a transition or dual-compare.

### CR-14 — Standby identity includes the ephemeral client port when application_name is shared (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_streaming.go:114`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** standbyIdentity uses the form 'name@addr:port' whenever the name repeats or is empty (lines 114-116). The code's own comment (lines 102-105) says standbys without an application_name report 'walreceiver'. The client port changes on every reconnect, so the identity changes too.

**Failure scenario:** Each reconnect of an unnamed standby creates a new key. For the 2-minute lookback the old key remains, so one synchronous standby can be counted twice by replica.no_sync_standby.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code-level; not run live. The alert engine's latestStandbys keys on DISTINCT ON (instance_id, slot_name, src), and replica.no_sync_standby counts sync_state over those rows.
```

**Verification reasoning:** standbyIdentity (replication_streaming.go) appends the client port only when the name repeats or is empty. The port is the ephemeral source port of each walsender connection, so it changes on reconnect. The unit run shows the identity moving from walreceiver@10.0.0.2:50001 to walreceiver@10.0.0.2:50117, while a single standby with the shared name stays plain 'walreceiver'. The key flows into metrics_replication via pipeline replicationSlot (application_name label). latestStandbys (alert/source_sql.go) keys DISTINCT ON (instance_id, slot_name, src) over a 2-minute lookback, so the pre-reconnect row still counts beside the new one, and replica.no_sync_standby can count one synchronous standby twice. Additional effect, by reading and not in the finding: advisor/snapshot.go loadReplication (5-minute window, DISTINCT ON slot_name, src) counts the stale key as an extra standby, which can make the config.wal_keep_size_low 'every standby has an active slot' test fail spuriously for up to 5 minutes. Not reproduced end-to-end: that needs two unnamed standbys reconnecting.

**Repro:**

```text
go test -count=1 -run TestVerifCR14 -v ./internal/check/ (temporary file, deleted). Output: two shared-name standbys before=[walreceiver@10.0.0.2:50001 walreceiver@10.0.0.3:50002] after_reconnect=[walreceiver@10.0.0.2:50117 walreceiver@10.0.0.3:50002]; single standby before=[walreceiver] after_reconnect=[walreceiver].
```

**Suggested fix:** Key on a stable identity (application_name plus client address), and disambiguate duplicates with a stable ordinal rather than the port.

**Fix notes:** The stable part is application_name plus client address; the port must not be part of the key. Duplicates need a stable ordinal (for example ordered by client address, then by a persisted slot of the standby), and the ordinal must not shift when the other standby reconnects, so test two standbys reconnecting in turn. A stable identity removes the stale key at the source for this case. The server-side DISTINCT ON keys (alert/source_sql.go latestStandbys, advisor/snapshot.go loadReplication) still double count during a genuine rename within the lookback.

### CR-15 — Receiver status mapping has a dead 'catchup' branch and inconsistent values for not-connected states (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_receiver.go:117`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** statusToFloat maps 'catchup' to 2 (line 117). The PostgreSQL docs list 'catchup' only as a pg_stat_replication state, not a pg_stat_wal_receiver status. Every other non-streaming receiver status maps to -1, while an absent row maps to 0 ('disconnected').

**Failure scenario:** A walreceiver that is up but between states reports -1 ('unknown'), while a walreceiver that has exited reports 0 ('disconnected'). The same not-connected condition has two different values.

**Evidence:**

```text
Docs (WebFetch of monitoring-stats, PG17): pg_stat_wal_receiver.status is described only as 'Activity status of the WAL receiver process', with no enumeration. Live, only 'streaming' and an absent row were observed.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The dead 'catchup' branch is real. The PostgreSQL REL_17_STABLE walreceiver.c WalRcvGetStateString returns only stopped, starting, streaming, waiting, restarting, stopping, or UNKNOWN; 'catchup' occurs only in identifiers (upstream_catchup_logged). The PG 17.11 and 19rc1 binaries carry the same receiver state set, and 'catchup' exists only as a walsender state. So replication_receiver.go:117-118 can never match. The docs drift is also real: README.md:1397 lists 'catchup' as a reported receiver status, and cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:547 (`m.Value == 1 || m.Value == 2 // streaming or catchup`) carries the same dead value. The -1 vs 0 inconsistency is real in code: the COALESCE(w.status,'disconnected') path yields 0, while any non-streaming row status hits the default and yields -1. Live, on a throwaway standby: with a streaming primary, pg_stat_wal_receiver returned 'streaming|...|5432'; with primary_conninfo cleared the view returned 0 rows and the exact check SQL returned 'disconnected||0||0' (value 0). The transient -1 path was NOT reproduced: with an unreachable primary the walreceiver backend sat in LibpqwalreceiverConnect while pg_stat_wal_receiver returned no row in 30 samples. system_views.sql filters the view with WHERE s.pid IS NOT NULL. The post-connect states (waiting, restarting, stopping) are the only reachable -1 path; WALRCV_WAITING is assigned in walreceiver.c, while the restarting and stopping assignments were not located in walreceiver.c. Impact is nil today: internal/server pipeline.go applyReplicationMetric (around lines 1136-1194) has no case for replication_receiver_status, so the value is not stored, and the agent treats -1 and 0 identically. No test pins catchup: replication_test.go:148-167 feeds a 'disconnected' row and asserts 0, and no test covers statusToFloat's catchup or default branch. Severity low matches the rubric (docs drift, dead code, no observable wrong data).

**Repro:**

```text
1) Source: PostgreSQL REL_17_STABLE src/backend/replication/walreceiver.c, WalRcvGetStateString: stopped/starting/streaming/waiting/restarting/stopping/UNKNOWN; no 'catchup'. 2) Binary scan of postgres:17.11-alpine and postgres:19rc1-alpine (docker cp to scratch, grep -a -o): receiver state strings present, 'catchup' only as walsender state. 3) Throwaway pglens-review-verif-cr15-pri (postgres:17.11-alpine) + pglens-review-verif-cr15-sby (standby via pg_basebackup -R, same image). Standby SELECT status,sender_host,sender_port,slot_name FROM pg_stat_wal_receiver -> 'streaming|pglens-review-verif-cr15-pri|5432|'. ALTER SYSTEM SET primary_conninfo='' + pg_reload_conf(): count(*) -> 0; check SQL (COALESCE(w.status,'disconnected') LEFT JOIN pg_stat_wal_receiver) -> 'disconnected||0||0'. primary_conninfo host=192.0.2.1 connect_timeout=60: pg_stat_activity walreceiver wait_event=LibpqwalreceiverConnect; 30 samples of pg_stat_wal_receiver -> NO_ROW. All containers, the volume and the network were removed.
```

**Suggested fix:** Remove the dead 'catchup' case. Map the documented not-streaming states to 'disconnected' consistently, and document the mapping.

**Fix notes:** Remove the case "catchup" branch at internal/check/replication_receiver.go:117-118. Also update cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:547 (drop `|| m.Value == 2` and the 'or catchup' comment) and README.md:1397 (list only streaming and disconnected, or the actual not-streaming states). Add a unit test for statusToFloat; none exists. No test asserts the catchup value. If non-streaming statuses are remapped to 0, agent behaviour is unchanged because both -1 and 0 mean not connected. Do not assume the -1 path is common: the view row is absent during connect, so transient rows are rare. Historical docs under docs/plans (STATE.md lines 236 and 432) mention catchup and can be left as history.

### CR-16 — autovacuum_count and autoanalyze_count emitted as gauges although they are cumulative counters (CONFIRMED, checks-relations)

**Location:** `internal/check/table_stats.go:125`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** autovacuum_count and autoanalyze_count are monotonic since the last stats reset (pg_stat_user_tables), but lines 124-128 emit them with pgtype.KindGauge.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The server's delta and reset handling does not apply to these series, so a stats reset is not detected and a rate cannot be derived.

**Correction (from verification):** Correction to the finding: 'a rate cannot be derived' is overstated, because the stored absolute can be differenced at query time.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: {"autovacuum_count", r.AutovacuumCount} in the gauge loop (line 125), emitted with KindGauge (line 128). Other pg_table_* counters use KindCounter (line 118).
```

**Verification reasoning:** The classification is inconsistent with the design. table_stats.go:125 emits autovacuum_count and autoanalyze_count through the gauge loop (KindGauge at line 128), while the other cumulative table counters (seq_scan..n_tup_hot_upd) use KindCounter (line 118). The design docs classify them as counters: docs/plans/002_plan-AnalysisBackend/phase_05.md:105 and phase_03.md:343. README.md:250-252 and 1176 state that counters are stored as per-second rates computed at ingest. Live on a throwaway primary: autovacuum_count was 1 after the first autovacuum cycle and 2 after the second, then pg_stat_reset_single_table_counters dropped it to 0, so the value is cumulative and resets to zero. Server path: internal/server/pipeline.go counter branch (about lines 436-459) routes through the delta engine and stores the rate as value; gauges store the absolute value. So today metrics_tables.autovacuum_count holds an absolute count with no reset event. Correction to the finding: 'a rate cannot be derived' is overstated, because the stored absolute can be differenced at query time. What is actually lost is consistency with the design classification and with how other table counters are stored, plus the counter_reset_detected event. A reset would be caught as counter_went_backwards (delta rule 4), since table_stats never sets Result.StatsReset. Impact is latent: no consumer reads these columns (checked internal/advisor, internal/server API files, web/src and api/openapi.yaml). Severity low matches the rubric.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway pglens-review-verif-cr15-pri (postgres:17.11-alpine): ALTER SYSTEM SET autovacuum_naptime='1s'; reload; CREATE TABLE avtest_cr16 (id int) WITH (autovacuum_vacuum_threshold=0, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0, autovacuum_analyze_threshold=0, autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor=0); INSERT 2000 rows; DELETE all; wait; SELECT relname, autovacuum_count, autoanalyze_count FROM pg_stat_user_tables -> 'avtest_cr16|1|1'. Second INSERT/DELETE cycle -> 'avtest_cr16|2|2'. SELECT pg_stat_reset_single_table_counters('avtest_cr16'::regclass) then the same query -> 'avtest_cr16|0|0'. Containers removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Emit both as KindCounter, consistent with the other cumulative table counters.

**Fix notes:** Flipping the kind is not a one-line fix. (a) As KindCounter, the counter branch stores pt.Rate (pipeline.go about 436-460), which flows into applyTableMetric (about 601-606). The metrics_tables.autovacuum_count column would then hold per-second rates, and history changes meaning at the deploy point. (b) The first sample per series after an agent restart is skipped (pt==nil). (c) Delta MaxGap is 10 minutes (internal/delta/engine.go rule 5): a table dropped by top-N selection for longer and then reselected yields NULL for that scrape. (d) Keeping these as gauges and fixing the docs (phase_03.md:343, phase_05.md:105) and the README principle is equally valid, and arguably better, because the column name autovacuum_count would mislead if it held a rate. Decide first. Test gap either way: TestProcess_CounterVsGaugeClassification (internal/server/pipeline_test.go:61) only checks idx_scan and n_live_tup, and TestTableStats_CounterGaugeClassification (internal/check/table_stats_test.go:38) only checks seq_scan and n_live_tup. phase_03.md:360 says the test should be table-driven over every column, so add the autovacuum and autoanalyze cases.

Unfiltered view (backend_type IN ('client backend','parallel worker')) showed one client backend active with Timeout/PgSleep and four parallel workers active with Timeout/PgSleep. ### AT-08 — ASH sample hides other users' sessions when the role lacks pg_read_all_stats (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/ash/sampler.go:201`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Without pg_read_all_stats (or pg_monitor), pg_stat_activity shows state as NULL for other users' sessions. The filter `state <> 'idle'` drops NULL rows, so those sessions are silently absent from samples. README.md:153 documents the monitoring role as having pg_monitor, so this is a misconfiguration path rather than the default.

**Failure scenario:** The monitoring role is created without pg_monitor. ASH reports idle while another user's workload is running.

**Evidence:**

```text
Container test on postgres:19rc1-alpine with a role lacking pg_read_all_stats while another user's session is active: the sample returns 0 rows. Code: sampler.go:201-203; README.md:153.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Reproduced on a local postgres:19rc1-alpine container (server_version_num 190000). For a role without pg_read_all_stats, another user's active session appears with state, backend_type, wait_event_type and query_id all NULL and query '<insufficient privilege>'. The sampler query (sampler.go:194-204) returns 0 rows for that role, because the hidden row fails both WHERE predicates (backend_type = 'client backend' and state <> 'idle'), and the COALESCE(state,'unknown') in the SELECT never fires because WHERE runs first. The same query as a pg_monitor role returns the session. No guard found: startASH is called unconditionally (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:149, no permission-tier gate), and no code warns about hidden sessions. The monitoring role is documented and granted as pg_monitor (deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:38, README.md:153), so this is a misconfiguration path. Low is right.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run -d --name pglens-review-at08-r1 -e POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust postgres:19rc1-alpine; CREATE ROLE lowpriv LOGIN; CREATE ROLE otheruser LOGIN; CREATE ROLE monitorrole LOGIN; GRANT pg_monitor TO monitorrole; docker exec -d <c> psql -U otheruser -d postgres -c 'SELECT pg_sleep(90)'. Then as lowpriv, the sampler query from sampler.go:194-204 gives rows=0 (grep -c . on empty output). As lowpriv, SELECT pid,usename,state,backend_type,wait_event_type,query_id,left(query,40) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename='otheruser' gives '96|otheruser|||||<insufficient privilege>'. As monitorrole, the same sampler query gives 'postgres|active|Timeout|PgSleep|'. Container removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Check for hidden sessions (compare count(*) with the visible count) or check role membership at startup, and warn when the role cannot see other sessions.

**Fix notes:** A NULL-tolerant state filter alone will not fix this, because backend_type is also NULL for the hidden session. Detection options: count rows where query = '<insufficient privilege>', or check pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_read_all_stats','member') at startup (false for lowpriv, true for monitorrole). The COALESCE(state,'unknown') at sampler.go:196 is dead code and can be removed or moved after the filter.

### AT-13 — Orphan episode start is not reset across an edgeless gap, so duration is overstated (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/topology/engine.go:189`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The orphan block only runs when len(obs.Edges) > 0 (engine.go:189). When an observation arrives with no edges, orphanAt is neither cleared nor aged, so a stale orphan episode carries over to the next orphaned observation and duration_seconds starts from the old start time. In production, edges are sticky (run.go:539, 563), which limits the impact.

**Failure scenario:** A standby is orphaned for 4 minutes, has no edges for 10 minutes, then is orphaned again. The first orphan_standby reports a duration of 14 minutes.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/topology/probe_test.go): duration_seconds is 231 immediately on reappearance after an edgeless gap. Code: engine.go:189-214.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Engine reproduction confirms the mechanism. An orphan episode starts at t=0 with a low-confidence edge. At t=60 orphan_standby fires with duration 60. Then an edgeless observation at t=660 clears nothing (engine.go:189 only runs with len(obs.Edges) > 0). The next orphaned observation reports duration 660, measured from the stale start. Production trigger: edges reach Apply only after the server's resolution at pipeline.go:258-259 (unresolved edges are dropped with 'continue'), so an edgeless observation happens when an edge's address stops resolving, for example when the fallback that resolved it stops applying (the advisor's localhost/published-port example). Agent-side edges are sticky: buildTopologyEdges (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:535-566) keeps the last host in the per-process lastEdgeState map (run.go:121), so the agent alone does not usually send empty edge lists after a host was seen. Restart is not the trigger, because the edge reappears only with a fresh receiver host. Production frequency is unverified, so low fits.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe in internal/topology (go test -count=1 -run TestVerifierProbeAT13OrphanGap -v ./internal/topology/): 't=60 orphan emitted: [orphan_standby]' with payload 'duration_seconds:60'; 't=660 edgeless observation: []'; 't=660 orphan again: [orphan_standby]' with payload 'duration_seconds:660'. Probe file deleted.
```

**Suggested fix:** Clear orphanAt and orphanedAt when an observation carries no low-confidence edges, or when the standby has a resolved edge.

**Fix notes:** In engine.go:189-214, clear orphanAt and orphanedAt when the observation carries no low-confidence edge (or no edge at all), not only when a high-confidence edge arrives (engine.go:183-184). Safe because the agent resends persisted edges on empty reading cycles (run.go:498-530).

Status: open

### AT-19 — compute_query_id 'off' is inferred from samples and logged even under the default auto setting (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/ash/sampler.go:258`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The sampler never reads the compute_query_id GUC. It infers 'off' after five consecutive samples with null query_id (sampler.go:237-253) and logs 'compute_query_id is off' (sampler.go:258-260). Under the default setting (auto), query_id can be null for reasons other than the GUC, so the log misstates the cause. ComputeQueryIDEnabled() has no production consumer.

**Failure scenario:** An operator enables pg_stat_statements with auto query IDs and sees 'compute_query_id is off' in the agent log, then changes a setting that was already correct.

**Evidence:**

```text
Container test: under the default auto setting, query_id is null. Code: sampler.go:237-260.
```

**Verification reasoning:** sampler.go never reads compute_query_id. It latches 'off' after 5 consecutive non-empty samples with null query_id (sampler.go:237-253) and logs 'compute_query_id is off' (sampler.go:256-260). Under the default 'auto', query_id is null for active sessions unless a module such as pg_stat_statements requests query IDs, so the log misstates the cause. ComputeQueryIDEnabled has no production consumer: startASH (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:33-103) keeps the sampler local and returns only stop and enabled.

**Repro:**

```text
postgres:17.11-alpine container: SHOW compute_query_id returned 'auto' and shared_preload_libraries was empty. With a detached 'SET application_name=pglens/shared; SELECT pg_sleep(8)' running, the sampler's exact SQL returned state=active, wait_event=PgSleep and an empty query_id. With 'SET compute_query_id = on' and pg_sleep(6), query_id was 5457019535816659310. The GUC is not the same thing as a null query_id.
```

**Suggested fix:** Read `SHOW compute_query_id` once at startup, log the actual value, and remove the inference.

**Fix notes:** Run SHOW compute_query_id once at startup and log the actual value. Drop the null-count latch and the warning. ComputeQueryIDEnabled can be removed because nothing calls it.

Status: open

### AT-20 — The agent's own monitoring sessions are counted as database workload (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/ash/sampler.go:203`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The sample query excludes only the sampler's own backend (`pid <> pg_backend_pid()`, sampler.go:203). The agent's other connections, such as pool checks and statistics collection, are counted when they are active, so monitoring load shows up as workload.

**Failure scenario:** Frequent stat checks run during a quiet period and appear as active sessions in ASH.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: sampler.go:203; the shared pool is used by the other checks (internal/agent/conn.go).
```

**Verification reasoning:** The sampler SQL (sampler.go:199-204) filters on backend_type, state and pid <> pg_backend_pid() only. The agent's other sessions are client backends named 'pglens/ash' (internal/agent/conn.go:146), 'pglens/shared' (conn.go:159) and 'pglens/<db>' (conn.go:218), so they appear while active. No downstream guard exists: SampleRow has no application_name, so buildASHRow (internal/server/pipeline.go:1196) cannot filter them. Impact scales with how long the agent's checks run; short checks contribute little.

**Repro:**

```text
In the local container, a session with application_name='pglens/shared' running pg_sleep was returned by the sampler's exact query as state=active, wait_event=PgSleep, with query_id null.
```

**Suggested fix:** Exclude backends whose application_name matches the agent's own marker, or whose pid belongs to the agent's pool.

**Fix notes:** Add AND application_name NOT LIKE 'pglens/%' to the sampler SQL. The sampler's own backend is already excluded by PID. Check that no user application uses the pglens/ prefix before adding the filter.

### AT-22 — Fake clock ticker Stop races with Advance (data race under -race) (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/clock/fake.go:61`

**Category:** race · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** fakeTicker.Stop writes t.stopped without holding f.mu, while Advance reads it under f.mu. This is test-only code, but CI runs repeated race stress (README.md:1506), so the race can fail the build.

**Failure scenario:** A test stops a ticker while another goroutine calls Advance. The race detector fails the test run intermittently.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/clock/probe_test.go): go test -race reports DATA RACE between Stop and Advance. Code: fake.go:61-68; Advance around fake.go:99.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The race is real. fakeTicker.Stop writes t.stopped at internal/clock/fake.go:67 without any lock, while Advance reads it at fake.go:113 under f.mu. I reproduced it in isolation, so the defect stands. Severity is corrected from medium to low for four reasons. clock.Fake is test-only: gopls shows NewFake used only from *_test.go files, and production uses clock.System(). internal/clock and internal/topology are not in STRESS_PKG (Makefile:75-76). The existing ash, alert, agent, server, advisor and leaktest packages pass under -race -shuffle=on with no race reported, so no current test trips it. The failure scenario is therefore latent and depends on a future test calling Stop concurrently with Advance. The CI claim is accurate: ci.yml race-stress runs make stress STRESS_ROUNDS=10 on non-PR events, but that target does not include internal/clock.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/clock/zz_probe_at22_test.go (deleted), body: for 200 iterations, f := clock.NewFake(start); ticker := f.NewTicker(time.Millisecond); two goroutines, one calling ticker.Stop() and one calling f.Advance(time.Millisecond), joined by a WaitGroup. Command: go test -race -count=1 -run TestProbeAT22StopVsAdvance ./internal/clock/ . Decisive output: WARNING: DATA RACE, Read at fake.go:113 in (*Fake).Advance, Previous write at fake.go:67 in (*fakeTicker).Stop, then FAIL ... race detected during execution of test. Existing suites, all with -race: go test -race -shuffle=on -count=3 ./internal/ash/... ./internal/alert/... ok; ./internal/agent/... ok; ./internal/server/... ok; ./internal/advisor/... and ./internal/leaktest/... -shuffle=on -count=1 ok. Note that -count=2 on advisor fails on an unrelated duplicate-registration panic (rule_test.go:22), which is not this race and does not affect the stress target.
```

**Suggested fix:** Take f.mu in fakeTicker.Stop, or make stopped an atomic.Bool.

**Fix notes:** fakeTicker has no back-pointer to Fake, so taking f.mu inside Stop needs a new field. The minimal fix is a sync/atomic Bool: Store(true) in Stop at fake.go:67 and Load() in Advance at fake.go:113. Latent trigger: production loops that call ticker.Stop() on shutdown, for example internal/agent/scheduler.go:255 and internal/ash/sampler.go:135, become racy as soon as a test drives them with Advance and does not join the goroutine first.
