### AT-23 — CanonicalLabels collides when label values contain the \x1f separator (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/pgtype/metric.go:41`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** CanonicalLabels joins keys and values with \x1f (metric.go:36-41). A label value containing \x1f can make two different label sets produce the same canonical string, so their series merge.

**Failure scenario:** A wait-event or datname value containing \x1f is merged with another series, so counts from two databases are summed.

**Evidence:**

```text
Probe in scratch copy (internal/pgtype/probe_test.go): two distinct label sets produce identical canonical strings (collide=true). Code: metric.go:36-41.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The defect is real. CanonicalLabels (internal/pgtype/metric.go:41-60) joins key=value pairs with an unescaped separator, so distinct label maps can canonicalize to the same string. The finding's specific scenarios do not hold. (1) database_stats (internal/check/database_stats.go:84) and activity's pg_connections_by_database (internal/check/activity.go:224) use single-key labels, where the canonical form is injective, so a datname containing the separator cannot merge two databases there. (2) activity.go:135 labels are only state and wait_event_type, both fixed PostgreSQL vocabularies, so a wait-event value with the separator is not a realistic source. (3) SeriesKey.Database keeps databases apart (metricDatname in internal/server/pipeline.go, around lines 405-410 and 437-442), so no counts from two databases are summed. The reachable case is a multi-key label set built from user-named identifiers within one database. table_stats.go:107 emits {schemaname, relname}. Example: relname 'x\x1fschemaname=y' with schemaname 'z' collides with relname 'x' and schemaname 'y\x1fschemaname=z'. The effects are shared delta state in internal/delta/engine.go Observe (spurious counter_went_backwards resets and dropped points), a shared series_id (internal/store/write.go:19-29 hashes the string), and a merged alert.Key (internal/alert/key.go:22). The wire layer does no label validation (internal/wire/envelope.go), and the pipeline passes labels straight through. The comment at metric.go:38-40 claiming the separator cannot appear in a PostgreSQL identifier is false: a database name containing it was created successfully (verified). PostgreSQL rewrites control bytes in application_name to escaped text, so that path is closed.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/pgtype/zz_probe_at23_test.go (deleted): a := CanonicalLabels(map[string]string{"a": "x\x1fb=y"}); b := CanonicalLabels(map[string]string{"a": "x", "b": "y"}). Command: go test -count=1 -v -run TestProbeAT23Collision ./internal/pgtype/ . Output: a="a=x\x1fb=y", b="a=x\x1fb=y", COLLIDE=true. PostgreSQL check, in a throwaway postgres:18.6-alpine container (pglens-review-at23-7f3a, removed): CREATE DATABASE "a\x1fb" (name built with printf 'a\037b') returned CREATE DATABASE; pg_database hex of the name is 611f62. application_name set to the same bytes became escaped text (hex 615c78316662).
```

**Suggested fix:** Length-prefix each key and value, or JSON-encode the sorted pairs.

**Fix notes:** Pitfall: store.SeriesID (internal/store/write.go:19-29) and alert.Key (internal/alert/key.go:22) hash this canonical string, so changing the encoding for every label set re-keys stored series and active alerts. Escape only when needed (escape the separator and the escape character themselves) so existing keys stay byte-identical. Also correct the false comment at metric.go:38-40.

Status: open

### AT-24 — Split-brain check scans every instance on every Apply under the global lock (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/topology/engine.go:223`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** detectSplitBrain iterates over every instance in every cluster (engine.go:223-235). It runs on every Apply (engine.go:218), and Apply holds the global engine mutex (engine.go:99-100). One envelope with N instances therefore costs O(N squared) under the lock.

**Failure scenario:** A deployment with several hundred instances pushing every few seconds spends measurable time under the topology lock on every push.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: engine.go:99-100, 218, 223-235.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The code matches the finding. Apply (internal/topology/engine.go:98-100) holds the write lock and calls detectSplitBrain (line 218). That loops over all of e.instances (lines 228-235) and filters by cluster, so the cost of each Apply is proportional to the total number of tracked instances across all clusters. The pipeline calls p.topo.Apply once per instance per envelope (internal/server/pipeline.go:293), so one envelope costs O(N*M). Measured: 0.14 ms per envelope at 100 instances, 1.3 ms at 300 and 11.7 ms at 1000. The quadratic growth is real but the absolute cost is small at realistic scale, so I kept it at low rather than medium.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/topology/zz_probe_at24_test.go (deleted). For n in {100,300,1000}: one engine on a fake clock, 20 reps, each rep applies one standby Observation per instance (ClusterID 1, RoleStandby), logging the time per rep. Command: go test -count=1 -v -run TestProbeAT24Cost ./internal/topology/ . Output: instances=100 per_envelope=144.378µs; instances=300 per_envelope=1.325341ms; instances=1000 per_envelope=11.659971ms.
```

**Suggested fix:** Keep an index of primaries per cluster and check only that cluster on each Apply.

**Fix notes:** Keep a per-cluster index of primaries, updated in Apply and pruned in Evict, so detectSplitBrain touches only the observed cluster. The finding's wording 'every instance in every cluster' is accurate, since the scan covers all clusters.

Status: open

### AT-26 — ASH top warning is derived from the last row's ticks, so empty results show a misleading warning (CONFIRMED, ash-topology-identity-host)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_ash.go:571`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** handleASHTop takes totalTicks from queryASHTop (api_ash.go:559) and shows a low-sample warning when totalTicks < 60 (api_ash.go:571). When the query returns no rows, totalTicks is 0, so the response warns about too few ticks even though the real cause is that there is no data.

**Failure scenario:** A filter that matches nothing returns an empty list with a warning that the sample is small, which suggests the data is noisy rather than absent.

**Evidence:**

```text
Code: api_ash.go:559, 571; the ticks source is the ticks CTE (api_ash.go:593-594).
```

**Verification reasoning:** queryASHTop (internal/server/api_ash.go:588-635) takes totalTicks only from entry rows (line 628, totalTicks = entry.Ticks). The ticks CTE reaches the result only through CROSS JOIN with top (line 609). When the filter matches nothing, top is empty, the join yields zero rows, totalTicks stays 0, and handleASHTop (line 571) sets the 'fewer than 60 samples' warning even though the range holds plenty of ticks. The same pattern exists in queryASHBuckets (windowTicks built from returned rows, lines 245 and 251) and queryASHGrouped (bucketTicks built from returned rows, lines 380 and 397), so handleASH and the group_by path show the same false warning when filters or the database match nothing. The impact is limited to the warning on empty or filtered-to-empty results, so low.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway postgres:18.6-alpine container (pglens-review-at23-7f3a, removed). Created metrics_ash with the columns the query uses, inserted 600 rows at 1-second spacing with window_ticks=1, queryid 42, wait_event_type 'CPU', samples 2. Ran the ticks CTE alone: returns 600. Ran the handleASHTop SQL (copied verbatim from api_ash.go:592-610, where clause inlined) with wait_event = 'Nope': returns (0 rows). The same query with wait_event_type = 'CPU' returns queryid 42, samples 1200, ticks 600. So the empty result carries no ticks to Go, and totalTicks stays 0.
```

**Suggested fix:** Return a distinct 'no data' status when there are no rows, and compute the warning only from ticks that were actually observed.

**Fix notes:** Take the ticks from a separate range query, or LEFT JOIN top with the ticks CTE and read ticks from the CTE rather than the entry rows. Derive the warning from that value. Apply the same change to handleASH and queryASHGrouped. Keep the ticks CTE unfiltered by database and filters (tickWhere, line 590), since that is intentional.

Status: open

### SI-06 — PushEnvelope contract: agent_id required in OpenAPI but absent accepted; schema allows extra keys the handler rejects (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/inventory.go:169`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** api/openapi.yaml:635 marks agent_id required and the PushEnvelope schema (lines 633-641) does not set additionalProperties: false. The handler differs on both points. An envelope without agent_id is accepted, and an agents row is fabricated with agent_id equal to the instance_id (inventory.go:166-171 and the INSERT at inventory.go:173). DisallowUnknownFields (ingest.go:104) rejects any extra top-level key with 400 'bad json'. The generated client types (web/src/api/generated.ts:1239-1248) inherit the schema, so clients following it get different behavior.

**Failure scenario:** A future agent bumps protocol_version and adds a top-level field. The server answers 400, and the agent treats 400 as drop (internal/agent/pusher.go, 4xx path), so samples are lost. Separately, an envelope without agent_id creates an agents row keyed by instance_id that no revocation can match (see SI-05).

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/inventory.go:169 `if agentParam == uuid.Nil {` / `agentParam = instUUID`; internal/server/ingest.go:104 `dec.DisallowUnknownFields()`; api/openapi.yaml:635 `required: [protocol_version, agent_id, agent_version, sent_at, instances]`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code: openapi.yaml:635 lists agent_id as required, and PushEnvelope (633-641) has no additionalProperties:false. generated.ts:1239-1248 types agent_id as a required string. The handler accepts a missing agent_id: upsertOne then falls back to the instance_id (inventory.go:169-171) and inserts an agents row with that id (173). Reproduced: an envelope without agent_id gives 202 {accepted:1,rejected:0}, and the INSERT INTO agents argument equals the instance_id. Advisor-style objection checked: DisallowUnknownFields runs in the decode (ingest.go:104-108) before the protocol-version gate (109-112), so an extra top-level key is rejected with 400 'bad json' even when the version is supported; the finding's scenario holds in that form. A bumped version that is out of range is rejected by the version gate with 400 in either case. Low stands: contract drift plus a fabricated agents row.

**Repro:**

```text
Harness: new instance (not in the existing map), envelope with AgentID='' via the IngestHandler path. Output: status=202 body={"accepted":1,"rejected":0}; the recorded INSERT INTO agents exec has args[0] equal to the instance_id. Schema checked by reading api/openapi.yaml:633-641 and web/src/api/generated.ts:1239-1248. Command: go test -run TestVF_SI06 -v ./internal/server/ (temporary file, deleted).
```

**Suggested fix:** Align the schema and the handler: reject a missing or invalid agent_id with 400 and remove the instance_id fallback. Either mark PushEnvelope additionalProperties: false, or allow unknown keys under an explicit protocol-version policy. Add a contract test that replays the openapi example.

**Fix notes:** Align the schema with the handler: either reject a missing or invalid agent_id with 400 and remove the instance_id fallback (inventory.go:169-171), or relax the schema. If additionalProperties is set to false, note that DisallowUnknownFields (ingest.go:104) already rejects extra keys with 400. Regenerate web/src/api/generated.ts after the schema change. Add the openapi example as a contract test.

Status: open

### SI-08 — Staleness restart or leader change re-emits agent_down and instance_unreachable for already-down instances (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/staleness.go:495`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** instanceUp is an in-memory map that starts empty. On the first observation of an instance that is already stale, the code emits agent_down and instance_unreachable again (staleness.go:496-508). Every process restart and every leadership change therefore re-emits events for all currently-down instances. The impact depends on how the alert engine deduplicates event rules, which was not verified.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The server restarts during a three-hour outage of five instances. Five agent_down and five instance_unreachable events are inserted at startup, which an event-driven rule may page on again.

**Correction (from verification):** The paging half of the scenario is REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/staleness.go:495 `prevUp, seenBefore := s.instanceUp[iidStr]` and staleness.go:496-508 `if !seenBefore {` emitting agent_down and instance_unreachable when `!up`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The re-emission is real. A new Staleness evaluator has an empty instanceUp map, so it re-emits agent_down and instance_unreachable for every already-stale instance (staleness.go:495-508). The paging half of the scenario is REFUTED. The engine restores firing state from the alerts store (engine.go Tick, eval.go Restore), and alert.Key has no time component (key.go), so the re-emitted instance_unreachable event maps to the same firing episode and Step returns TransitionNone with no notification. The agent_down alert is metric-based (reads instances.last_seen, no EventType), so the re-emitted agent_down event rows feed no alert. The only effect is duplicate rows in the events table and timeline. Note: the tokensave index serves 'main' and refuses this branch, and Serena is bound to the main checkout, so all code reading was done with Read on the worktree files.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (deleted) against a local timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17 container (name pglens-review-si-8f6a, removed). Command: PGLENS_REVIEW_DSN=postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:<mapped port>/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI08 -count=1 -v. Decisive output: 'process 1 staleness: agent_down=1 instance_unreachable=1'; 'process 1 engine notifications: [instance_unreachable key=instance_unreachable/<iid>/ state=firing]'; 'after restart staleness: agent_down=2 instance_unreachable=2'; 'restarted engine notifications: (none)'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Seed instanceUp at Start from the latest persisted agent_down or agent_up event per instance, or from instances.last_seen. Alternatively emit only on observed transitions.

**Fix notes:** Location: internal/server/staleness.go:495-508. Options: seed instanceUp at Start from persisted agent_down/agent_up events or instances.last_seen, or emit only on observed transitions. Low priority. The paging claim in the finding text should be removed.

Status: open

### SI-10 — Two staleness thresholds: gauge 90s, alert metric 60s (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/staleness.go:320`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The pglens_up gauge uses threshold = 3 * 30s = 90s (staleness.go:315-321 with defaultExpectedInterval = 30s at staleness.go:26). The alert up metric uses last_seen >= now() - 60 seconds (internal/alert/source_sql.go:115). An instance is therefore reported down by the alert 30 seconds before /metrics shows it down, so dashboards and alerts disagree for every outage.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** An agent stops at t0. At t0+60s the alert metric reads 0 while pglens_up still reads 1 until t0+90s.

**Correction (from verification):** The claimed 30-second lead of the alert is REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/staleness.go:320 `return 3 * iv`; internal/server/staleness.go:26 `defaultExpectedInterval = 30 * time.Second`; internal/alert/source_sql.go:115 `CASE WHEN i.last_seen >= now() - interval '60 seconds' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The divergence between the two thresholds is real. The alert metric sample flips to 0 at 60s (source_sql.go:115), while pglens_up stays 1 until 90s (staleness.go:320). The claimed 30-second lead of the alert is REFUTED. The metric source seeds the sample timestamp at now-For (source_sql.go:141-143). The first stale sample produces TransitionOpened (eval.go Step), and the engine neither persists nor notifies Opened (engine.go:302). The alert therefore fires on the next engine tick, roughly 60s + 1 to 2 engine intervals after last_seen. With the default 30s interval that is about 90-120s, which is no earlier than the gauge flip. Only a shorter PGLENS_ALERT_INTERVAL (about 15s) would fire it earlier.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (deleted), real 30s wait between ticks, same container. Command: go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI10 -count=1 -v. Decisive output: 'age~65s: alert metric value=0 gauge pglens_up=1 notifications=(none)'; 'age~95s: alert metric value=0 gauge pglens_up=0 notifications=[agent_down key=agent_down/<iid>/ state=firing] [instance_unreachable ...]'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Define one staleness threshold constant and use it both for the gauge and to derive the alert SQL interval.

**Fix notes:** Use a single staleness threshold constant for both the gauge (staleness.go:315-321) and the alert SQL interval (source_sql.go:115). The comment at source_sql.go:137-140 misdescribes how For interacts with the Opened transition, so rewrite it. Correct the finding's impact text.

Status: open

### SI-17 — Listener failure is logged and the process exits with status 0 (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-server/main.go:175`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** When ListenAndServe fails (for example the port is in use), the error is sent to listenErr. The select at main.go:172-176 logs it and falls through to Shutdown, and main returns normally, so the process exits 0. Supervisors that restart on failure (systemd Restart=on-failure, restart-on-failure policies) treat the failure as a clean stop. The comment at main.go:163-165 shows the author considered exit paths but not the exit status.

**Failure scenario:** Port 8080 is held by another process. The server logs 'listen: ...' and exits 0. systemd does not restart it, and the service stays down silently.

**Evidence:**

```text
cmd/pglens-server/main.go:174-176 `case err := <-listenErr:` / `log.Printf("listen: %v", err)`; cmd/pglens-server/main.go:179 `_ = srv.Shutdown(ctx)`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** cmd/pglens-server/main.go:174-176 logs the listenErr and falls through to Shutdown. main then returns normally, so the process exits with status 0 and no os.Exit(1) is called anywhere on this path. No guard found.

**Repro:**

```text
Built the server with go build ./cmd/pglens-server into the scratchpad, held 127.0.0.1:18093 with a python listening socket, then ran PGLENS_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:18093 PGLENS_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=<32 hex chars> ./pglens-server under timeout 15. stderr: listen: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:18093: bind: address already in use. Then EXIT_CODE=0. Binary and helper deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Return a non-zero status on listener failure: record the error and exit with status 1 after deferred cleanup, or have run() return the error to main.

**Fix notes:** Do not call os.Exit inside the select, since that skips the deferred pool, staleness and engine stops (the comment at main.go:163-165 warns about exactly this). Instead have run() return an error or exit code, let the defers run, and then exit 1 from main.

Status: open

### SI-18 — Migration files whose names fail Sscanf are skipped silently (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/store/migrate.go:55`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** `if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(name, "%04d_", &version); err != nil { continue }` drops any .sql file whose name does not match the exact prefix. For example 0016-add-index.sql fails on the literal underscore. The file is not logged, not recorded and not reported as an error, so the schema silently lacks the migration while the server runs. Duplicate version numbers are not detected either.

**Failure scenario:** A developer names a migration 0016-events-index.sql. Startup succeeds, the index is never created, queries on events run slower, and nothing reports it.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/store/migrate.go:55 `if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(name, "%04d_", &version); err != nil {`; internal/store/migrate.go:56 `continue`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** internal/store/migrate.go:55-57 continues silently on any Sscanf error, with no log, no error and no record. A second file with the same version number is skipped silently by the schema_migrations exists check (migrate.go:58-64), so duplicate versions are not detected either. internal/store/migrate_test.go covers only specific named migrations and not the naming rule. All current files 0001 through 0015 match the pattern, so making the check strict is safe.

**Repro:**

```text
Standalone Go program in the scratchpad calling fmt.Sscanf(name, '%04d_', &version) on test names. Output: 0016_events_index.sql version=16 err=nil; 0016-events-index.sql version=16 err=input does not match format skipped=true; 0016 events.sql err=input does not match format skipped=true; 0016_a.sql version=16 err=nil; 0016_b.sql version=16 err=nil (the second is then skipped by the exists check at migrate.go:58-64). Program deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Return an error for any .sql entry that does not match ^[0-9]{4}_.+\.sql$, and fail on duplicate version numbers.

**Fix notes:** Return an error for any .sql entry that does not match ^[0-9]{4}_.+\.sql$, and fail on duplicate version numbers within the embedded set. The current set has no duplicates, so the stricter check should pass on startup. Add a unit test that feeds the name list through the same parsing logic.

Status: open

### SI-19 — Shutdown can block indefinitely in the deferred pool.Close (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-server/main.go:179`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** main.go:177-179 gives srv.Shutdown 15 seconds and ignores its error, but Shutdown does not cancel the contexts of in-flight requests. Requests still inside Pipeline.Process keep their pooled connections. When run returns, the deferred pool.Close (main.go:79) waits until every acquired connection is released (pgxpool Close semantics). Shutdown is therefore bounded by the slowest in-flight database call, not by the 15-second budget.

**Failure scenario:** SIGTERM arrives during a slow envelope write waiting on a lock. Shutdown returns after 15s with its error ignored, pool.Close blocks, and the orchestrator sends SIGKILL after its grace period.

**Evidence:**

```text
cmd/pglens-server/main.go:177-179 `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)` / `_ = srv.Shutdown(ctx)`; cmd/pglens-server/main.go:79 `defer pool.Close()`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Verified by code and library documentation, not by a live lock reproduction. main.go:177-179 gives Shutdown 15s and ignores its error. net/http Server.Shutdown does not interrupt active connections or cancel their request contexts (go doc net/http.Server.Shutdown). Pipeline.Process begins a transaction on the request context (pipeline.go:108) and holds the pooled connection until commit or rollback. pgxpool Pool.Close blocks until all connections are returned (go doc github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool.Pool.Close), and its deferred call at main.go:79 runs last in LIFO order. Precision: Shutdown itself returns at 15s. What is unbounded is process exit inside pool.Close. Impact is limited: the 202 is never written, a SIGKILL rolls back the transaction, and the agent retries.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading: cmd/pglens-server/main.go:79 (defer pool.Close), main.go:177-179 (15s context, Shutdown error ignored), pipeline.go:108-114 (Begin on request context, deferred Rollback). Library docs: go doc net/http.Server.Shutdown ('without interrupting any active connections'); go doc github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool.Pool.Close ('Blocks until all connections are returned to pool and closed'). No live reproduction was run.
```

**Suggested fix:** Tie request contexts to a base context (http.Server.BaseContext) that is cancelled after the Shutdown deadline, so in-flight pipeline queries abort before the pool is closed.

**Fix notes:** A BaseContext that is cancelled after the Shutdown deadline, as the finding suggests, works. Cancel it before pool.Close is reached, and keep the 202 unsent on cancellation so the agent does not ack the envelope. Also note that Shutdown's own return is already bounded at 15s, so the fix target is the process exit path.

Status: open

### SI-20 — resolveAddr picks an arbitrary instance when addresses collide (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/pipeline.go:194`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** When the edge has no port, the query `SELECT instance_id FROM instances WHERE cluster_id=$1 AND addr=$2 LIMIT 1` has no ORDER BY. With several instances sharing an address (for example behind a proxy or NAT), PostgreSQL may return any of them. The topology edge is then attributed to a wrong upstream, which can produce a false role or failover conclusion, and the result is not stable across calls.

**Failure scenario:** Two instances in one cluster advertise addr 10.0.0.5 with no port. The standby's upstream edge resolves to instance B on one envelope and to A on the next, so the topology edge flips.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/pipeline.go:194 `query := `SELECT instance_id FROM instances WHERE cluster_id=$1 AND addr=$2 LIMIT 1``; internal/server/pipeline.go:196-199 port-qualified variant used only when port > 0.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Mechanism reproduced on the real schema, but the trigger is narrower than the finding says. pipeline.go:194 has no ORDER BY, and instances has no unique constraint on (tenant, cluster, addr): instances_addr_idx is non-unique, and inventory.go:244-277 only emits duplicate_instance_suspected. Reproduced: two instances at the same address in one cluster; the query returned bbbbbbbb... ; after an addr round trip with no data change (UPDATE to 10.0.0.9, then back to 10.0.0.5), it returned cccccccc... instead. EXPLAIN uses instances_addr_idx. Trigger: the database path is reached only for port-0 edges. buildTopologyEdges (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:557) sets Port only when sender_port is positive, so Port stays 0 only when the walreceiver reports no positive port. The finding's proxy or NAT example keeps a port and does not reach this branch. Also, the in-envelope addr-only map (pipeline.go:152-154) is last-writer-wins and runs before the database query, which is also ambiguous and is not mentioned in the finding.

**Repro:**

```text
Container: timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17 with migrations 0001 through 0014 applied. Inserted agent, cluster 42, and two instances at 10.0.0.5 port 0. psql: count of rows at that address = 2. SELECT ... LIMIT 1: bbbbbbbb-0000-0000-0000-000000000001. After UPDATE addr to 10.0.0.9 and back to 10.0.0.5 (UPDATE 1 each), the same SELECT returned cccccccc-0000-0000-0000-000000000002. EXPLAIN: Index Scan using instances_addr_idx. Container removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Require a port match, or ORDER BY a deterministic key and treat multiple matches as ambiguous (no edge).

**Fix notes:** Two places need ambiguity handling, not just ORDER BY: the database query at pipeline.go:194 and the addr-only in-envelope map at pipeline.go:152-154. When the edge port is 0 and more than one instance matches, return no edge instead of picking one. When the port is known, require a port match.

Status: open

### SI-21 — metrics_replication dedup index omits source, so distinct source rows collide (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/store/migrations/0002_hypertables.sql:74`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The unique index metrics_replication_dedup_idx on (instance_id, COALESCE(upstream_id, zero-uuid), slot_name, ts) predates the source column, which 0014 added without updating the index. Rows with the same instance, upstream, slot and timestamp but a different source (for example 'sender' and 'slot') collide, and WriteReplication uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the second row is dropped silently. Reproduced on timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17: the 'slot' row for the same timestamp was dropped and the 'sender' row kept. The collision needs identical ts for both sources, which the independently jittered check tickers (internal/agent/scheduler.go) make rare.

**Failure scenario:** Two replication rows for one standby carry identical ts, one with source 'slot'. The slot row is dropped, so evaluateSlots (which filters source = 'slot') has no state for that scrape and slot_inactive timing is affected.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/store/migrations/0002_hypertables.sql:74-76 `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX metrics_replication_dedup_idx ON metrics_replication` / `(instance_id, COALESCE(upstream_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid),` / `slot_name, ts);`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Verified and reproduced. 0002_hypertables.sql:74-76 creates metrics_replication_dedup_idx without source. 0014 only adds columns, and no later migration recreates the index (files 0001 through 0015 checked). writeTypedRows (internal/store/write.go:396-437) uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a collision drops the second row silently. The live database index definition confirms the omission. Rarity: wire.Result.TS is clk.Now() at drain time (cmd/pglens-agent/run.go:223), one per result with nanosecond precision, and PostgreSQL stores microseconds. A collision needs the same microsecond for a sender row and a slot row whose slot_name matches the standby's application_name, so it is rare, as the finding states.

**Repro:**

```text
Container: timescale/timescaledb:2.31.0-pg17 with migrations 0001 through 0014. Two INSERTs into metrics_replication with identical ts 2026-10-23 10:00:00.123456+00, same instance, slot_name standby1, source sender then slot. First INSERT 0 1. Second INSERT 0 0. SELECT returned only the sender row. Fix check: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on (instance_id, COALESCE(upstream_id, zero uuid), slot_name, COALESCE(source,''), ts), then DROP the old index and RENAME, in one transaction, on a hypertable with 2 compressed chunks. It succeeded. The slot row then inserted with INSERT 0 1 and both rows were kept. Container removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add a new forward-only migration (0016) that recreates metrics_replication_dedup_idx including source, creating the new index before dropping the old one.

**Fix notes:** The migration runner executes each file in one transaction (migrate.go:70-82), so keep create, drop and rename in one file. COALESCE(source,'') is needed because legacy rows have NULL source (0014 comment), and NULLs are distinct in unique indexes. Creating the replacement index on compressed chunks worked in TimescaleDB 2.31.0 in the test above. Optionally add tenant_id, which the other dedup indexes include.

Status: open

### SI-22 — Clock-skew metric has two sign conventions under one name (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/server/ingest.go:125`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** ingest.go:123-125 calls ObserveAgentClockSkew(time.Since(env.TransmittedAt).Seconds()) only when the agent is more than 30s ahead, so the value is negative. pipeline.go:811-818 writes the same metric name, pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds, into the metrics table with the absolute value. The /metrics exposition (metrics_handler.go:29) therefore shows a negative number for the same condition that the stored series records as positive. The in-process gauge is also updated only for large skew, so small skew is never observed.

**Failure scenario:** An agent is 40s ahead. /metrics reports pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds = -40 while the stored series records 40 for the same push. Any dashboard or alert that combines the two reads the wrong sign.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/server/ingest.go:125 `ObserveAgentClockSkew(time.Since(env.TransmittedAt).Seconds())`; internal/server/pipeline.go:811-814 `skew := now.Sub(sent).Seconds()` / `if skew < 0 {` / `skew = -skew`; internal/server/metrics_handler.go:29 writes pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds from the in-process gauge.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code reading and a repro agree. ingest.go:123-125 calls ObserveAgentClockSkew(time.Since(env.TransmittedAt).Seconds()) only when TransmittedAt is more than 30s after server now (agent ahead), so the value is negative. pipeline.go:811-814 computes now.Sub(sent), flips it to the absolute value, and stores it as pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds. metrics_handler.go:29 exposes the in-process gauge, so /metrics shows the signed value and the stored series shows the absolute one. The gauge is only Set on large skew and is never cleared, so it stays stale: after a +40s push it reads -39.9996, and it is unchanged after a +5s push and after an in-sync push. The alert side is not affected: the Tier-0 clock_skew rule (internal/alert/builtin.go) reads the stored series with GT 30, which is correct. The impact is therefore confined to the /metrics self-metric, which is wrong in sign and stale. Severity stays low.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary in-package test internal/server/zz_review_si22_24_test.go (deleted afterwards). Command: go test ./internal/server/ -run TestReviewSI22_ClockSkewSigns -count=1 -v. Pushes through IngestHandler(NewAuth, NewInventory(nil), NewPipeline(nil,nil)) with X-Pglens-Transmitted-At = now+40s, then reads MetricsHandler output. Output: after agent +40s push: pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds -39.999622557; after +5s push: same line; after in-sync push: same line. selfMetricRows with TransmittedAt=now+40s stores value 39.99999727. PASS.
```

**Suggested fix:** Use one signed convention (now minus TransmittedAt) for both sinks, and update the in-process gauge on every push.

**Fix notes:** Do not make the stored series signed. The Tier-0 clock_skew rule (internal/alert/builtin.go, Metric pglens_agent_clock_skew_seconds, GT 30) would then never fire for an agent behind by more than 30s. Keep the absolute convention, set the gauge on every push (ingest.go:123-125 only sets it when skewed, which leaves the last large-skew value stuck), and make /metrics report the same absolute value (metrics_handler.go:29). Locations: ingest.go:123-125, pipeline.go:811-814.

Status: open

### SI-24 — Event rows have no dedupe key; retried committed envelopes duplicate events (CONFIRMED, server-ingest-store)

**Location:** `internal/store/write.go:642`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** WriteEvents uses a plain INSERT, and the events table has no unique key (0001 creates it; 0015 adds an index on ts only). If an envelope commits but the response is lost, the agent resends it (pusher.go:251-254 retries network errors), and events such as cardinality_truncated (pipeline.go:344-348) and counter_reset_detected are inserted again. Metric rows are deduplicated by ON CONFLICT, but events are not. The per-check counters IncCheckError and IncCheckOK (pipeline.go:339-343) are incremented before commit and double-count on retry the same way.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A cardinality_truncated event is committed for an envelope at 10:00:15, but the response is lost to the agent's timeout. The agent retries, and two identical events exist. Alert rules keyed on events fire twice.

**Correction (from verification):** Two sub-claims are REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
internal/store/write.go:642 `func WriteEvents(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, rows []EventRow) error {`; internal/server/pipeline.go:339-343 `if r.Error != "" {` / `IncCheckError(r.Check)`; internal/server/pipeline.go:344 `if r.Truncated {`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The core claim is confirmed. WriteEvents (write.go:642-671) uses a plain INSERT. The events table (0001_meta.sql:73-82) has only a bigserial PK, and 0015 adds an index on ts only, so no unique key exists. Metric rows do use ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (write.go:313-330), so the asymmetry is real. The agent retries a network error or 5xx forever with the same envelope (pusher.go:250-254 and the 5xx branch), so a lost 202 causes a resend. Each resend re-runs the in-loop IncCheckError/IncCheckOK (pipeline.go:339-343) before commit, so the counters double-count, and cardinality_truncated (pipeline.go:344-355) is inserted again. The repro confirms both. Two sub-claims are REFUTED. counter_reset_detected is not duplicated: the first delivery moves the delta baseline to the reset timestamp, so the retry hits Rule 2 (engine.go:90-91) and emits nothing. Topology events are not re-emitted by an immediate retry: role changes are transition-based and split-brain/orphan emission is throttled (topology/engine.go). Seeded alert rules that key on events (builtin.go: instance_unreachable, no_primary_in_cluster, failover_detected, split_brain_detected, slot_inactive) do not include cardinality_truncated, and cardinality alerting uses the ON CONFLICT-deduplicated gauge. So 'alert rules fire twice' holds only for a custom Tier-1 rule keyed on cardinality_truncated. Severity low is right.

**Repro:**

```text
Same temporary test file and container as SI-23. Command: PGLENS_REVIEW_DSN='postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:55433/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test ./internal/server/ -run 'TestReviewSI24' -count=1 -v. TestReviewSI24_RetriedEnvelopeDuplicatesEvents processes the identical envelope (one result with Truncated:true) twice through Pipeline.Process. Output: delivery 1 accepted=1; delivery 2 accepted=1; cardinality_truncated rows after 2 identical deliveries: 2; pglens_check_ok_total{database_stats} delta after 2 deliveries: 2. TestReviewSI24_CounterResetNotDuplicatedOnRetry processes counter 1000 at t0, counter 50 at t0+1m, then the same t0+1m envelope again. Output: counter_reset_detected rows after reset + retry: 1 (refutes the sub-claim).
```

**Suggested fix:** Give events a deterministic dedupe key (instance, type, ts, payload hash) with a unique index and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Move the check counters after commit.

**Fix notes:** events has no unique key: 0001_meta.sql:73-82 has only the bigserial PK, 0015 adds events_ts_idx only, and events is not a hypertable (0002 does not list it). A unique index on (tenant_id, instance_id, type, ts, payload-hash) is feasible, but the migration must delete existing duplicates before creating the index. Only cardinality_truncated (pipeline.go:344-355, ts = r.TS) is both per-envelope and duplicated. Topology events and staleness events use now() or transition logic, so a ts-based key does not fit them. The check counters at pipeline.go:339-343 (and the no-DB path at pipeline.go:848-852) need to move after tx.Commit, which means collecting the results first. Do not add dedupe on the counter_reset path: delta Rule 2 already suppresses the duplicate. Location of the insert: store/write.go:652-655.

Status: open

### SA-05 — Metrics query range check overflows: 1ns step over a ~8000-year range bypasses the 10000-point cap (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:737`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** points := int(math.Ceil(float64(duration) / float64(step))) (line 737). to.Sub(from) saturates at MaxInt64 nanoseconds, and with step=1ns the float-to-int conversion overflows to a non-positive value. The clamp at line 738 then sets points=1, so the cap check at lines 741-742 never fires. The raw-row query at lines 777-781 then scans the whole range for that instance and metric.

**Failure scenario:** An authenticated client requests the full 8000-year span at 1ns step. It gets 200 with one point while the server runs an unbounded raw-metrics scan for that series, which causes DB load and a 2-minute WriteTimeout risk.

**Evidence:**

```text
Overlay test: from=0001-01-01T00:00:00Z to=9999-12-31T23:59:59Z step=1ns returns 200 with a single point (SA-METRICS). The control with a 2-day span and 1ns step returns 422 as expected. The bucket index guard at api.go:42 in the loop prevents a panic.
```

**Verification reasoning:** In handleMetricsQuery (api.go ~720-745), duration = to.Sub(from) saturates at MaxInt64 ns (about 292 years). With step=1ns, float64(duration)/float64(step) is about 2^63. On amd64, int() of that value is MinInt64, so points is <=0 and gets clamped to 1, and the 10000-point cap never fires. The finding's mechanism is confirmed. The bug is platform-specific: Go leaves out-of-range float-to-int conversion implementation-dependent, and arm64 saturates to MaxInt64, which would yield 422. Severity lowered from medium because the impact is small. metrics has 30-day retention (migration 0003), so the overflow request scans the same retained rows a legal 30-day request does, with no extra DB load. The query has a 5s context timeout (api.go), so the finding's 2-minute WriteTimeout claim is wrong. The real effect is a bypassed validation that returns one misleading null point.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go test in internal/server (deleted afterwards) calling a.handleMetricsQuery on &API{} (nil pool, so validation runs and the response is all-null). Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA05MetricsOverflow -v ./internal/server/ on linux/amd64, go1.27.2. Decisive output: 'SA05 overflow: 8000y span at 1ns: status=200 body={"series":[{"ts":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","value":null}]}'; 'SA05 control: 2d span at 1ns: status=422 ... would produce 172800000000000 points, max 10000'; 'SA05 control: 8000y span at 1s: status=422 ... would produce 9223372037 points, max 10000'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compute the point count in float64 and compare to maxMetricPoints before converting to int, reject when duration/step overflows, and cap the total range (for example one year) before the query.

**Fix notes:** Compare float64(duration)/float64(step) with maxMetricPoints before the int conversion, and reject when the ratio is over the cap. Test from=0001-01-01 to=9999-12-31 at step=1ns on amd64 and expect 422. Per the fixer's judgement, a span cap would also limit output size, but the DB cost is already bounded by retention.

Status: open

### SA-07 — Events and statements endpoints scan unbounded history when from/to are omitted (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:829`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** handleEvents (api.go:829) applies no default time window when from or to are absent, and the type filter has no supporting index (events_lookup_idx is (tenant_id,cluster_id,ts DESC) and events_ts_idx is (ts) only). handleStatements (api.go:971) aggregates the full retained history per instance when no window is given, bounded only by a 5s timeout.

**Failure scenario:** A dashboard or script calls /events?type=... or /statements without a window across months of retained data. Each call scans the whole history for that cluster or instance, which slows writes and other reads and can hit the 5s timeout.

**Evidence:**

```text
api.go:833-860 (handleEvents) sets fromPtr/toPtr only when the params are present. api.go:971 handleStatements has no default range. Migrations in internal/store/migrations define no index on events.type.
```

**Verification reasoning:** handleEvents (api.go ~829-930) applies no default window, but the SQL already has LIMIT (default 100, max 1000), so the finding's add-LIMIT fix is already in place. The type filter has no index: events_lookup_idx is (tenant_id, cluster_id, ts DESC) from 0001, and events_ts_idx is (ts) from 0015. On 1M rows, a rare type with no window is a Parallel Seq Scan at 35 ms (32 ms with a cluster filter), and a common type is 0.14 ms via a backward ts index. Events are sparse state transitions with 90-day retention (staleness.go eventRetention), so realistic volume is far from the 5s timeout. handleStatements (api.go) has no default window and aggregates the whole retained instance history (30-day retention). But the UI never omits the window: the statements page (QueryListPage.tsx) and the events page (EventsPage.tsx) always send from and to, the default range is 1h, and absolute ranges are capped at 30 days (timerange.ts). Only direct API callers reach the unbounded path, so severity is low.

**Repro:**

```text
Throwaway container postgres:18.6-alpine named pglens-review-sa07-events (trust auth), removed afterwards. DDL: events table as in 0001_meta.sql, plus events_lookup_idx (tenant_id, cluster_id, ts DESC) and events_ts_idx (ts) from 0015. Data: 1,000,000 rows, type 'scrape_ok', cluster_id 1 to 5, ts spread over the last 1e6 seconds, no 'rare_type' rows, then ANALYZE. Query shape is the handler's, with LIMIT 100. (1) type='rare_type', no cluster: Parallel Seq Scan on events, Rows Removed by Filter 333333 per worker, Execution Time 35.081 ms. (2) type='scrape_ok', no cluster: Index Scan Backward using events_ts_idx, Execution Time 0.144 ms. (3) type='rare_type' with cluster_id=3: Parallel Seq Scan, Execution Time 32.437 ms, so the lookup index is not chosen at this size.
```

**Suggested fix:** Default to a bounded window (for example the last 24h) when from is absent, enforce a maximum span, add an index on (tenant_id,cluster_id,type,ts) for the type filter, and add LIMIT where the response is a list.

**Fix notes:** The events LIMIT already exists, so drop that part. An index on (tenant_id, type, ts DESC) helps only at much larger volume. The cheap change is a default window for /statements when from is absent (for example 24h), and a documented maximum span on both endpoints.

Status: open

### SA-12 — Ungrouped ASH reports resolution_seconds=1 while rows are 10-second windows (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_ash.go:189`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The ungrouped path sets ResolutionSeconds: 1 (lines 159, 182, 189), but each metrics_ash row is an aggregation over the agent's 10-second window (api_ash.go:286-287, cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:21).

**Failure scenario:** A client that spaces samples by resolution_seconds plots ungrouped rows 10 times too densely, or computes samples-per-second off by a factor of 10.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_ash.go:189 resp := ashResponse{ResolutionSeconds: 1, Statistical: true}; api_ash.go:286-287 ashWindowSeconds comment; cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:21 const ashWindow = 10 * time.Second.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code reading confirmed. The ungrouped path sets ResolutionSeconds: 1 at api_ash.go:189 (handleASH). Lines 159 and 182 are the no-pool and ASH-disabled responses, also in handleASH. handleASHTop also hard-codes 1 at lines 548 and 567. Rows: the agent aggregates over ashWindow = 10 * time.Second (cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:21), and api_ash.go:285-288 documents ashWindowSeconds as the finest stored resolution. The grouped path uses ashResolution, a multiple of 10 (api_ash.go:300-307). The UI never uses the ungrouped path: AshPage.tsx:17 sets DEFAULT_GROUP = 'wait_event_type', readGroup (line 39-40) never returns empty, and line 126 always sends group_by. So this is an API-only contract issue. Also, checks.ash.interval is configurable (ash.go SetInterval), so 1 is not a guaranteed sample interval either. Not reproduced at runtime.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only. api_ash.go:189 (ResolutionSeconds: 1 on the ungrouped path); api_ash.go:285-288 (ashWindowSeconds = 10); cmd/pglens-agent/ash.go:21 (ashWindow = 10s); web/src/features/ash/AshPage.tsx:17, :39-40, :126 (UI always sends group_by).
```

**Suggested fix:** Return ashWindowSeconds (10) for raw rows, and document resolution_seconds in openapi as the row spacing.

**Fix notes:** For the ungrouped rows, report ashWindowSeconds (10). handleASHTop's value (lines 548 and 567) describes an aggregated range, so document it rather than report 1. Document resolution_seconds in api/openapi.yaml as the spacing between rows (the ASH example at ~line 1376 shows 1 for the top endpoint).

Status: open

### SA-15 — Host unavailable response leaks the zero time as sampled_at (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_host.go:19`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** hostAPIResponse.SampledAt is a time.Time with json:"sampled_at,omitempty". omitempty has no effect on struct types, so the zero value is emitted. The openapi HostResponse also declares a metrics map while the server emits flattened keys.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The UI shows a sample timestamp of year 1 for an unavailable host, and typed clients that expect null or an absent key misparse it.

**Correction (from verification):** The UI claim is refuted: web/src/features/instance/HostSection.tsx renders only query.data.reason in the unavailable branch and never reads sampled_at.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_host.go:19 SampledAt time.Time `json:"sampled_at,omitempty"`; api_host.go:92 "sampled_at": resp.SampledAt. Overlay: unavailable response contains "sampled_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z".
```

**Verification reasoning:** The defect is real but only on the unavailable path. api_host.go:81 writes hostAPIResponse with a zero SampledAt. omitempty has no effect on struct types such as time.Time (api_host.go:19), so sampled_at 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z is emitted. The success path builds its own map (api_host.go:88-100) with a real sample time, so it is unaffected. The UI claim is refuted: web/src/features/instance/HostSection.tsx renders only query.data.reason in the unavailable branch and never reads sampled_at. The year-1 string is a valid RFC 3339 date-time, so typed clients do not misparse it; the defect is a sentinel where the contract implies absence. The second half holds as contract drift: openapi HostResponse (api/openapi.yaml ~405-415) declares a metrics map, but the server never emits it (Metrics is json:"-" and the keys are flattened at api_host.go:95-100). HostSection.metricValues tolerates both shapes.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in internal/server (deleted): chi router with API{pool:nil}, GET /api/v1/instances/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111/host. Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA15HostUnavailable -v ./internal/server/. Output: status=200 body={"instance_id":"11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111","available":false,"reason":"target is not local to any agent","sampled_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

**Suggested fix:** Use *time.Time (nil when no sample) with omitempty, and align the openapi HostResponse with the flattened shape.

**Fix notes:** Use SampledAt time.Time with json:"sampled_at,omitzero". go.mod is go 1.27.1, so omitzero is available, and omitempty will not work on time.Time. A *time.Time with omitempty also works. Align the openapi HostResponse: document the flattened host_* keys and drop or describe metrics.

Status: open

### SA-20 — UI sends no CSP, frame or referrer headers; state-changing routes rely only on SameSite=Strict (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/webui.go:20`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** SPAHandler sets only X-Content-Type-Options (webui.go:20). There is no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, and no Referrer-Policy. State-changing routes have no Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check and depend on the SameSite=Strict cookie alone, which does not cover same-site sibling subdomains.

**Failure scenario:** If a same-site subdomain is compromised, it can issue cross-subdomain requests that carry the session cookie, and the UI can be framed without restriction.

**Evidence:**

```text
webui.go:20 w.Header().Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff") is the only security header set in this handler.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The factual claims hold. SPAHandler (webui.go:20) sets only X-Content-Type-Options, and the repro shows no CSP, X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors or Referrer-Policy header. NewRouter (http.go:14-61) installs only Recoverer and RequireCredential, with no header middleware. No repo file sets these headers. No Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check exists anywhere: RequireCredential (session.go:153-182) accepts the session cookie on every method for every /api/ path. The cookie is SameSite=Strict (session.go:293), so cross-site requests and cross-site iframes carry no cookie, which blunts both CSRF and clickjacking. The residual gap is same-site: a compromised sibling subdomain is same-site and its requests carry the cookie. createSilence decodes JSON without a Content-Type check (api_alerts.go:310), so a text/plain simple POST with no preflight would be accepted there. That makes the missing Origin check a real defence-in-depth gap, but exploitation needs an attacker already on a same-site host. Hence low, not a security hole.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (deleted): SPAHandler over fstest.MapFS, GET /. Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA20SPAHeaders -v ./internal/server/. Response headers: Content-Type, Accept-Ranges, Content-Length, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate. Code grep for Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin across cmd and internal found only webui.go:20 and the SameSite line at session.go:293.
```

**Suggested fix:** Send a CSP (default-src 'self' plus frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options DENY and Referrer-Policy no-referrer, and reject unsafe methods whose Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site is not same-origin.

**Fix notes:** Add a router-level header middleware in NewRouter (http.go), not only in SPAHandler, so API and error responses get the headers too. Before a strict CSP, check the built index.html for inline scripts or styles. Add an Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check for unsafe methods in RequireCredential, and require application/json on JSON-body writes such as createSilence.

Status: open

### SA-21 — writeJSON ignores the encode error; NaN values produce 200 with an empty body (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:102`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** writeJSON discards the error from json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v) (line 102), after the status header is already written. A float NaN or Inf in a payload fails encoding and yields a 200 with no body.

**Failure scenario:** A future metric or ratio division by zero produces NaN, and the client receives an empty 200 that fails JSON parsing with no server-side log.

**Evidence:**

```text
api.go:99-102: writeJSON sets the status and then _ = json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v). Overlay test: a NaN value returns status=200 bodyLen=0 (SA-NAN). No in-scope producer of NaN was found in this review.
```

**Verification reasoning:** writeJSON (api.go:99-103) writes the status header before encoding and discards the Encode error, so a failed encode leaves a 200 with an empty body. Reproduced. The defect is latent: I found no current in-scope producer. The wire envelope is encoding/json (internal/wire/envelope.go), and json.Marshal rejects NaN and Inf, so NaN cannot enter metrics through the agent path. Handler divisions are guarded (handleTables api_relations.go:115-116 checks live > 0; the statement mean is a SQL CASE). A fix in writeJSON covers every handler. Companion latent bug not in the finding: mustJSON (api_host.go:104-107) also swallows the Marshal error, so a NaN host metric yields nil bytes, json.RawMessage(nil) encodes as null, and the host endpoint returns 200 null. That path is established by reading, not run.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (deleted): writeJSON(recorder, 200, map[string]any{"v": math.NaN()}). Command: go test -count=1 -run TestZZSA21NaNWriteJSON -v ./internal/server/. Output: SA21 nan: status=200 bodyLen=0 body="". Control with 1.5: status=200 body={"v":1.5} with a trailing newline.
```

**Suggested fix:** Encode to a buffer first, log and return 500 on error, and sanitize NaN/Inf to null before encoding.

**Fix notes:** Encode to a buffer first (json.Marshal); on error log it and call writeError(500) before WriteHeader. Apply the same fix to mustJSON and its callers in api_host.go. writeError also ignores its Encode error, but it encodes only strings, so it is harmless.

Status: open

### SA-22 — Lock and activity endpoints silently hide decode failures as empty or healthy results (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_locks.go:83`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** handleLocks treats a failed json.Unmarshal of the stored tree as an empty tree (line 83-86), and stale is computed from the snapshot timestamp, so the response can show no blocking with stale=false. handleActivity ignores the labels unmarshal error (line 131).

**Failure scenario:** A corrupt lock_snapshots row makes the UI report no lock contention as fresh data.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_locks.go:83 if json.Unmarshal(raw, &tree) == nil { ... }; api_locks.go:131 _ = json.Unmarshal(labels, &m.Labels).
```

**Verification reasoning:** The code behaviour is real. internal/server/api_locks.go:83-86 uses `if json.Unmarshal(raw, &tree) == nil {...}` with no else branch, so a decode failure yields empty nodes and sessions. Stale is computed only from the row timestamp (line 78), so a fresh row with an undecodable tree returns stale=false. The stated trigger is not reachable as written. lock_snapshots.tree is `jsonb NOT NULL` (internal/store/migrations/0008_locks.sql:6), so Postgres rejects non-JSON text and there is no 'corrupt row'. The only writer is the agent's fixed lockTree struct (internal/check/locks.go:39-43, 182), fed through WriteLockSnapshots (internal/store/write.go:527-537). A decode failure therefore needs a shape mismatch, such as version skew or a writer change. I did not find a writer that produces one, so the severity stays low. The labels half (api_locks.go:131, `_ = json.Unmarshal(labels, &m.Labels)`) is unreachable from producer data: metrics labels are marshalled from map[string]string (internal/store/write.go:322-331 and 354-361) into a jsonb column with default '{}'. Test coverage: api_locks_integration_test.go only checks the happy path, and api_locks_test.go only checks the absent-row case, so no test pins the empty-on-failure behaviour.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in package server, since deleted (the mock setup is in mockpool_test.go): mockPool{queryRowVals: []*mockRow{{vals: []any{time.Now(), []byte(raw)}}}}, routed via (&API{pool: mp}).registerContentionRoutes(chi.NewRouter()), GET /api/v1/locks?instance_id=<uuid>. Command: `go test ./internal/server/ -run TestVerifySA22 -v -count=1`. Decisive output: raw=[] gives 200 {"stale":false,"nodes":[],"sessions":[]}. raw={"nodes":{"pid":1},"sessions":[]} gives 200 with stale=false and nodes []. Control raw={"nodes":[{"pid":1}],"sessions":[]} gives nodes [{"pid":1}]. Only the first two are the bug, and the test passed, confirming the silent fallback. Not run: a tree of `{}` or one missing `sessions` decodes without error, so `resp.Nodes = tree.Nodes` assigns nil and the response carries `"nodes":null` (Go encodes a nil slice as null; reasoned from encoding rules, not executed).
```

**Suggested fix:** Return 500 or set stale=true with a reason when the stored tree cannot be decoded, and log label decode failures.

**Fix notes:** Location: internal/server/api_locks.go:79-86 (the json.Unmarshal into the tree struct). Fix options: return 500 on decode failure, or set stale=true with a reason. Log the error. Pitfall 1: a successful decode of `{}` or a tree missing `sessions` overwrites the []json.RawMessage{} defaults with nil, so the response emits `null`. Guard the nil slices after decode, not just the error branch. Pitfall 2: this is not a corrupt-row fix. jsonb guarantees valid JSON, so the realistic case is a shape mismatch. Add a test that feeds a wrong-shape tree. Nothing existing pins the current behaviour. Labels: api_locks.go:131 is unreachable from producer data. Logging the error is enough, and it is low priority.

Status: open

### SA-23 — Finding mute accepts any future until, with no upper bound (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/api_findings.go:199`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** muteFinding checks only until.After(time.Now()) (line 199), so an arbitrary far-future timestamp is accepted and a critical finding can be silenced indefinitely with no maximum duration.

**Failure scenario:** An operator or compromised token mutes a critical finding until 9999-12-31 and it never reappears in the default open list.

**Evidence:**

```text
api_findings.go:198-202: until, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, in.Until); if err != nil || !until.After(time.Now()) { ... 400 }.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The claim holds. internal/server/api_findings.go:198-202 checks only `until.After(time.Now())`, with no upper bound. time.Parse RFC3339 caps the year at 9999, so the effective limit is year 9999, which is practically indefinite. Nothing else bounds it. The OpenAPI spec says only 'future' (api/openapi.yaml:1750, MuteFindingRequest 619-624). The UI presets cap at 7 days (web/src/features/findings/MuteDialog.tsx:18-24), but the 'Explicit timestamp' datetime-local input accepts any future value (MuteDialog.tsx:33-43, 84). The mute is persisted, and the advisor upsert (internal/advisor/store.go:54) keeps state='muted' while muted_until > last_seen, so the finding stays muted across evaluation passes. The default list excludes muted findings (api_findings.go:100). Additional facts from the reasoning. Any caller that passes RequireCredential (http.go:25) may mute: a UI session or any holder of the shared agent bootstrap token, so an agent host can mute too. Mutes leave no audit row. internal/server/api_audit.go covers command_audit only. The reason is already required and non-empty (api_findings.go:194), so the suggested 'require a reason' is already in place. Severity stays low (hardening plus missing audit), not a critical security hole.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (since deleted): mockPool{execRows: []int64{1}}, routed via (&API{pool: mp}).registerFindingsRoutes(chi.NewRouter()). POST /api/v1/findings/query.slow_mean/mute with body {"reason":"silence forever","until":"9999-12-31T23:59:59Z"}. Command: `go test ./internal/server/ -run TestVerifySA23 -v -count=1`. Decisive output: code=200 body {"finding_id":"query.slow_mean","mute_reason":"silence forever","muted_until":"9999-12-31T23:59:59Z","state":"muted"}. Control with until=2000-01-01T00:00:00Z gives code=400 'until must be a future RFC3339 timestamp'.
```

**Suggested fix:** Cap the mute duration (for example 90 days) and require a non-empty reason that is logged.

**Fix notes:** Location: internal/server/api_findings.go:198-202 (muteFinding). Add a maximum duration, for example until <= now+90d, returning 400. Mirror the cap in api/openapi.yaml (MuteFindingRequest/muteFinding description) and in web/src/features/findings/MuteDialog.tsx (the explicit field has no max). Regenerate web/src/api/generated.ts if the spec changes. For the audit gap, add a mute audit row or table, since command_audit is commands-only. The advisor upsert at internal/advisor/store.go:54 reads muted_until, so a cap does not break expiry.

Status: open

### SA-24 — Constant-time password compare leaks the password length (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `internal/server/session.go:277`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** constantTimePasswordMatch returns early on a length mismatch (session.go:277), and Auth.Validate in internal/server/auth.go returns early on a length mismatch too. The early return reveals the length of the secret to a remote caller.

**Failure scenario:** An attacker learns the password length by timing responses, which reduces the search space for brute force.

**Evidence:**

```text
session.go:277 func constantTimePasswordMatch(got, want string) bool; auth.go: early return when lengths differ before subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The length leak is real but not practically exploitable. The Go standard library documents that ConstantTimeCompare 'returns 0 immediately' on a length mismatch (/usr/local/go/src/crypto/subtle/constant_time.go:17-20). internal/server/session.go:277-283 (constantTimePasswordMatch) returns early on length mismatch, and its dummy ConstantTimeCompare call is a no-op for timing. The same pattern is at internal/server/auth.go:30-35 (Auth.Validate). That path is the more exposed one: it runs on every /api/ request through RequireCredential and on ingest, and it has no failure sleep. The session path sleeps 250 ms on a failed login (session.go:219). That is a constant offset, so it does not hide the nanosecond difference by itself. Network and timer jitter are in the milliseconds, so a remote attacker cannot resolve a ~15 ns difference in practice. Severity low (hardening).

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary benchmarks in package server (since deleted): BenchmarkVerifySA24LengthMismatch calls constantTimePasswordMatch("short-guess", "a-much-longer-configured-password-value"). BenchmarkVerifySA24LengthMatch calls constantTimePasswordMatch with equal lengths where the last byte differs. Command: `go test ./internal/server/ -run '^$' -bench VerifySA24 -benchtime=2s -count=3`, Go 1.27.2 on linux/amd64. Decisive output: LengthMismatch 0.9525, 0.9904, 0.9155 ns/op. LengthMatch 16.88, 15.47, 15.81 ns/op.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compare SHA-256 digests of both values with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, so the length is not observable.

**Fix notes:** Fix both locations, not only session.go. (1) internal/server/session.go:277-283 constantTimePasswordMatch. (2) internal/server/auth.go:30-35 Auth.Validate. Compare SHA-256 digests of both values with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, and drop the dummy calls, which do nothing for timing. Auth.Validate runs on every request, so the per-request SHA-256 cost is negligible.

Status: open

### SA-25 — Openapi documents fewer status codes and auth schemes than the server implements (CONFIRMED, server-api)

**Location:** `api/openapi.yaml:1`

**Category:** docs · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** POST /api/v1/session is documented with 204, 400 and 401 but the server also returns 503 and 500. /api/v1/agents/{agent_id}/commands is documented as agentBearer-only and 403 for a non-owner, but the server also accepts a session cookie (commands.go:235).

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** Generated clients miss the 503/500 branches and the session-authenticated access path, so error handling and access reviews rely on incomplete docs.

**Correction (from verification):** The cookie claim is REFUTED.

**Evidence:**

```text
session.go login handler returns 503 and 500 paths not in openapi; commands.go:235-244 authenticatedAgent accepts the session cookie path.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The finding is partly right and partly wrong. The session-login gap is real. api/openapi.yaml:1810-1813 documents POST /api/v1/session with only 204, 400 and 401. internal/server/session.go:223-225 returns 503 when the store is nil, and session.go:228-231 returns 500 when token creation fails. The 503 is effectively unreachable in production, since cmd/pglens-server/main.go:113 always builds a non-nil store. The 500 fires only on a crypto/rand failure. The cookie claim is REFUTED. internal/server/commands.go:235-244 (authenticatedAgent) calls s.auth.Validate(r), which reads only the Authorization Bearer header and never the session cookie. A valid session cookie on the poll endpoint returns 401 'agent authentication failed', which matches the spec's 401 (openapi.yaml:1917). The spec's poll description is therefore accurate on the cookie point. There is one real undocumented case. A valid bearer with no X-PGLENS-Agent-ID header returns 403 'agent identity header is required' (commands.go:249-253), while the spec's 403 covers only the non-owner case (openapi.yaml:1918-1922). openapi_test.go (TestOpenAPICoversEveryRoute, TestOpenAPIAgentRoutesAreBearerOnly) checks path, method and security only, not response codes, so the gap is not caught. Severity low (docs drift).

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test (since deleted), run as `go test ./internal/server/ -run TestVerifySA25 -v -count=1`. (a) newSessionTestServer with a valid session cookie and no bearer, GET /api/v1/agents/<uuid>/commands: decisive output code=401. (b) Same server, Authorization: Bearer agent-token and no agent header: code=403. (c) RegisterSessionRoutes with a nil store, POST /api/v1/session with the correct password: <redacted> body {"error":"session_unavailable","detail":"session store is not configured"}. Note: the reproduction's cookie check used the full middleware chain via NewRouter, which is the production path.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add the missing responses and security alternatives to openapi and regenerate generated.ts.

**Fix notes:** Edit api/openapi.yaml: add 500 and 503 to POST /api/v1/session (around lines 1810-1813). Add the 403 'agent identity header is required' cause to the poll 403 description (around 1918-1922). Drop the cookie-acceptance claim entirely. The poll endpoint is Bearer-only in both spec and handler. Regenerate web/src/api/generated.ts after the spec change. Optional: add a response-code coverage check to openapi_test.go. The current tests would not catch this class of drift.

Status: open

### AA-06 — Silence regex can be broken out of its anchor and match every alert (CONFIRMED, alert-advisor)

**Location:** `internal/alert/silence.go:37`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** A regex matcher value is spliced into '^(?:' + value + ')$' without checking that it is balanced. A value with an early close paren and an alternation, such as 'nope)|(.*', produces '^(?:nope)|(.*)$', which matches any string. Validate compiles the same wrapped form, so the value passes validation. VERIFIED in a scratch copy: a silence for rule_id 'nope)|(.*' matches the unrelated rule 'replica.lag_high'.

**Failure scenario:** An operator creates a silence for one noisy rule with a regex that contains an unbalanced group. Every alert on the instance is silenced: Suppressed is true, notifications stop, and the UI shows suppressed alerts without a visible reason.

**Evidence:**

```text
silence.go:37: if _, e := regexp.Compile("^(?:" + m.Value + ")$"); e != nil { ; silence.go:56: re, e := regexp.Compile("^(?:" + m.Value + ")$")
```

**Verification reasoning:** The mechanism is real. Silence.Validate (silence.go:37) and Matches (silence.go:56) both wrap the value in '^(?:' + v + ')$'. For nope)|(.* that gives ^(?:nope)|(.*)$, which matches any string. createSilence calls Validate (api_alerts.go, createSilence), so the value is accepted. I downgraded from medium: only alternation-shaped values escape the wrapper, and anyone who can create a silence can already silence everything with '.*', so there is no capability gain. The input has to be deliberately contrived.

**Repro:**

```text
Same temporary file and command. TestReviewAA06: Validate returns nil for 'nope)|(.*'. Matches on rule_id 'replica.lag_high' returns true. The control 'nope' matches only itself (false for replica.lag_high). Validate rejects 'foo)', which shows that only balanced breakouts escape. Passes.
```

**Suggested fix:** Compile the matcher value on its own (regexp.Compile(m.Value)) in Validate and reject it when it does not compile; balanced groups cannot then escape the wrapper. Compile each matcher once rather than on every Matches call.

**Fix notes:** The suggested fix is correct. Go's regexp rejects an unmatched ')' in the raw value, and every breakout needs one, so compiling the raw value in Validate rejects exactly these shapes. Compiling once per matcher, not per Matches call, is a separate performance improvement.

Status: open

### AA-17 — Index definition facts are loaded without a bound (CONFIRMED, alert-advisor)

**Location:** `internal/advisor/snapshot.go:763`

**Category:** performance · **Confidence:** low

**Description:** loadIndexFacts reads every object_facts row of kind index_def for the instance with no limit or time bound, on every pass. The sibling-instance load (snapshot.go:591-595) also joins object_facts for all kinds. The volume is proportional to the number of indexes, which can be large. Not measured in this review.

**Failure scenario:** An instance with tens of thousands of indexes loads all definitions each pass, and the advisor run exceeds its per-instance budget.

**Evidence:**

```text
snapshot.go:763: SELECT datname, key, COALESCE(value_text, ''), COALESCE(labels->>'def_hash', '') FROM object_facts WHERE tenant_id='default' AND instance_id=$1 AND kind='index_def'
```

**Verification reasoning:** loadIndexFacts (snapshot.go:763-764) reads every object_facts row of kind index_def for the instance with no limit and no time bound, and it runs on every pass. Two parts of the finding are wrong or incomplete. The sibling join does not cover all kinds: snapshot.go:595-596 restricts it to 'setting', 'index_def' and 'backup'. Also, loadFacts (snapshot.go:440-443) already reads every object_facts row of every kind for the instance on each pass, so index_def rows are read twice. Growth is monotonic: index_def rows are upserted (store/write.go:500) and never deleted, since only check_skip and check_partial rows are deleted (write.go:508, 518), and object_facts has no retention policy (0007_facts.sql:42-50). The impact is unmeasured. Low is right for realistic index counts, because the agent only ships about 200 indexes per database per scrape.

**Repro:**

```text
Code-level verification only. Evidence: snapshot.go:440-443 (loadFacts, no kind filter), snapshot.go:763-764 (loadIndexFacts, unbounded), snapshot.go:595-596 (sibling join restricted to three kinds), store/write.go:500 (upsert), write.go:508 and 518 (only check_skip and check_partial are deleted).
```

**Suggested fix:** Limit the query to the indexes present in the current metrics_indexes window, or cache definitions and reload only changed rows (by observed_at).

**Fix notes:** The bigger read is loadFacts (snapshot.go:440-443), which already loads index_def rows for every kind, so limiting loadIndexFacts alone does not remove the duplicated read. Limiting to indexes in the current metrics_indexes window needs the loader to run after loadIndexes, or to filter by the names in s.Indexes. Growth needs pruning of index_def rows that have not been seen for a long time, since nothing deletes them today.

Status: open

### WD-05 — Healthy copy claims no lag is measurable, but the server reports ok with lag up to the threshold (CONFIRMED, web-data)

**Location:** `web/src/lib/fleet.ts:112`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** describeHealth for 'ok' says no replication lag is measurable. The server reports ok while replay lag is within healthLagThresholdSeconds, and degraded only above it. The spec example also shows health ok with a non-zero lag value. The unit test asserts the same misleading phrase.

**Failure scenario:** An operator sees a cluster marked healthy, with copy saying no lag is measurable, while the same cluster shows 20 s of replay lag. The operator dismisses real lag as absent.

**Evidence:**

```text
lib/fleet.ts:112 'Healthy: a primary is present, all instances are up, and no replication lag is measurable.' internal/server/api.go:157 healthLagThresholdSeconds (30 s per the server comment); api.go:177-180 degraded only when lag > threshold, otherwise ok. lib/fleet.test.ts:17 'expect(sentence).toMatch(/no replication lag/i)'.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The inaccuracy is confirmed, but severity is corrected to low. healthForCluster returns ok whenever max replay lag is <= 30 s (api.go:177-180). The copy at fleet.ts:112 says no replication lag is measurable, and fleet.test.ts:17 asserts it. The sentence is not visible text: ClusterCard.tsx:35 exposes describeHealth only in the health badge's aria-label, and ClusterPage.tsx:125 shows only the raw health word. The visible contradiction is an 'ok' badge next to a visible 'Max replay lag' row. So the harm is limited to assistive-technology users, plus docs drift: the README 'Fields explained' rule (ok = no replication lag; degraded = any lag > 0) is also stale against the 30 s server rule.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary Go internal test (same as WD-04): go test -count=1 -run TestReviewWD04Health -v ./internal/server/ gives 'healthForCluster(primary=1, anyDown=false, instances=2, lag=20s) = "ok"'. ### WD-11 — formatDuration rounds seconds to 60 inside a minute (CONFIRMED, web-data)
```

**Location:** `web/src/lib/format/duration.ts:20`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Seconds are rounded after the minute split, so a value just under an hour carries into '60s' instead of rolling over to the next minute.

**Failure scenario:** A lag or age of 3599.999 s is shown as '59m 60s' in the replication and activity columns.

**Evidence:**

```text
lib/format/duration.ts:20-22 'if (remaining > 0 || parts.length === 0) { parts.push(`${localizedNumber(remaining, locale, { maximumFractionDigits: 2 })}s`) }'. Verified formatDuration(3599.999) returns '59m 60s'.
```

**Verification reasoning:** web/src/lib/format/duration.ts:13-22: minutes are split from the unrounded remainder, and only then is the seconds part rounded to two decimals (line 21, maximumFractionDigits: 2). So a remainder of 59.999 prints as '60s' after '59m', and the carry never reaches the minutes. Reproduced with the exact function body.

**Repro:**

```text
Copied web/src/lib/format/duration.ts verbatim (same shared stub as WD-09) and ran 'node repro.ts' with Node v24.14.1. Decisive output: formatDuration(3599.999) -> "59m 60s"; formatDuration(59.999) -> "60s"; formatDuration(86399.999) -> "23h 59m 60s"; formatDuration(3599.4) -> "59m 59.4s" (correct, so the defect is limited to values that round up to 60 s). Scratch files removed afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Round total seconds to the displayed precision before splitting into hours, minutes and seconds, so the carry propagates. Add a test for 3599.999 and 59.999.

**Fix notes:** Round the total seconds to the displayed precision (for example Math.round(seconds*100)/100) before splitting into days, hours, minutes and seconds, so the carry propagates. Add tests for 3599.999, 59.999 (expect 1m 0s) and 86399.999 (expect 1d 0h 0m 0s) in duration.test.ts.
