### WD-12 — Finding schema omits returned fields and POST mutes outside the spec path (CONFIRMED, web-data)

**Location:** `api/openapi.yaml:495`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The OpenAPI Finding schema omits first_seen, last_seen, resolved_at, muted_until and mute_reason, which the server returns. The server also mutes on any POST under /api/v1/findings/*, because findingPathID trims the /mute suffix only when it is present. That route is not in the spec. The web uses the documented paths at runtime, so the impact is for generated clients and automation.

**Failure scenario:** A client generated from the spec cannot read first_seen, last_seen or muted_until. Any POST to /api/v1/findings/{id} with a valid reason and until mutes the finding, and an automation built on the spec does not know that it mutes.

**Evidence:**

```text
api/openapi.yaml Finding schema lines 495-512 do not list the five fields. internal/server/api_findings.go:48 'r.Post("/api/v1/findings/*", a.muteFinding)'; api_findings.go:203 findingPathID(r, "mute") trims the suffix only when present.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The spec's Finding schema (api/openapi.yaml:495-512) omits first_seen, last_seen, resolved_at, muted_until and mute_reason, although the server returns them (api_findings.go findingSelect and findingJSON). Route: api_findings.go:48 'r.Post("/api/v1/findings/*", a.muteFinding)'. findingPathID trims the /mute suffix only when present, so POST /api/v1/findings/{id} mutes that finding. The spec documents only POST /api/v1/findings/{finding-id}/mute (openapi.yaml:1746). The parity test hides this. internal/server/openapi_test.go:220-232 canonicalizeRegisteredRoute maps every non-GET catch-all under /api/v1/findings/* to the /mute template, so TestOpenAPICoversEveryRoute (lines 145-191) treats the bare-id POST as documented. The web uses the documented path (web/src/api/findings.ts:125), so runtime impact is limited to generated clients and automation. The spec has no additionalProperties: false, so the extra fields are valid but undocumented.

**Repro:**

```text
Code trace, no run: api/openapi.yaml:495-512 (no five fields) + api_findings.go:48 (POST catch-all) + findingPathID trimming only when the suffix is present + openapi.yaml:1746 (documented mute path) + openapi_test.go:220-232 (masks the bare POST).
```

**Suggested fix:** Add the five fields to the Finding schema and regenerate generated.ts. Restrict the POST route to the /mute suffix and return 404 otherwise. The fix is server-side, outside web/src.

**Fix notes:** Server side, outside web/src. Restrict the POST route to the /mute suffix and return 404 otherwise. Make the same change for the DELETE catch-all at api_findings.go:49, which has the same shape; I did not verify the unmute handler body. Change canonicalizeRegisteredRoute in openapi_test.go so the test stops masking the bare-id routes. Add the five fields to the Finding schema and regenerate web/src/api/generated.ts.

### WD-15 — parseLargeIntStrings is dead code and its comment claims protection that is not active (CONFIRMED, web-data)

**Location:** `web/src/api/client.ts:83`

**Category:** docs · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** parseLargeIntStrings rewrites 16 or more digit queryid numbers into strings, but nothing calls it. Its comment says statements, ash and plans responses pass through it, which is false. The server currently emits queryid as a string, so there is no present precision loss, but the comment implies a guard that does not exist.

**Failure scenario:** A maintainer relies on the comment, types queryid as a number in a new endpoint, and a 19-digit queryid loses its last digits in the browser.

**Evidence:**

```text
api/client.ts:83-86 'export function parseLargeIntStrings(raw: string): unknown { const rewritten = raw.replace(/(?<!\\)("queryid"\s*:\s*)(-?\d{16,})(?=\s*[,}])/g, ...); return JSON.parse(rewritten) as unknown }'. A grep over web/src finds only the definition.
```

**Verification reasoning:** parseLargeIntStrings has no caller in any non-test source file. A repo-wide grep (excluding node_modules) finds only its definition at web/src/api/client.ts:83, its own unit tests in web/src/api/client.test.ts (lines 3, 94-116), and the stale plan text in docs/plans/003_plan-Frontend/phase_07.md:117-135. The doc comment at client.ts:78-82 says it parses responses from /api/v1/statements, /api/v1/ash, /api/v1/ash/top and /api/v1/plans, which is false in the present tense. Two parts of the comment are wrong, not just the call site. (a) /api/v1/plans carries no queryid: planHistoryItem in internal/server/api_plans.go:12-19 has no queryid field, and the OpenAPI Plan schema has none. (b) The server already emits queryid as a decimal string on /api/v1/ash and /api/v1/ash/top (internal/server/api_ash.go:48-50 and 626 use strconv.FormatInt into a string; formatQueryID at 637-643 returns *string). The OpenAPI spec (api/openapi.yaml lines 258, 299, 335) types queryid as a string with a digits pattern. So there is no present precision loss, and the function is a leftover from the phase_07 plan, where queryid was a JSON number. The failure scenario (a future numeric queryid silently losing digits) is hypothetical, so the severity stays low under the docs-drift rubric. I did not read the statements handler in Go, so the string claim for /api/v1/statements rests on the OpenAPI schema only.

**Repro:**

```text
Run from the worktree: `grep -rn "parseLargeIntStrings" --exclude-dir=node_modules .` Output: docs/plans/003_plan-Frontend/phase_07.md:117, :131, :134, :135; web/src/api/client.ts:83; web/src/api/client.test.ts:3, :94, :99, :103, :112. No non-test source file calls it. Server emission: internal/server/api_ash.go:48-50 comment 'Keep them as decimal strings in JSON', QueryID *string on ashBucket; api_ash.go:626 entry.QueryID = strconv.FormatInt(qid, 10); internal/server/api_plans.go:12-19 planHistoryItem has no queryid field. The tokensave MCP graph refused every call (branch mismatch: served 'main', worktree on another branch), so this was checked with grep and Read only.
```

**Suggested fix:** Delete the function, or wire it into the fetch path with a test using a 19-digit queryid. Correct the comment in either case.

**Fix notes:** Preferred fix: delete parseLargeIntStrings (web/src/api/client.ts lines 78-86) together with its describe block in web/src/api/client.test.ts (lines 94-116) and the import on line 3. Deleting only the function breaks that test file. The finding's evidence grep also omits client.test.ts, which references the function. If the function is kept instead, the comment must say it is unused, must drop /api/v1/plans from the endpoint list (its response has no queryid), and must not describe the endpoints as already routed through it. Do not reintroduce a numeric-queryid rewrite unless some endpoint actually emits a numeric queryid; the ash endpoints already emit strings. Optionally mark step 4 of docs/plans/003_plan-Frontend/phase_07.md as superseded, since it still says queryid is a JSON number. No files were created or changed during this verification.

**Description:** When the alerts query fails, alertsAvailable is false and firingAlerts falls back to an empty array. The cluster cards receive no alert count, and ClusterCard defaults alertCount to 0 and hides the badge unless it is above 0. A card looks alert-free although the alert data is unknown. The summary bar shows 'Unavailable', but the cards do not.

**Verification reasoning:** FleetPage.tsx:69 sets firingAlerts = alertsQuery.data ?? EMPTY_ALERTS, and lines 238-241 pass alertCount = 0 when alerts failed. ClusterCard.tsx:22 defaults alertCount to 0 and line 100 renders the badge only above 0, so the card shows no badge. ### WU-23 — Signal policy branch reads a field the API never returns (CONFIRMED, web-ui)

**Location:** `web/src/features/auth/RequireSession.tsx:23`

**Category:** ux · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** On a session query error the guard renders 'Impossibile verificare la sessione.' with no retry control, and the session query uses REFRESH.static (interval 0), so it never refetches on its own.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** A brief network blip at page load leaves the operator on an error screen with no action except reloading.


**Suggested fix:** Add a retry button that calls the session query's refetch.

**Fix notes:** Add a retry control in RequireSession.tsx at the error branch that calls the session query's refetch (useSession spreads the query object, so refetch is available). Describe the defect as 'no in-page retry', not 'no refetch'.

### DR-09 — Docs say pg_control functions are superuser-only; PUBLIC has EXECUTE by default, and the test REVOKE hides it (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql:41`

**Category:** docs · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The script comment says the pg_control functions are restricted to superusers by default and need explicit EXECUTE grants. README L164 says that without them cluster identity falls back to cluster_name. On fresh PostgreSQL 15 to 19 clusters, PUBLIC has EXECUTE on pg_control_system() and pg_control_checkpoint(), so the role can call them without the grant. The harness REVOKEs EXECUTE from PUBLIC to mimic the docs, so INT-PERM-002 passes only because of that artificial REVOKE.

**Failure scenario:** Operators skip the grant believing identity falls back, but the agent reads the real cluster identity. A hardened cluster that revoked PUBLIC gets a permission error, and the troubleshooting section (README L1566-1580) misdiagnoses it. The integration test never exercises the real default, so a change in that default goes unnoticed.

**Evidence:**

```text
monitoring_user.sql L41-44 comment. README L164 and L1375-1385. deploy/sql/README.md L42. test/pgtest/pgtest.go L406-407 REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC. test/pgtest/perm_test.go L26-36 expects SQLSTATE 42501 for RoleT0NoControl. Verified: fresh 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19 clusters grant PUBLIC EXECUTE, and pglens called both functions without an explicit grant.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The comment at deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql L41-42, README L164 and L1375-1385, and deploy/sql/README.md L42 say the pg_control functions are superuser-only by default and need an explicit grant. Fresh PG15 and PG19rc1 clusters grant PUBLIC EXECUTE on both, so the grant is only needed on hardened clusters. The harness REVOKEs from PUBLIC at test/pgtest/pgtest.go L406-407, which is why INT-PERM-002 passes. The troubleshooting section at README L1566-1580 is correct for a hardened cluster, so the claim that it misdiagnoses the problem does not hold. The impact is docs drift plus a test that does not exercise the default, so low rather than medium.

**Repro:**

```text
On PG15 (postgres:15.19-alpine) and PG19rc1: `select p.oid::regprocedure, has_function_privilege('public', p.oid, 'EXECUTE') from pg_proc p where p.proname in ('pg_control_system','pg_control_checkpoint')` returns pg_control_system()|t and pg_control_checkpoint()|t on both clusters. The default is PUBLIC EXECUTE.
```

**Suggested fix:** Correct the comment, deploy/sql/README.md L42 and README L164 and L1375-1385 to state the actual default (PUBLIC EXECUTE on PG15 to 19 unless hardening revokes it). Keep the GRANT as an idempotent no-op or drop it. In tests, do not REVOKE; add one test that asserts the default and one that covers the revoked case explicitly.

**Fix notes:** Correct the monitoring_user.sql L41-42 comment, README L164 and L1375-1385, and deploy/sql/README.md L42 to state the real default: PUBLIC has EXECUTE on PG15-19 unless hardening revokes it. Keep the GRANT as an idempotent step. Do not change the troubleshooting section at README L1566-1580, which is right for hardened clusters. In tests, drop the REVOKE at pgtest.go L406-407 for the default case and keep an explicit revoked-case test.

### DR-14 — PUBLIC can call pg_logical_emit_message, which writes WAL under default read-only (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql`

**Category:** readonly-invariant · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** pg_logical_emit_message is executable by PUBLIC and is not blocked by default_transaction_read_only on PG15 and PG18. It writes WAL, not user data, so the impact is WAL growth and spurious messages for logical decoding consumers.

**Failure scenario:** A monitoring session emits many transactional messages, which grows WAL and wakes logical decoding consumers.

**Evidence:**

```text
Verified: the T0 role under the default read-only setting called pg_logical_emit_message successfully on PG15 and PG18. The script contains no REVOKE for it.
```

**Verification reasoning:** On PG15 and PG19rc1, a pg_monitor role with default_transaction_read_only=on runs pg_logical_emit_message successfully, while CREATE TABLE is refused with 'cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction'. The emit also succeeds inside BEGIN READ ONLY, including under EXPLAIN ANALYZE. The comment at deploy/sql/monitoring_user.sql L78-81 says the server refuses writes, so that guarantee is incomplete. Reachability from pglens is narrow: internal/agent/exec_explain.go L38-67 replays an existing pg_stat_statements statement by queryid, so an operator cannot supply arbitrary SQL, and parameterised (normalised) statements are refused. The impact is WAL growth and messages to logical decoders, not user data, so low.

**Repro:**

```text
PG15 and PG19rc1, role rtest with pg_monitor and `ALTER ROLE rtest SET default_transaction_read_only = on`: `show default_transaction_read_only` returns on. `select pg_logical_emit_message(true,'dr14','probe')` returns 0/1935E88 on PG15 and 0/01B930D8 on PG19, rc 0. `create table ro_probe(i int)` returns ERROR cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction. On PG15, `BEGIN READ ONLY; EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT TEXT) SELECT pg_logical_emit_message(true,'dr14','probe'); COMMIT;` returns a plan and COMMIT rc 0. On PG19rc1 after REVOKE of the 4-argument overloads, the emit as rtest fails with ERROR permission denied for function pg_logical_emit_message.
```

**Suggested fix:** REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_logical_emit_message(boolean, text, text) and the bytea overload FROM PUBLIC in each monitored database.

**Fix notes:** The overloads differ by major. PG15-18 have (boolean,text,text) and (boolean,text,bytea), while PG19rc1 has (boolean,text,text,boolean) and (boolean,text,bytea,boolean). The 3-argument REVOKE in the suggested fix fails on 19 with function does not exist. Use a DO block that loops over pg_proc where proname='pg_logical_emit_message' and REVOKEs each oid::regprocedure, which works on every major. Verified: the 4-argument REVOKE works on 19rc1. REVOKE from PUBLIC also affects roles that legitimately use the function, such as CDC heartbeats, which need an explicit re-grant. It must run in each monitored database.

### DR-17 — Shipped compose and systemd units omit read_only, cap_drop, no-new-privileges and syscall or capability limits (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/docker-compose.yml:84`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The agent and server services have no read_only, cap_drop: [ALL] or security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]. The systemd units set NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp and ProtectSystem=strict but no CapabilityBoundingSet, RestrictAddressFamilies, SystemCallFilter or ProtectKernel* directives.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The agent parses untrusted database output. A compromise of that process gets a writable container root and the default capability set.

**Correction (from verification):** The failure scenario is overstated.

**Evidence:**

```text
deploy/docker-compose.yml L84-88 for the agent has none of those keys. deploy/systemd/*.service contain only the listed directives.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The missing keys are real. The review checkout's deploy/docker-compose.yml (the agent service L69-94 and the server service L29-67) has no read_only, cap_drop or security_opt. Both systemd units contain only NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome and Restart, with no CapabilityBoundingSet, RestrictAddressFamilies, SystemCallFilter or ProtectKernel*. The failure scenario is overstated. Dockerfile.agent L38 and Dockerfile.server L33 set USER nonroot on distroless static. A nonroot process has no effective capabilities by default, and the root filesystem is root-owned, so the writable-root and default-capability claim does not hold as written. Some writable surface remains (the volume at /var/lib/pglens and any writable /tmp). Hardening is still a sound defence-in-depth item.

**Repro:**

```text
Searched deploy/docker-compose.yml and deploy/systemd/*.service in both the worktree and the review checkout: none of cap_drop, read_only, security_opt, CapabilityBoundingSet, RestrictAddressFamilies, SystemCallFilter appear. Dockerfile.agent L36-38 and Dockerfile.server L31-33 show the USER nonroot lines.
```

**Suggested fix:** Add read_only: true with tmpfs for needed paths, cap_drop: [ALL], security_opt no-new-privileges to the compose services. Add CapabilityBoundingSet=, RestrictAddressFamilies= and SystemCallFilter=@system-service to the units.

**Fix notes:** Compose (deploy/docker-compose.yml, agent and server services): add cap_drop: [ALL] and security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]. Add read_only: true only with tmpfs for any path that must be written (the agent writes the pglens-agent-data volume; check /tmp). Units: add SystemCallFilter=@system-service, CapabilityBoundingSet= (empty) and RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6. Pitfalls: keep AF_UNIX, because a DSN may point at a local socket directory (TargetIsLocal handles '/' host). Do not set ProcSubset=pid on the agent, since it would hide /proc/meminfo, /proc/stat and /proc/loadavg. Be careful with ProtectProc on the agent. Correct the failure scenario text.

### DR-18 — Example pins proc_path to /proc, so the /host/proc mounts are unused (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `deploy/agent.example.yaml:11`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The example sets proc_path: /proc, and its comment says to use /host/proc inside a container. config.go gives the YAML value precedence over the HOST_PROC environment variable, so the /host/proc mount in deploy/docker-compose.yml is ignored and process-level collection reads the container's own /proc.

**Failure scenario:** Process-level host metrics in the container describe the container's namespace, not the host, so the UI shows mismatched data.

**Evidence:**

```text
deploy/agent.example.yaml L11. internal/agent/config.go L76-80 precedence: YAML proc_path, then HOST_PROC, then /proc. deploy/docker-compose.yml L85-86 mounts /proc and /sys at /host/proc and /host/sys.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The config fact holds. HostProcPath (internal/agent/config.go L76-84) gives YAML proc_path precedence over HOST_PROC, and deploy/agent.example.yaml L11-12 sets proc_path: /proc and sys_path: /sys, while its comment says to use /host/proc in a container. The compose file mounts /proc and /sys at /host/proc and /host/sys (L85-86) but sets neither HOST_PROC nor HOST_SYS, so the mounts are unused. The stated impact is wrong. internal/host/collector.go reads only gopsutil memory, swap, cpu count, cpu times and load, all kernel-wide procfs files. There is no per-process collection. The one real effect of the pin is on cgroup detection, which reads sysPath/fs/cgroup (cgroup.go L14-23). Also, in the shipped example, cmd/pglens-agent/run.go L164-170 appends host samples only for targets where TargetIsLocal is true. The example's only target has host_local: false, so the example ships no host metrics at all, and the 'UI shows mismatched data' scenario cannot occur there. The consumer search for HostProcPath was partly blocked (tokensave refused because the served branch is main), so I checked internal/host and run.go directly.

**Repro:**

```text
Read: internal/agent/config.go L76-84; deploy/agent.example.yaml L11-12; deploy/docker-compose.yml L85-86 (no HOST_PROC/HOST_SYS in the agent environment, L76-81); cmd/pglens-agent/run.go L153-170 (pending append gated by agent.TargetIsLocal); internal/host/collector.go L30-98.
```

**Suggested fix:** Remove proc_path from the example so HOST_PROC applies, or set proc_path: /host/proc in the container example. Make the comment match.

**Fix notes:** A fix that only removes proc_path does not work: compose sets neither HOST_PROC nor HOST_SYS, so the agent falls back to /proc. Either set proc_path: /host/proc and sys_path: /host/sys in deploy/agent.example.yaml, or add HOST_PROC=/host/proc and HOST_SYS=/host/sys to the compose agent environment. Pitfall: /host/sys makes applyCgroup read the host root cgroup (internal/host/cgroup.go L14-23), which usually has no memory.max, so the container's own memory limit would stop being applied. Decide that intentionally. Separate observation worth recording: the shipped example collects host metrics and discards them because its only target has host_local: false.

### DR-19 — Agent --healthcheck reports healthy on any HTTP response, including 503 for revoked or unauthorized (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `cmd/pglens-agent/main.go:66`

**Category:** ux · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The healthcheck returns 0 for any HTTP response. /healthz returns 503 for revoked, unauthorized and incompatible states (pusher.go L466-520), so the Docker HEALTHCHECK in Dockerfile.agent reports healthy while the agent is not shipping data. The comment calls this intentional, but the operator sees healthy.

**Failure scenario:** A token is revoked and /healthz returns 503 indefinitely. docker ps shows healthy, and no alert fires.

**Evidence:**

```text
cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L66-75 with the comment and return 0 on any response. internal/agent/pusher.go L466-520 returns 503 for those states. Dockerfile.agent HEALTHCHECK runs the --healthcheck binary.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The code matches the finding. runAgentHealthcheck (cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L58-75) returns 0 for any HTTP response. HealthzHandler (internal/agent/pusher.go L476-479) returns 503 for HealthIncompatible, HealthRevoked and HealthUnauthorized. Dockerfile.agent L36-37 runs the --healthcheck binary as HEALTHCHECK. A temporary test confirmed that a 503 response yields exit 0. The 'no alert fires' part is only partly true. Server-side, internal/alert/source_sql.go L110-116 marks revoked instances as Inapplicable (by design), so agent_down does not page for revoked agents. For other non-reporting states the staleness path normally fires agent_down. The operator-visible Docker status is still misleading in all three states. No compose service waits on the agent's health (checked test/compose/*.yml and deploy/docker-compose.yml). README L1678 documents the 503 states, but not the Docker status.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary test in cmd/pglens-agent (created, run, deleted; git status clean afterwards): httptest server returning 503 with a JSON body, PGLENS_HEALTHZ_LISTEN pointed at it, then runAgentHealthcheck(). Output: `healthcheck exit code against a 503 /healthz = 0`, `--- PASS`. Command: `GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go test ./cmd/pglens-agent -run TestDR19TmpHealthcheckReturnsZeroOn503 -count=1 -v`.
```

**Suggested fix:** Return non-zero on 503 so the container shows unhealthy, or expose a separate degraded signal. At minimum document the behaviour in the README.

**Fix notes:** In cmd/pglens-agent/main.go L58-75, return 1 when the status is 503, and keep the comment about not restarting. Docker does not restart a container merely for being unhealthy, so the comment's rationale is consistent with Docker. Add a unit test like the reproduction above. If the exit code stays 0, document in the README that Docker health does not reflect revoked, unauthorized or incompatible states. Note that agent_down is intentionally suppressed for revoked agents (source_sql.go L110-116).

### DR-20 — E2E evidence counts all host containers whose name contains pglens, including developer stacks (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `scripts/e2e_evidence.sh:18`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** docker ps -a --filter 'name=pglens' counts every container and network named like *pglens* on the host, so developer stacks inflate the RESIDUAL count and the evidence reports leftovers the suite did not create.

**Failure scenario:** Release evidence reports residual resources from unrelated stacks, which misleads the reviewer.

**Evidence:**

```text
scripts/e2e_evidence.sh L18-19 use the name filter.
```

**Verification reasoning:** scripts/e2e_evidence.sh L18-19 count `docker ps -a --filter 'name=pglens'` and `docker network ls --filter 'name=pglens'`, with no label or run-specific prefix. The name filter matches substrings, so any host container or network whose name contains pglens is counted. Verified live: the host listed 23 containers matching the filter, and only one was created in this session. The rest belong to other sessions or stacks. The suite's own containers are not named with a dedicated prefix that I could find (e2e resources go through compose service names), so the filter is not targeted at the suite's resources at all.

### DR-21 — Makefile hardcodes vite=8.2.2 while web/package.json pins vite 8.3.5 (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `Makefile:164`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The build metadata target writes a hardcoded vite version that differs from the version the web project pins, so the recorded build info does not describe the built toolchain.

**Failure scenario (as originally reported; see correction):** The build metadata reports vite 8.2.2 for a bundle built with 8.3.5, which misleads a later audit.

**Correction (from verification):** I initially refuted it from the worktree alone, and the main checkout shows the reviewed state.

**Evidence:**

```text
Makefile L164 printf 'built_at=%s\nvite=8.2.2\n'. web/package.json L81 pins vite 8.3.5.
```

**Verification reasoning:** On the reviewed branch the premise holds. The main checkout is on review/full-audit-2026-10 (.git/HEAD). Its web/package.json L81 pins "vite": "8.3.5", and the Makefile L164 hardcodes vite=8.2.2, so the recorded build metadata does not match the pin. My worktree is a different snapshot (branch worktree-wf_..., commit 5d70570) where package.json still says 8.2.2 at L80. The Makefile and package.json differ between the two trees in dependency pins, so the mismatch is a difference in branch state. I initially refuted it from the worktree alone, and the main checkout shows the reviewed state. The hardcoded literal is also a drift hazard on any future vite bump.

**Repro:**

```text
Read (not git): web/package.json L81 `"vite": "8.3.5"`; Makefile L164 `vite=8.2.2`; .git/HEAD `ref: refs/heads/review/full-audit-2026-10`. Diff of web/package.json: worktree L80 `"vite": "8.2.2"` vs review L81 `"vite": "8.3.5"`.
```

**Suggested fix:** Read the version from web/package.json or from the installed vite package instead of hardcoding it.

**Fix notes:** In Makefile web-build (L164), derive the value from web/package.json, for example with node -p reading devDependencies.vite, or from the installed web/node_modules/vite/package.json. Before relying on it, confirm web/pnpm-lock.yaml on the review branch resolves vite 8.3.5 (I did not read the review lockfile). Note that the worktree snapshot pins 8.2.2, so checks against that snapshot will not show the mismatch.

### DR-22 — make clean discards local edits to internal/webui/dist/index.html without asking (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `Makefile:191`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The clean target runs git checkout -- internal/webui/dist/index.html, which silently discards uncommitted local changes to that file.

**Failure scenario:** A developer edits the embedded placeholder page, runs make clean, and loses the edit.

**Evidence:**

```text
Makefile L191.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Makefile:191 runs `git checkout -- internal/webui/dist/index.html` unconditionally inside `clean`, and no guard prevents it. The restore is deliberate: web/vite.config.ts:44-45 builds into ../internal/webui/dist with emptyOutDir true, so every web build overwrites the tracked placeholder, and docs/plans/003_plan-Frontend/STATE.md:972 records that clean preserves the committed placeholder. Git restores from the index, so only unstaged edits are lost; staged edits survive. The loss is confined to uncommitted hand edits to the one placeholder page, with no product data or runtime effect, so low holds. The trigger is narrow: after any make web-build the file is already modified by vite, so the hand edit must be made to the placeholder with no build in between.

**Repro:**

```text
Run in the worktree (no .built present). Appended '<!-- LOCAL UNSTAGED EDIT -->' to internal/webui/dist/index.html (git status: ' M'). Ran `make clean`: exit 0. grep count of the edit: 0. git status: empty. Staged variant: git add of one edit, then a further unstaged line, then make clean: staged line kept (count 1), unstaged line gone (count 0), status 'M ' (staged). The tracked file was restored with git checkout HEAD and git status is clean. No scratch files were created for this check.
```

**Suggested fix:** Remove the checkout from clean, or check for local changes first and refuse to proceed.

**Fix notes:** Do not remove the checkout, and do not refuse on any local change: after a web build the file is always modified, so a refusal breaks the normal make web-build then make clean flow, and removing the restore leaves the built index.html beside a removed .built. Restore only when the tree holds build output: `if [ -e internal/webui/dist/.built ]; then git checkout -- internal/webui/dist/index.html; fi`, placed BEFORE the find line (Makefile:190), which deletes .built. Pitfall: the test has to run before that find line.

### DR-23 — Server image build copies host untracked dist assets into the Go build stage (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `Dockerfile.server`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The builder stage runs COPY . . and .dockerignore line 39 has a root-anchored dist/ pattern, so the host's untracked internal/webui/dist is copied. internal/webui/webui.go embeds all:dist. Files that the web-builder output does not overwrite can persist into the embedded UI.

**Failure scenario:** A developer has a stale local web build. The image embeds stale or mismatched UI files that are not in the release.

**Evidence:**

```text
Dockerfile.server COPY . . and the later COPY --from=web-builder /src/internal/webui/dist. .dockerignore L39 is root-anchored. internal/webui/webui.go L11 //go:embed all:dist.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The mechanism is real. .dockerignore:39 is `dist/`, which matches only the context-root dist, so the host's internal/webui/dist is copied by `COPY . .` (Dockerfile.server:16). The later `COPY --from=web-builder` (line 17) adds files without deleting leftovers, so the `//go:embed all:dist` in internal/webui/webui.go:11 embeds them. The impact is narrow: (a) IsPlaceholder() has no non-test caller (cmd/pglens-server/main.go uses only webui.Assets()), so a leftover .built changes no behaviour; (b) leftover hashed assets are unreferenced by the new index.html; (c) Makefile:100 makes test-ui-e2e depend on web-build build-images, so a host dist holding a same-version build is the normal state for local image builds, not stale data. The reporter's stale or mismatched scenario needs a non-vite leftover, and vite.config.ts:45 emptyOutDir true normally clears those. Side effect: the image's .built marker depends on host state, because the web-builder stage runs pnpm build (no marker written) rather than make web-build.

**Repro:**

```text
Probe with `docker build -f <probe Dockerfile> <context>` using postgres:17.11-alpine as the base, since no golang image is local. The probe's builder stage mirrors Dockerfile.server lines 16-17 (COPY . . then COPY --from=web-builder of internal/webui/dist). Context was a copy of the worktree with the real .dockerignore. Host-style leftovers added: internal/webui/dist/.built and assets/old-1234abcd.js. Builder-stage `find` output: .built, assets/old-1234abcd.js, assets/app-NEWHASH.js, index.html. Clean context with no host leftovers: only assets/app-NEWHASH.js and index.html. Builds were untagged and no containers were started. Scratch contexts were deleted.
```

**Suggested fix:** Anchor the ignore rule so it covers internal/webui/dist (for example **/dist/ or internal/webui/dist/), and copy only the Go sources into the builder stage.

**Fix notes:** Do not change to a bare **/dist/. Dockerfile.agent:4-5 runs `COPY . .` then `make build`, which compiles cmd/pglens-server (Makefile:15) and its all:dist embed; with no index.html in the context the agent image build fails. Use the pattern .gitignore already uses: `internal/webui/dist/*` followed by `!internal/webui/dist/index.html`, keeping the COPY --from line. Verify with a probe build like the one above.

### DR-25 — govulncheck is installed at @latest in the security gate (CONFIRMED, deploy-roles)

**Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:122`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest is unpinned, so the scanner version changes silently and can break the job or change its results.

**Failure scenario:** A new govulncheck release with a regression makes the security job fail or pass incorrectly on an unrelated change.

**Evidence:**

```text
ci.yml L122.
```

**Verification reasoning:** ci.yml:122 is the only unpinned install in the repo. `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest` resolves to the newest release on each run. The same workflow pins golangci-lint (GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION v2.13.2, ci.yml:29), so the inconsistency is clear. No guard exists: there is no Dependabot or Renovate config (.github contains only workflows/). Module checksums through the Go proxy limit tamper risk, so the impact is non-reproducible CI and surprise failures, not a supply-chain hole. The regression scenario is plausible but cannot be reproduced without a future release.

**Repro:**

```text
`grep -rn '@latest' .github Makefile scripts Dockerfile.agent Dockerfile.server test deploy` returns only ci.yml:122 and Makefile:50 (the message text). `ls .github` shows only workflows/.
```

**Suggested fix:** Pin a specific released version and bump it deliberately, for example through Dependabot or Renovate.

**Fix notes:** Add a pinned env var beside GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION (ci.yml:17-29) and install @${{ env.GOVULNCHECK_VERSION }} at line 122. Update the Makefile:50 hint, which also says @latest. Pick a released govulncheck tag that builds with the go.mod toolchain (go 1.27.1).

### RO-10 — ReadOnlySession documents a guarantee the GUC cannot provide (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/conn.go:68`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The doc comment says the server refuses writes for the whole session, and that writes fail 'rather than depending on the agent never issuing them'. default_transaction_read_only is a user-settable GUC, so the session can clear it. The check is defence in depth, not a boundary.

**Failure scenario:** No current command path sends a statement outside BEGIN READ ONLY, so no write is reachable today. A future path, or a simple-protocol statement outside a transaction, that runs SET default_transaction_read_only = off and then a write would succeed, and the comment would lead a reviewer to trust the guard.

**Evidence:**

```text
conn.go:71-76 `the server itself is told to refuse writes for the whole session: every transaction ... then starts READ ONLY, and INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, DDL, nextval() and friends fail inside PostgreSQL rather than depending on the agent never issuing them`; line 78 `SET default_transaction_read_only = on`. Verified on PG17 and PG19: `SET default_transaction_read_only = off` succeeds for an ordinary role, and a subsequent INSERT succeeds where the role has INSERT.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The comment at internal/agent/conn.go:68-76 overstates the guarantee. default_transaction_read_only is a user-settable GUC, so a session can clear it, and the comment's claim that writes fail "rather than depending on the agent never issuing them" is false as a boundary. The real protection on the EXPLAIN path is the explicit BEGIN READ ONLY (internal/agent/exec_explain.go:89-92) with a ROLLBACK defer. A cleared GUC inside that transaction does not allow a write, and the SET is reverted on ROLLBACK. No current code path sends user SQL outside a READ ONLY transaction: checks run fixed statements, and EXPLAIN text runs inside the wrapper. No write is reachable today, so this is a misleading comment about a security property, which is low under the rubric.

**Repro:**

```text
Container postgres:19rc1-alpine (pglens-review-ro-main, since removed). Role mon with LOGIN, SELECT and INSERT on table ro10. Step 1, as mon: SET default_transaction_read_only = on; INSERT INTO ro10 VALUES (1) gives ERROR: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction. Step 2: SET default_transaction_read_only = off; SHOW reports off; INSERT INTO ro10 VALUES (2) gives INSERT 0 1. Step 3, the explain wrapper shape: SET default_transaction_read_only = on; BEGIN READ ONLY; SET default_transaction_read_only = off; INSERT INTO ro10 VALUES (3) gives ERROR: cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction; ROLLBACK; SHOW reports on. Commands were docker exec <container> psql -U mon -d postgres -c "..." with one -c per statement.
```

**Suggested fix:** Correct the comment. Make the read-only property a database-privilege property: at startup, check with has_table_privilege and pg_has_role that the monitor role has no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or CREATE privileges and no signal privilege it does not need, and refuse command execution otherwise.

**Fix notes:** Correct the comment at conn.go:68-76. The actual controls are the monitoring role's privileges and the READ ONLY wrapper on the EXPLAIN path. An optional hardening is a startup check with has_table_privilege and pg_has_role that the monitor role holds no write privileges, but it is not required for this verdict.

### RO-14 — A lost replication slot reports zero retained WAL and no safe-size metric (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/check/replication_slots.go:52`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** retained_bytes is COALESCE(pg_wal_lsn_diff(..., restart_lsn), 0). A lost slot has restart_lsn NULL, so the value becomes 0. safe_wal_size is also NULL for a lost slot, so that metric is omitted. Only the wal_status label shows the problem.

**Failure scenario:** The most urgent state, a lost slot whose WAL the primary can recycle, looks like zero retained WAL. A retained_bytes alert never fires. Only an alert keyed on status=lost would catch it.

**Evidence:**

```text
replication_slots.go:52-56 `COALESCE(pg_wal_lsn_diff(CASE WHEN pg_is_in_recovery() THEN pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() ELSE pg_current_wal_lsn() END, restart_lsn)::bigint, 0) AS retained_bytes`; lines 102-112 omit replication_slot_safe_wal_size_bytes when NULL. Verified on PG19: with max_slot_wal_keep_size=2MB and a physical slot that fell behind, the slot showed wal_status=lost, restart_lsn IS NULL, safe_wal_size NULL, and the agent's query returned retained_bytes=0.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The query at internal/check/replication_slots.go:52-56 yields retained_bytes=0 when restart_lsn is NULL, because pg_wal_lsn_diff returns NULL and COALESCE turns it into 0. safe_wal_size is omitted (lines 105-112). The 0 is physically accurate, since the WAL has already been released. The state is still visible: every metric carries status=lost (labels at 79-83). The built-in slot_inactive event (internal/server/staleness.go:612-646, 660-690) keys on slot_active, and a lost physical slot is inactive (active=f in the repro), so the built-in alert still fires. Only user-defined retained-bytes threshold rules (the mapping at internal/alert/source_sql.go:67) are blind to a lost slot. No replication_slot_lost gauge exists. That makes this a low-severity gap, not medium.

**Repro:**

```text
Container postgres:19rc1-alpine (pglens-review-ro-main, since removed). ALTER SYSTEM SET max_slot_wal_keep_size='2MB'; SELECT pg_reload_conf(); SELECT pg_create_physical_replication_slot('ro14s', true); CREATE TABLE ro14 with 30000 rows of 1000 bytes; CHECKPOINT twice; pg_switch_wal(); CHECKPOINT. pg_replication_slots: ro14s | physical | active=f | wal_status=lost | restart_lsn NULL | safe_wal_size NULL. Real replicationSlotsCheck.Scrape through pgxpool: replication_slot_retained_bytes slot=ro14s status=lost value=0; replication_slot_active slot=ro14s status=lost value=0. Healthy slot ro14ok created afterwards, status=reserved: retained_bytes=5.368224e+06, safe_wal_size=1.1408952e+07. Command: RO14_DSN=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:<port>/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/check -run TestZZVerifyRO14 -v.
```

**Suggested fix:** Emit retained_bytes only when restart_lsn is not NULL, or emit a sentinel and document it. Add an explicit replication_slot_lost gauge, and alert on it.

**Fix notes:** Either emit a replication_slot_lost gauge, or document that retained_bytes=0 with status=lost means the WAL is already released. Consider a built-in rule on status=lost so threshold-only setups are covered.

### RO-17 — isMountWarning matches mount points by string prefix, not path component (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/mount.go:27`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The check uses strings.HasPrefix on the cleaned paths without a separator boundary, so /data matches /database.

**Failure scenario:** Identity path /database/identity.json is treated as being on a separate mount at /data, so the root-mount warning is suppressed.

**Evidence:**

```text
mount.go:27 `if mountpoint != "/" && strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Clean(path), filepath.Clean(mountpoint)) {`
```

**Verification reasoning:** The bug is real. The check at internal/agent/mount.go:27 (and the identical copy at cmd/pglens-agent/main.go:416) uses strings.HasPrefix without a path-component boundary, so /data matches /database/identity.json and the function returns false (no warning). The production path is cmd/pglens-agent/main.go:388 (checkMountWarning), which feeds getCheckWarnings (main.go:374) for the diagnostics output. The copy in internal/agent/mount.go is called only from config_test.go:343, so the finding's cited file is not the production one. Impact is a suppressed diagnostic warning, so low is right.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/agent/zz_verify_ro17_test.go (deleted). Mountinfo had a root line and '40 36 8:3 / /data rw,relatime - ext4 /dev/sdc3 rw'. Command: go -C <worktree> test ./internal/agent/ -run TestVerifyRO17MountPrefix -v -count=1. Output: 'path /database/identity.json isMountWarning=false err=<nil>' (expected true, since no separate mount holds that path).
```

**Suggested fix:** Compare with a boundary: `path == mp || strings.HasPrefix(path, mp + "/")`.

**Fix notes:** Fix both copies: internal/agent/mount.go:27 and cmd/pglens-agent/main.go:416. Use p := filepath.Clean(path); mp := filepath.Clean(mountpoint); match if p == mp || strings.HasPrefix(p, mp+"/") (mountpoint '/' is already excluded). Pitfall: mountinfo escapes spaces and other special characters in the mount-point field as octal (for example \040), so a mount point containing a space never matches the raw string. This is separate from the finding.

### RO-18 — Fingerprint's url.Parse error echoes the DSN, password included (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/identity/fingerprint.go:27`

**Category:** security · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The error wraps the url.Parse error, and url.Error includes the raw URL. The comment says a fingerprint is safe to log and a DSN never is, but the error path leaks the password. pgx's own parse error redacts it.

**Failure scenario:** Latent: a DSN that pgx accepts but url.Parse rejects is not known to exist. If one did, the error would reach stderr through run.go:469 and the password would reach the logs.

**Evidence:**

```text
fingerprint.go:25-27 `u, err := url.Parse(dsn); if err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf("fingerprint: parse dsn: %w", err) }`. Verified offline: the message is `fingerprint: parse dsn: parse "postgres://pglensuser:<redacted>@db.example.invalid:notaport/app": invalid port ":notaport" after host`. pgx.ParseConfig on the same DSN prints `postgres://pglensuser:<redacted>@...`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The defect is real. Fingerprint (internal/identity/fingerprint.go:25-27) wraps the url.Error from url.Parse, and url.Error includes the raw DSN. Reproduced: pgxpool.ParseConfig accepts the keyword-form DSN 'host=db.example.invalid user=pglensuser password=<redacted> dbname=app', and Fingerprint returns an error containing the password. The finding's own example (postgres://...:notaport/app) is not reachable: pgxpool.ParseConfig rejects it first with pgx's redacted message. In shipped code the branch is currently unreachable. Run mode requires the postgres:// or postgresql:// prefix (internal/agent/config.go:273), and pgconn's parseURLSettings (config.go:622-627) runs the same url.Parse and strips the url.Error, so any URL-form DSN that fails url.Parse is already rejected by NewManager. The check subcommand (cmd/pglens-agent/main.go runCheck) never calls Fingerprint, and the only caller is localIdentity (internal/agent/conn.go:580). Severity stays low, since the leak exists in the function but needs an input the agent currently refuses.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/identity/zz_verify_ro18_test.go (deleted). Command: go -C <worktree> test ./internal/identity/ -run TestVerifyRO18FingerprintEcho -v -count=1. Decisive output for the keyword DSN: 'pgxpool.ParseConfig err: <nil>' and 'Fingerprint err: fingerprint: parse dsn: parse "host=db.example.invalid user=pglensuser password=<redacted> dbname=app": invalid URL escape "%zz"'. For the URL example: pgxpool.ParseConfig returned 'cannot parse `postgres://pglensuser:<redacted>@...`', so it never reaches Fingerprint.
```

**Suggested fix:** Return a fixed message without wrapping the url.Error, for example `fingerprint: DSN is not a valid URL`.

**Fix notes:** Replace the wrap with a fixed message: return "", errors.New("fingerprint: DSN is not a valid URL"). Tests for the fix must use a keyword-form DSN (for example a password containing %zz), because the URL example in the finding never reaches this branch.

### RO-20 — isPermissionDenied matches on substrings of error text (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/check/instance_info.go:112`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Any error text containing '42501' or 'permission denied' is treated as a permission failure. Other checks already use pgErrorCode.

**Failure scenario:** A non-permission error whose text contains the digits 42501 switches the cluster identity to the manual source. Cluster grouping on the server then changes.

**Evidence:**

```text
instance_info.go:112 `return strings.Contains(s, "42501") || strings.Contains(s, "permission denied") || strings.Contains(s, "must be superuser")`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The text match is real and changes behaviour. internal/check/instance_info.go:112 matches '42501' or 'permission denied' in err.Error(), while the other checks use pgErrorCode (pgerr.go). Reproduced with the mock connection: when the first query fails with a non-SQLSTATE error whose text contains '42501', Scrape falls through to the fallback query, returns err=nil, and reports cluster_id_source=manual with an empty system_identifier. The trigger is rare in practice: a non-permission error must carry the phrase and the fallback query must succeed. Low is kept.

**Repro:**

```text
Temporary file internal/check/zz_verify_ro20_test.go (deleted; a stray sed edit to it was reverted by deleting the file). Command: go -C <worktree> test ./internal/check/ -run TestVerifyRO20PermissionMatch -v -count=1. Output: 'calls=2 err=<nil>' and 'pg_up labels: cluster_id_source="manual" system_identifier=""'. The first queryRow returned fmt.Errorf("unexpected row shape, column code 42501 out of range"), which is not a *pgconn.PgError.
```

**Suggested fix:** Use pgErrorCode(err) == pgInsufficientPrivilege, as other checks do.

**Fix notes:** Replace the body with `return pgErrorCode(err) == pgInsufficientPrivilege`, since pgerr.go already defines the constant. internal/check/instance_info_test.go TestIsPermissionDenied (lines 52-64) builds its errors with testError, which is not a *pgconn.PgError, so it will fail after the fix. Rewrite those cases with &pgconn.PgError{Code: "42501"}. A 'must be superuser' error also carries SQLSTATE 42501, so the code check covers it.

### RO-22 — backoffDelay documents a 60-second cap, but jitter can push retries to 120 seconds (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/pusher.go:320`

**Category:** docs · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The comment says the delay is capped at 60 seconds. The cap is applied to the base only, and random jitter up to the base is added afterwards.

**Failure scenario:** Retries can wait up to 120 seconds, which is longer than the documented cap. This does not lose data.

**Evidence:**

```text
pusher.go:320 `// backoffDelay returns exponential backoff + jitter, capped at 60s.`; line 326 `base := time.Duration(math.Min(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt-1)), 60)) * time.Second`; lines 328-330 `jitterMax := int64(base); jitter := time.Duration(rand.Int63n(jitterMax + 1)); return base + jitter`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The cap is applied to the base only. backoffDelay (internal/agent/pusher.go:321-331) returns base+rand[0,base], so for attempt>=7 (base=60s) the result lies in [60s,120s]. The only caller, pushOne (pusher.go:234-238), sleeps on backoffDelay(attempt) with no further clamp. No guard elsewhere. The comment 'capped at 60s' is therefore wrong. TestPusher_BackoffCapped (pusher_test.go:23-30) asserts <=120s, so the test already encodes the 120s ceiling and only the comment is stale. The finding's 'no data loss' note is correct.

**Repro:**

```text
Verbatim copy of backoffDelay run in a scratch Go program (go run, 500k samples per attempt, stdlib only). Scratch files were deleted afterwards.
```

**Suggested fix:** Apply the cap after adding jitter, or correct the comment.

**Fix notes:** Prefer correcting the comment at pusher.go:320 to say the base is capped at 60s and jitter adds up to one base (max about 120s). Capping after jitter would make many agents bunch at exactly 60s, which defeats the jitter's purpose. If the code is changed instead, TestPusher_BackoffCapped must tighten its bound to 60s.

### RO-23 — Signal target is verified in one statement and signalled in another, leaving a race on PID reuse (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/exec_signal.go:40`

**Category:** race · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The PID is checked against pg_stat_activity in one statement and signalled in a second statement. Between the two, the PID can be reused by another client backend.

**Failure scenario:** Requires AllowSignal=true and PID reuse inside a millisecond window. The wrong client session is terminated.

**Evidence:**

```text
exec_signal.go:40-44 `SELECT COALESCE(backend_type, ''), ... FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = $1`; line 69 `conn.QueryRow(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("SELECT %s($1)", function), *args.PID)`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code reading confirms the TOCTOU. The identity check (exec_signal.go:40-44, SELECT from pg_stat_activity WHERE pid=$1) and the signal (line 69, SELECT pg_terminate_backend($1)) are two separate round trips on the same pooled connection, with no lock or single-statement binding in between. pg_terminate_backend and pg_cancel_backend take only a PID. The window is real, but exploiting it needs AllowSignal=true (default off), tier T2, and PID reuse by a new client backend inside a sub-millisecond gap, so the likelihood is negligible. The rubric lists races under high, but the realistic impact here is low. Not reproduced: PID reuse cannot be forced on a live instance.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only. exec_signal.go lines 40-44 (identity SELECT) and line 69 (signal) run as separate QueryRow calls on the same conn. internal/command/gate.go:18-24 gates on tier T2 and AllowSignal. No mutex or statement-level binding covers the gap.
```

**Suggested fix:** Check and signal in one statement, for example `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = $1 AND backend_type = 'client backend' AND usename IS DISTINCT FROM current_user AND application_name NOT LIKE 'pglens%'`, and treat zero rows as rejected.

**Fix notes:** The proposed single-statement rewrite narrows the window but does not close it, because the pg_stat_activity scan and the function call still run at different times within the statement. A race-free fix must bind backend identity beyond the PID, for example backend_start. That needs an Args change: internal/command/types.go:26-33 carries only PID today, so the server would have to pass the backend_start it observed. Keep the existing isPglensApplication and ownRole checks; the proposed WHERE clause does not reproduce them exactly.

### RO-24 — Dispatcher comment says a failed capability refresh keeps a conservative state, but it keeps the last state (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/agent/command.go:184`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The comment says the last state is conservative. In fact the previous tier, which may be stale and higher, is kept, and the refresh error is discarded.

**Failure scenario:** A revoked pg_signal_backend stays granted in the agent's gate until the next successful refresh. PostgreSQL still enforces the real privilege, so no escalation occurs, but the gate and the comment are misleading.

**Evidence:**

```text
command.go:184-186 `// Keep the last known conservative capability state on a transient refresh failure; the executor will still enforce its gates.` followed by `_ = refresher.RefreshCapabilities(ctx)`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** RefreshCapabilities (internal/agent/conn.go:529-544) returns before touching the cache when ensureCache or Shared fails, so the previous permTier, which may be T2, stays in place. The dispatcher (internal/agent/command.go:184-186) discards the error with `_ =`, and command.Allowed (internal/command/gate.go:18-24) then passes the stale tier. The comment's 'conservative' wording is wrong, and so is 'the executor will still enforce its gates': exec_signal.go does no tier check, and only PostgreSQL enforces the privilege. A non-acquire error inside queryCapabilities does drop the tier, so the stale window only applies to connection-acquire failures. PostgreSQL still refuses the signal after a revoke, so there is no escalation.

**Repro:**

```text
Local throwaway container pglens-review-ro24-k3m9 (postgres:18.6-alpine), removed afterwards. CREATE ROLE mon LOGIN; CREATE ROLE victim LOGIN; a background victim session pg_sleep(120). (1) As mon, before any grant: pg_terminate_backend(210) gives ERROR: permission denied to terminate process; DETAIL: Only roles with privileges of the role whose process is being terminated or with privileges of the "pg_signal_backend" role may terminate this process. (2) GRANT pg_signal_backend TO mon, then pg_terminate_backend(237) returns t. (3) REVOKE pg_signal_backend FROM mon, then pg_terminate_backend(210) gives the same permission-denied ERROR.
```

**Suggested fix:** On refresh failure, drop the tier to T0 for the gate check, or correct the comment.

**Fix notes:** Fail closed: when RefreshCapabilities errors, gate that command at T0 (or as the executor does), instead of ignoring the error. Alternatively correct the comment at command.go:25-27 and drop 'conservative' and 'the executor will still enforce its gates'. Note that the Go executors do no tier check; PostgreSQL is the only enforcement point. The fix must be made in dispatch, since RefreshCapabilities's error path is the only place the stale tier survives.

### RO-25 — index definition hash lowercases identifiers, so case-only changes are not detected (CONFIRMED, readonly-audit)

**Location:** `internal/check/index_stats.go:128`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** hashNormalizedDefinition lowercases the definition. Quoted identifiers that differ only in case hash the same.

**Failure scenario:** An index is rebuilt on a column named "Col" in place of col. The def_hash is unchanged, and the definition change is not reported.

**Evidence:**

```text
index_stats.go:128 `normalized := strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ToLower(def[start:end+1])), " ")`.
```

**Verification reasoning:** hashNormalizedDefinition (internal/check/index_stats.go:121-131) lowercases the whole (...) span, so quoted identifiers and string literals that differ only in case hash the same. The mechanism is confirmed with real pg_get_indexdef output. The finding's example is wrong, though: a change from quoted ("Col") to unquoted (col) keeps the quotes in the lowercased text, so it does change the hash. The real misses are a case-only quoted rename and a partial-index literal change. Consumers: advisor/rules_relation.go:218-233 (sibling index-definition divergence) and server/pipeline.go:1070-1073 (stored DefHash). ValueText keeps the full definition, so the change stays visible in the fact text. The existing test TestIndexStats_DefHashIsWhitespaceInsensitive (index_stats_test.go:38-40) intentionally tests keyword-case insensitivity, and no test covers identifier or literal case.

**Repro:**

```text
Real output from a postgres:18.6-alpine review container: after CREATE INDEX i1 ON t ("Col") and ALTER TABLE t RENAME COLUMN "Col" TO "COL", pg_get_indexdef gives ...USING btree ("Col") then ...USING btree ("COL"). A partial index changed from WHERE (status = 'Active'::text) to 'active'::text also gives different text. Fed to a verbatim copy of hashNormalizedDefinition: quoted case-only rename equal_hash=true; partial-index literal case equal_hash=true; "Col" to unquoted col equal_hash=false; control a to b equal_hash=false. Scratch program deleted; container removed.
```

**Suggested fix:** Hash pg_get_indexdef output with whitespace normalised but case preserved. pg_get_indexdef is already canonical.

**Fix notes:** Fix the normalization without touching quoted identifiers or literals: collapse whitespace only, or lowercase only unquoted keyword tokens. Preserve case inside double quotes and single quotes. pg_get_indexdef output is already canonical. The fix must update TestIndexStats_DefHashIsWhitespaceInsensitive, which currently expects keyword-case insensitivity, and add cases for quoted identifiers and literals. Changing the hash will also change stored def_hash values, so expect one-time divergence reports in advisor/rules_relation.go.

### TD-05 — SYS-ALERT-004 silence check is a one-shot negative with no settle window (CONFIRMED, tests-docs)

**Location:** `test/scenario/alerting.go:335`

**Category:** test-gap · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** Once the firing state is observed, the scenario reads the mock receiver once and requires zero bodies. There is no window that spans the notifier's delivery interval, so a notification leaked later is not caught.

**Failure scenario:** The notifier ignores the silence on its second cycle. The scenario passes because its single read happened before that cycle.

**Evidence:**

```text
alerting.go:331-336: receiverCall then 'if len(bodies) != 0' with no loop.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Confirmed as a one-shot negative with no settle window: test/scenario/alerting.go:331-337 reads the receiver once, after waitForAlertState has seen firing with suppressed=true. Failure scenario reworded: the second-cycle leak is largely unreachable, because internal/alert/engine.go:302 only lets transitions reach Notify, so a steadily firing alert is not re-sent on later ticks. The reachable regression is a dropped !Suppressed guard at engine.go:311. That path would POST immediately after Upsert (engine.go:307), so the single read misses it only if the POST lands after the read. With a 2-second tick (test/compose/scenario-alerting.yml:14) and a 500-millisecond poll, that window is narrow, which is why severity is low.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only (e2e stack not run): test/scenario/alerting.go:331-337; internal/alert/engine.go:302, 307 and 311; test/compose/scenario-alerting.yml:14.
```

**Suggested fix:** Assert len(bodies) == 0 at every tick across at least two notifier intervals, using Consistently, and fail on the first delivery.

**Fix notes:** If a settle window is added, assert zero deliveries across at least two ticks (about 6 seconds at the 2-second interval) with a bounded loop that fails on the first delivery. A re-notify on later cycles is not reachable, so the window only needs to cover the delivery that follows Upsert.

**Location:** `test/scenario/net.go:71`

### TD-15 — SYS-AGENT-005 reads the baseline before the revoke, so in-flight pushes can fail the no-growth check (CONFIRMED, tests-docs)

**Location:** `test/scenario/agent.go:353`

**Category:** test-gap · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The baseline count(*) is taken at lines 353-356, before the UPDATE that revokes the agent. Envelopes accepted between the baseline read and the revoke raise the count, and the 30-second consistency loop then reports 'kept collecting after revocation'.

**Failure scenario:** A push that completes in the milliseconds between the baseline query and the UPDATE makes the scenario fail, even though the agent behaves correctly.

**Evidence:**

```text
agent.go:353-356 baseline query. The UPDATE follows the baseline.
```

**Verification reasoning:** Code reading confirms the race. test/scenario/agent.go:353-356 takes a global count(*) FROM metrics baseline, then the UPDATE revokes at line 358, then the 30s loop at lines 389-399 fails on any n > baseline with no tolerance and no re-baseline. Ingest is synchronous: internal/server/ingest.go:137 checks IsRevoked, then pipeline.Process at ingest.go:163 writes the rows in a transaction before the 202 is returned, and internal/server/pipeline.go has no goroutines. So any push that passed the IsRevoked check before the UPDATE and commits after the baseline read is counted. The window is wider than the finding says: it includes the whole transaction of a push straddling the revoke, not only the milliseconds between baseline and UPDATE. Pushes run every 5s (harness.go:418 push_interval), so the flake probability per run is low but nonzero.

**Repro:**

```text
Code-only (no live stack). Read test/scenario/agent.go lines 353-399, internal/server/ingest.go lines 137-163, and internal/server/pipeline.go (grep for 'go ' statements returns none).
```

**Suggested fix:** Take the baseline after the healthz state reads 'revoked' and after a short quiescence, or assert that no row has ts >= revokeTS instead of comparing counts.

**Fix notes:** Take the baseline only after /healthz reports state=revoked (and after a short settle), so pushes that were in flight at revoke time have finished. Do not rely on a bare ts >= revokeTS filter without checking clock ordering: metrics.ts is the agent's sample time, and buffered envelopes carry pre-revoke ts.

**Evidence:**

```text
harness.go:716-740 cache and lookup (from an earlier read this session; not reproduced).
```

**Verification reasoning:** The mechanism is reproduced. Docker reassigns the ephemeral host port on stop, kill and restart. The harness pool cache never invalidates: test/harness/harness.go:718-740 (pgPool) builds the DSN once from the resolved port and caches it in h.pools, and Compose() at harness.go:766-823 clears nothing. reconcileServerPorts and reconcileAgentBinaryPort update only the API clients and the binary agent config. The literal failure in the finding (restart a DB service, then call DB()) is not reachable today, because DB() always targets timescaledb and no scenario restarts it. The reachable victim is test/scenario/reset.go:44, where pg := e.PG("pg") feeds a load goroutine (lines 45-57) that runs pg.Exec every 100ms. Lines 98-101 SIGKILL and start the pg container, after which the goroutine's errors are discarded at line 54, so load silently stops after the restart in container mode. The comment at reset.go:36-37 claiming the pool reconnects is false there. The scenario still passes, because its assertions read agent-derived rows, not this load. Binary mode is immune because PG_HOST_PORT pins the port (test/compose/topo-standalone.yml:15-31). archiving_test.go:55-61 calls pg.Reset(), which does not refresh the DSN, but the pool is not used afterwards (execPostgres uses docker exec), so it is harmless today.

**Repro:**

```text
docker run -d --name pglens-review-td16-a1 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 0:5432 postgres:18.6-alpine gave host port 33291. docker kill -s SIGKILL then docker start gave 33292. docker stop then docker start gave 33293. On a second container pglens-review-td16-b, docker port gave 33309, then docker restart gave 33310. A python socket connect to 127.0.0.1:33292 returned [Errno 111] Connection refused, and 33293 was open. Both containers were removed with docker rm -f, and docker ps -a shows none left.
```

**Suggested fix:** Key the cache by the resolved host:port and re-resolve after restarts, or clear cached pools in Compose() on restart, start and up.

**Fix notes:** Evicting h.pools entries does not help holders of a live *pgxpool.Pool, such as the reset.go goroutine. The robust fix is pgxpool.Config.BeforeConnect (or a DSN built from a live port lookup) that re-resolves the published port on every new dial. Also fix the reset.go comment and the goroutine's error handling, and fix archiving_test.go's pg.Reset() comment.

### TD-23 — SYS-LOAD-002 checks max transaction age > 0, not the >1s its error message states (CONFIRMED, tests-docs)

**Location:** `test/scenario/load.go:69`

**Category:** test-gap · **Confidence:** medium

**Description:** The check requires maxXact > 0, but the failure message says '>1s'. The underlying query in internal/check/activity.go:46-50 excludes the agent's own backend and ignores NULL xact_start. So any other open transaction satisfies the check, including the scenario's own lock holder.

**Failure scenario:** The check does not measure the blocked transaction the scenario claims to prove. A regression that reports the blocked transaction at 0.2 s still passes, and the message misleads whoever debugs a failure.

**Evidence:**

```text
load.go:66-69 variable and comparison. activity.go:46-50 query text.
```

**Verification reasoning:** The mismatch is real. load.go:66-69 asserts maxXact > 0, the failure message at load.go:91 says (>1s), and the comment at load.go:45 claims the storm's long-held transactions are reflected. The comment at load.go:60-65 explains that the >0 threshold is deliberate: the 1ms hold means the age reflects queueing only. So the message and the line-45 comment are wrong, while the assertion is intentionally weak. The weakness is real but argued from code, not reproduced: activity.go:46-50 excludes only the check's own backend, so any open client transaction passes. Each statement sets xact_start, so the agent's other concurrent check and ASH connections can satisfy > 0 with no storm at all. The finding's wording 'the scenario's own lock holder' is loose, since the storm sessions themselves hold the open transactions. The suggested >1s threshold is not supported by measurement. With a throwaway postgres:17.11-alpine container and the same lock-storm command (50 sessions, default --hold 1ms, 12s), the activity query sampled every ~0.4s during the storm gave a max xact age between 0.042 and 0.230 s, and 0 after the storm. The storm report showed succeeded 2471, failed 0, client max_wait_ms 632.4. So a >1s assertion would likely fail the scenario unless the hold is lengthened. This was a single local run without the agent, not the e2e stack. Impact is misleading failure text and a weak assertion, with no wrong data stored, so severity stays low.

**Repro:**

```text
1) Built test/workload into the scratchpad as workloadctl, then ran workloadctl lock-storm --dsn 'postgres://postgres:<redacted>@127.0.0.1:<port>/postgres?sslmode=disable' --sessions 50 --duration 12s against pglens-review-td23a7f3 (postgres:17.11-alpine). Report: "succeeded": 2471, "failed": 0, "max_wait_ms": 632.42. 2) Concurrently, every ~0.4s: docker exec pglens-review-td23a7f3 psql -U postgres -tAc "SELECT COALESCE(max(EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - xact_start)),0) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type='client backend' AND pid <> pg_backend_pid()". Output during the storm: 0.0598, 0.0462, 0.0641, 0.0480, 0.0424, 0.0462, 0.0706, 0.1058, 0.0593, 0.0944, 0.0555, 0.1034, 0.0826, 0.2304, 0.0677, 0.0950, 0.0540; after the storm: 0. Min positive 0.042 s, max 0.230 s. 3) Container removed with docker rm -f; the worktree is unchanged.
```

**Suggested fix:** Assert the age of the blocked transaction (for example greater than its known wait, or greater than 1s), or correct the message and the stated claim.

**Fix notes:** Do not raise the assertion to >1s with the default --hold 1ms: the measured server-side max was about 0.2 s and the client max wait was about 0.63 s. Either change the message at load.go:91 and the claim at load.go:45 to match the > 0 check, pointing at the rationale at load.go:60-65, or make a stronger threshold reachable by lengthening --hold as SYS-UI-008 does (--hold 45s). A longer hold changes the load profile and the storm timing budget (checkCtx at load.go:49), so re-verify on the real e2e stack if you take that route. To isolate the storm's transactions, tag the storm connections (for example with application_name in the DSN built at load.go:30-31) and filter the activity rows on that, rather than relying on a threshold. The ASH Lock assertion at load.go:110-118 already covers storm visibility.

### XU-06 — Idle-in-transaction metric drops aborted sessions (CONFIRMED, metric-unit-catalogue)

**Location:** `internal/check/activity.go:47`

**Category:** inaccuracy · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** pg_max_idle_in_transaction_seconds filters on state = 'idle in transaction', so sessions in 'idle in transaction (aborted)' are not counted. The advisor rule txn.idle_in_transaction (rules_query.go:161) and the conn idle_in_transaction alert (migration 0013) therefore never see them. Locks are released when the transaction aborts, so the impact is connection hygiene rather than blocking.

**Failure scenario:** An application leaks connections in 'idle in transaction (aborted)' after errors without rollback. No idle-in-transaction finding or alert is raised, although pg_max_state_age_seconds{state} does carry the age.

**Evidence:**

```text
activity.go:47: COALESCE(max(EXTRACT(epoch FROM now() - state_change)) FILTER (WHERE state = 'idle in transaction'), 0) AS max_idle_in_txn. Container postgres:18.6-alpine: pg_stat_activity showed 'idle in transaction|1' and 'idle in transaction (aborted)|1'; the filter used by the check matched 1 session.
```

**Verification reasoning:** activity.go 47 FILTER matches only state = 'idle in transaction', so 'idle in transaction (aborted)' sessions contribute 0 to pg_max_idle_in_transaction_seconds. The advisor rule txn.idle_in_transaction (rules_query.go 161) and the conn.idle_in_transaction seed (migration 0013 renames it to this metric) read that metric and therefore miss them. The per-state series pg_max_state_age_seconds (activity.go 200) does carry the aborted state. The finding's lock claim is correct: after the error, the aborted session held no locks on u (pg_locks count 0), so the impact is connection hygiene, not blocking.

**Repro:**

```text
postgres:18.6-alpine container (pglens-review-xu03-b71e). Session A: BEGIN; SELECT 1/0; left idle (state 'idle in transaction (aborted)'). Session B: BEGIN; SELECT 1; idle (state 'idle in transaction'). Verbatim activity.go 42-52 query output: 'active | Timeout | 1 | 16.896660 | 0'; 'idle in transaction | Client | 1 | 4.050669 | 4.050504'; 'idle in transaction (aborted) | Client | 1 | 0 | 0'. Per-state age query (activity.go 75): 'idle in transaction (aborted) | 19.514927'. Lock check: BEGIN; LOCK TABLE u IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE; SELECT 1/0; then pg_locks showed 0 locks on u after the error.
```

**Suggested fix:** Use FILTER (WHERE state LIKE 'idle in transaction%') and add a test for the aborted state.

**Fix notes:** Fix at activity.go 47: FILTER (WHERE state LIKE 'idle in transaction%'), and add a test with the aborted state. The per-state series already carries the aborted state (activity.go 200), so the fix is one line plus a test. Also check the txn.idle_in_transaction rule description, which currently describes only plain idle-in-transaction sessions.

Status: open

### XU-10 — metrics/query returns one arbitrary series per bucket for labelled metrics (CONFIRMED, metric-unit-catalogue)

**Location:** `internal/server/api.go:779`

**Category:** contract · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** The handler filters only on instance, metric and optionally datname, orders by ts, and keeps the last row per bucket. For a labelled metric requested without a database (pg_backends by state, pg_lock_waits by wait_event, pg_connections_by_database, pg_io_* by backend_type, object and context), the response is one arbitrary series per bucket. Counter-kind series are stored as per-second rates under *_total, *_ms_total and *_bytes names, and openapi.yaml does not say so. The web UI requests only single-series metrics today, so no current screen is wrong.

**Failure scenario:** An integration asks for pg_backends without a state filter and charts whichever state sorts last in each bucket. A client that reads pg_xact_commit_total as a cumulative counter gets commits per second.

**Evidence:**

```text
api.go:779-781: SELECT ts, value FROM metrics WHERE instance_id=$1 AND metric=$2 AND ts >= $3 AND ts < $4 ORDER BY ts. api.go:807: bucketValues[idx] = val. openapi.yaml:1197-1204 documents 'missing intervals are null, never zero or interpolated' and nothing about labels or rate semantics.
```

**Verification reasoning:** internal/server/api.go:779-781 filters only on instance_id, metric and optional datname, orders by ts, and line 807 sets bucketValues[idx] = val, so the last row per bucket wins. The labels column is never read. Rows with different label sets at the same ts tie, so the winner is arbitrary and can change between requests. Counters are stored under their original names with per-second rates as the value (internal/server/pipeline.go:470-476 sets value = pt.Rate and keeps m.Name), so pg_xact_commit_total holds rates. api/openapi.yaml:1197-1204 says only 'missing intervals are null'. Neither MetricsResponse nor MetricPoint describes labels or rate units. Web: the instance page's only metrics query is OverviewSection (InstancePage.tsx:95), and once a database is applied its series are single-series. ActivitySection reads another endpoint. Not verified: other pages that might call metrics/query, and the pg_lock_waits and pg_io_* examples.

**Repro:**

```text
Code reading only; not reproduced against a live server.
```

**Suggested fix:** Accept label filters and aggregate the series per bucket (sum or average, stated in the response). Document units and rate semantics in openapi.yaml, or expose explicit increase series for *_total names.

**Fix notes:** The fix belongs in the handler (api.go:779-807) and in the OpenAPI description. Either accept label filters and aggregate per bucket, or document that unfiltered labelled metrics return an arbitrary series. Also add a deterministic tie-break such as ORDER BY ts, labels.

### XE-07 — orphan_standby cannot fire for the documented unresolvable-upstream case (CONFIRMED, event-type-catalogue)

**Location:** `internal/server/pipeline.go:258`

**Category:** bug · **Confidence:** high

**Description:** Edges whose upstream cannot be resolved are dropped before the engine sees them. An orphan standby with an unresolvable upstream therefore looks like one with no edges, and engine.go:189 requires len(obs.Edges) > 0 to start the orphan timer. README.md:1459 documents orphan_standby for the case 'upstream cannot be resolved'.

**Failure scenario:** A standby points at an upstream that is missing from inventory (deleted or never registered). No orphan_standby is ever emitted, although the README says it is. The operator trusts the absence of the event.

**Evidence:**

```text
pipeline.go:258-260 `if !ok { continue }`; topology/engine.go:189 `if !hasResolvedEdge && len(obs.Edges) > 0 {`; README.md:1459 row for orphan_standby. Scratch test: 0 orphan_standby events over 300 s with an unresolvable upstream.
```

**Verification reasoning:** pipeline.go:258-260 drops every edge whose upstream does not resolve, after the single-primary fallback at 249-257. engine.go:189 requires len(obs.Edges) > 0 before the orphan clock starts, so a standby whose upstream was never registered or monitored never produces orphan_standby. The operational case in the README (primary down, standby not promoted) does work, because the primary's row still exists and the resolveAddr DB fallback (pipeline.go:180-205) resolves it. Only the literal documented wording ('upstream cannot be resolved', README.md:1459, phase_07 around lines 184-185) is unreachable. Low severity: the gap is narrow and the design comments (pipeline.go:137-139, run.go:518-521) state that a resolvable target is intended, so this is mainly docs drift. I did not run test/scenario/replication.go:312.

**Repro:**

```text
Engine-level scratch test in internal/topology (since deleted). Command: go test -count=1 -v -run TestXE07_ ./internal/topology/ . Output: 'XE07 case A (no edge object, 300 s): orphan_standby events=0'; 'XE07 case B (low edge object, 300 s): orphan_standby events=5 first at ~1m0s'. The pipeline drop was confirmed by reading pipeline.go:258-260.
```

**Suggested fix:** Pass an edge with the unresolved target through to the engine (placeholder To, confidence low) so the orphan timer starts, or correct README.md:1459 and the docs/plans phase_07 text (around lines 184-185) to say the documented case cannot fire.

**Fix notes:** Either correct the orphan_standby rows in README.md:1459 and docs/plans/001_plan-Foundations/phase_07.md (around lines 184-185) to say an unregistered upstream cannot be detected, or pass a placeholder low-confidence edge for unresolved upstreams so the orphan clock starts. Do not change the engine without also deciding the intended behaviour, since the code comments treat resolvable targets as required.
